items.title: Virtual mapping experts help B&M Group map out its store of the future
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Discount retailer B&M Group has created a fully immersive digital twin of one of its flagship stores for the first time. Working with 3D virtual mapping specialist Apollo3D, activity focused on the Worthington Way store in Wigan, supporting the retailer’s newly unveiled “store of the future” concept and providing B&M with a blueprint it can […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Discount retailer B&M Group has created a fully immersive digital twin of one of its flagship stores for the first time.
Working with 3D virtual mapping specialist Apollo3D, activity focused on the Worthington Way store in Wigan, supporting the retailer’s newly unveiled “store of the future” concept and providing B&M with a blueprint it can use to plan expansion and refurbishment projects across its rapidly growing estate.
Leeds-based Apollo3D was brought in by B&M in March this year, scanning the 55,000 sq ft store (including garden centre and non-customer areas) ahead of a seven-phase transformation that was completed in August. The resulting model, nicknamed “Wigan 2.0” by the project team, combined a full 3D digital twin with a drone flythrough of the site, giving B&M’s design team a way to test layout changes, signage and even floor colours before a single wall was moved.
Rob Dixon, who led the store design for B&M, said the technology changed how decisions were made: “The Apollo 3D technology and full-store scan were absolutely invaluable in giving the team a detailed and comprehensive view of the entire customer journey. The level of insight and detail enabled us to identify opportunities and make more informed design decisions across the store, from wayfinding and brand communications through to flooring execution. It was a hugely valuable tool in shaping the overall customer experience and bringing the design vision to life for the store.”
The store stayed open throughout the seven-phase rebuild, with B&M able to plan around the model rather than closing sections off for measurement and assessment. By June, the first phase of the physical rebuild was complete, informed almost entirely by the virtual staging Apollo3D had produced months earlier.
Beyond the build itself, the model has taken on a life of its own inside B&M. Footage from the scan, including a side-by-side before-and-after walkthrough, was shown to management and staff at the company’s annual conference, and VR headsets were used to give colleagues a first look at the finished store, including new break rooms, shopping aisles, new self-checkouts, chilled food areas and customer entrance. A version has also been adapted for customers to explore online ahead of visiting in person.
Mark Shepherd, managing director and founder of Apollo3D, said the Wigan project shows what is possible when digital mapping is used beyond a single stage of a project: “We’ve worked with retailers, healthcare providers and facilities teams for years, and the businesses that get the most out of this valuable technology are the ones that keep coming back to the model, long after the initial scan. For B&M, that means using it for design, for training, for marketing and now, as a template for how they approach future stores.”
He added that the approach also points to a wider shift in how retailers manage their estates: “A single accurate scan can be reused again and again, for a refit, for planning a Christmas display, even for showing a fully stocked shelf without a warehouse full of stock behind it. That’s a real change in how retail businesses can work, and it’s one that pays for itself very quickly across a large store network.”
For B&M, which operates from more than 790 stores in the UK and France, the Wigan project is expected to inform how future refurbishments and new store openings are planned, reducing the need for repeat site visits and giving teams a shared reference point from design through to construction. The retailer has already indicated the model will be used to support decisions on range changes and seasonal displays, an area where the ability to visualise a fully stocked shelf without physical stock is expected to save both time and cost.
B&M Group CEO, Tjeerd Jegen, said the project marks a shift in how the retailer will approach its estate going forward: “This is a genuinely groundbreaking way for us to plan our stores. Having a store mapped out in this much detail, before any physical work begins, means every layout and design decision is grounded in how a real customer actually moves through the space, not a floor plan on paper.
“It gives us a way to grow that is cost-effective, sustainable and futureproof, and Wigan has shown us exactly how that can work across the wider estate as we continue to invest in our stores.”
Apollo3D, which was founded in 2017 and is based at Wharfebank Mills in Otley, has a client list spanning retail, healthcare, hospitality and facilities management, including Primark, Marks & Spencer, Greene King, the NHS and OCS.

items.body:
Walmart gets onboard with OpenAI’s ChatGPT fashion push as virtual try-on and favourites launch
Shoppers can use selfies to visualise clothing and accessories, explore looks from screenshots and save finds before buying through retailers’ websites.
A dress spotted on social media, an outfit for an autumn wedding or a new style to try: OpenAI is adding tools to ChatGPT that let shoppers move from an idea to an image of themselves wearing it, with Walmart among the retailers involved from launch.
The new Virtual Try On and Favourites features allow users to visualise clothing and accessories using their own photographs, then save products to return to later. Shoppers can describe what they want, upload an image of an item or use a screenshot as the starting point for a search.
Walmart is bringing its fashion range into the experience. Daniel Danker, EVP AI Acceleration, Product, and Design, said on LinkedIn that the US retail giant was working with OpenAI “from day one” to make its fashion available through Virtual Try On, Shop this Look and Favourites.
Sharing an example himself, he added: “Found something I like. Think I should I buy it?”
A selfie and a screenshot
OpenAI gives the example of shopping for a dress for an autumn wedding in Vermont. A user can upload a photograph of themselves alongside a screenshot of a dress they are considering and ask ChatGPT to generate a virtual try-on.
The search can also start with a description, such as a black-tie dress with a halter neckline, or inspiration from a celebrity outfit or a look found on social media. For clothing and accessories shown in shopping results, users can select “Try on” and take or upload a selfie. Alternatively, they can add a product image directly to a conversation and ask to see how it might look on them.
“See it. Try it on. Save it for later,” OpenAI says in its Instagram post introducing the tools.
Favorites gives those discoveries a home in ChatGPT’s Library, where users can bookmark products and organise them into folders. The launch announcement says shoppers can revisit saved items and their try-on images before making purchases through merchants’ websites.
The generated pictures have limitations. OpenAI says they may not reproduce the person or product exactly and do not guarantee size or fit. Reference photographs are retained for future try-ons, with options to change or delete them in settings.
Another fashion shopping channel for Walmart
Walmart’s involvement builds on its existing relationship with OpenAI. In October 2025, the retailer announced plans to let customers shop through ChatGPT using Instant Checkout, covering purchases made within the chatbot. The new fashion announcement also describes journeys that take shoppers to merchants’ own websites to buy.
Virtual try-on is already part of Walmart’s online fashion business. In September 2022, it introduced Be Your Own Model, using technology from its Zeekit acquisition to show clothing on customers’ own photographs. Walmart said that service covered more than 270,000 items at launch, including Free Assembly, Scoop and other own label and national brands. The figure describes its earlier offering; the supplied announcement does not specify how many Walmart products are supported in the new ChatGPT experience.
OpenAI says its new features build on ChatGPT Images 2.5 and will be available globally across all ChatGPT consumer plans on mobile, web and desktop.
So hot right now
OpenAI is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

PrettyLittleThing kicks off a fresh take on sports-inspired style with its first-ever collaboration with the National Football League (NFL), the professional American football league.
Bringing together the energy and heritage of American football with PrettyLittleThing’s fashion forward style, the collection puts a contemporary spin on classic varsity dressing.
For the first time, the iconic NFL influence meets PrettyLittleThing’s signature approach to trend-led fashion, designed to take you from game day to everyday life. The collection blends nostalgic sporting influences, with recognisable NFL inspired details.
Varsity inspired styles, ideal for everyday dressing. Elevated athleisure designed to achieve the off-duty aesthetic, effortlessly. Slogan tees, oversized outerwear and boxy silhouettes with timeless retro detailing. Colour pops of red sit alongside primary shades of ash grey, navy, forest green, oatmeal and cream. Looks that are in a league of their own.
The standout? The one-of-a-kind American Football Bag (of course). A timeless burgundy colourway is elevated with gold accents and embossed NFL shield detailing. The perfect accessory. Game day dressing (that goes the distance) brought to you by PrettyLittleThing, in collaboration with NFL, Officially Licensed Product.
A PrettyLittleThing representative added: “We are delighted to collaborate with the NFL on our Official Licensed Product range. Our 25-piece collection was designed in-house and highlights the dynamic intersection between female fashion and sport fandom.”
“The timeless style and prestige of the NFL comes to life in this collaboration with PrettyLittleThing.” said Salha Latif, vice president, international consumer products and licensing. “The range of apparel on offer celebrates what makes the NFL so distinctive, providing clothing for all fans in all settings, perfect timing ahead of the 2026 NFL London Games kicking off this weekend.”

The £5M redevelopment of the Bridge of Allan site has seen the former Co-op store – […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Co-op is launching its new Bridge of Allan store (Friday, 2 October), opening its doors and welcoming the community into the their new Co-op following a multi-million pound investment to transform the shopping experience for the Stirlingshire spa town.
The £5M redevelopment of the Bridge of Allan site has seen the former Co-op store – which was located in a converted garage – knocked down and replaced with more than 10,000 sq ft of retail and back-of-shop space across two floors. The extensive programme of works provide the community with a modern, purpose-built store which is fit for the future. Building materials have been used which are sympathetic to the local area and, behind the scenes, new facilities provide for colleague wellbeing and, enhanced storage and warehousing to promote product availability and resilience.
The store will open between 7am-10pm daily, and supports over 20 local jobs. The new store includes Costa coffee express and hot food – including a serve-over counter by Fife-based Stephens Bakery. Other added services include key cutting and a photo booth, with a free-to-use ATM providing access to cash in the community.
The online home delivery of groceries is available through Co-op’s own online shop – shop.coop.co.uk – and its delivery partners, with orders picked fresh in the local store and delivered quickly and conveniently in the community. Parcel collection services are also available. This all sits alongside Co-op’s focus on fresh and healthy produce; meats and dairy; meal ideas; food to go; fresh flowers; ready meals; pizzas and, award-winning beers, wines and spirits.
Customer car parking has also been enhanced, with resurfacing work and additional spaces created by Co-op, and EV charging also set to be introduced after launch. Ownership of part of the car park will be returned to Stirling Council.
A key focus throughout the works, which commenced in June 2024, has been Co-op’s commitment to working closely with and listening to the community, with outcomes including the provision of a temporary store, ATM and online delivery throughout the majority of the works to continue to serve and support the community.
Andy Baird, Co-op’s divisional operations director, said: “We are delighted to invest in Bridge of Allan – the whole team is excited to now be welcoming the community into their brand new Co-op, the new store looks fantastic. We are so grateful for all the support from the community throughout the works. We have invested to develop a store for Bridge of Allan which is fit for the future, our aim is to have created a hub contributing to local life and meeting the needs of our community and visitors to the area. We have a focus on offering quality products, value and choice that can be enjoyed by everyone along with a range of added services.
“We’re proud to serve Bridge of Allan, and we are now enjoying welcoming the community as they pop into their new Co-op. We’re here to contribute to local life and conveniently serve and support the community.”
Rachel Hargreaves, Co-op’s director of property, development and estates, said: “The investment in Bridge of Allan is a wonderful example of Co-op’s ongoing work to innovate and enhance its estate which, alongside our investment in price, products and proposition, is designed to give our members and customers what they want and need, locally and conveniently. I am proud of the whole team effort, and in particular of how the local community has been at the heart of our approach throughout the process – listening to local residents has helped to shape the programme of works and creation of the new store. I am delighted to see this redevelopment now come to fruition, and thrilled that we are welcoming the community into their brand-new local Co-op.”

items.body:
LeMieux, the leading global clothing, footwear and equestrian brand, has appointed James Davenport as chief financial officer and Richard Cotter as non-executive chairman, as the business enters its next phase of international growth.
Davenport brings more than two decades of senior financial and operational leadership, with a career spanning finance, strategy, manufacturing, supply chain, technology and business transformation. He joins LeMieux from Neal’s Yard Remedies, where he served as chief finance officer.
Prior to Neal’s Yard Remedies, Davenport spent more than 21 years at innocent drinks as chief operating officer, joining the business during its early growth phase when it had a small team and annual revenues of around £7 million. During his tenure, he played a key role in the transformation and international expansion of the business, helping it grow to approximately £470 million in annual revenue. He was involved in supporting the launch into new international markets, establishing the company’s own manufacturing facility and supporting a business that now sells more than one million drinks every day.
Richard Cotter joins LeMieux as non-executive chairman, bringing extensive experience in consumer, retail and international brand businesses. An experienced CEO and non-executive director, Cotter was previously Global Brand President of Berghaus, where he helped grow the business into one of the leading global outdoor brands, chairman of Jack Wolfskin the €350m German outdoor and lifestyle brand and the executive chairman of Jollyes Retail Group the fast growing pet retailer, supporting its rapid store rollout and successful sale in 2024.
He has also held a number of senior board and advisory roles across consumer and retail businesses and currently serves as chairman of The Sleep Group, Absolute Collagen and the Kindred nursery group. His experience in building brands, scaling retail businesses and leading organisations through periods of significant growth will be particularly valuable as LeMieux continues its international expansion.
Thw appointments come at an important stage in LeMieux’s development. LeMieux is the supplier of choice to world-class athletes, with a strong and highly engaged global community, the brand has built significant momentum internationally and continues to expand its product offering and reach.
As chief financial officer, Davenport will lead LeMieux’s global finance organisation, supporting the company’s continued investment in product innovation, digital capability, international expansion and operational excellence.
“LeMieux has built an exceptional brand with a passionate community, an outstanding reputation and an exciting vision for the future. I’m delighted to be joining the business at such an important stage in its journey and look forward to helping support its continued growth while maintaining the entrepreneurial spirit and customer focus that have made the company so successful,” said Davenport.
“James brings an exceptional combination of financial leadership, operational expertise and experience scaling internationally recognised consumer brands. His track record of supporting sustainable growth and building high-performing teams makes him an outstanding addition to our executive leadership team, and we’re delighted to welcome him to LeMieux,” said Dan Mahoney, CEO, LeMieux
On the appointment of Richard Cotter as non-executive chairman, Mahoney said: “Richard’s experience and leadership will be invaluable as LeMieux enters its next phase of growth. He brings a wealth of commercial and strategic expertise, and his appointment further strengthens our Board as we continue to build LeMieux into a truly global equestrian and lifestyle brand.”
The appointments reflect LeMieux’s continued investment in strengthening its leadership capability as the premium equestrian and lifestyle brand accelerates growth across international markets.

items.body:
Your next beauty appointment just got easier. Superdrug has launched an online booking service for its Beauty Studio, giving customers a simple new way to plan their treatments before they even step into the store.
From a fresh Mylee gel mani and perfectly shaped brows to a new hair colour or piercing, customers can now pre-book a wide range of treatments with Superdrug’s experienced beauty therapists. Each appointment includes a consultation, helping customers find the treatment and finish that works for them.
Treatments available include:
- Nails, including Gel Polish and Builder Gel manicures, nail extensions and pedicures.
- Brows, including shaping and tinting
- Waxing, including full-face waxing and threading
- Lashes, including Korean lash lifts, strip lash application, tinting and express lash extensions
- Hair, from an extensive colour menu and complete restyles to fresh blow-dries
- Piercings (walk in only)
Following the continued success of Superdrug’s Beauty Studios and growing demand for its in-store beauty services, online booking is now live across 72 stores. The service will roll out to over 200 Beauty Studio locations by the end of October, making it even easier for customers to secure a convenient appointment and fit a little beauty time into their day.
Stores already offering online booking include White City, Manchester Arndale, Cribbs Causeway, Merry Hill, Stratford, Cardiff St Davids, Newry Buttercrane, Brighton Churchill Sq, Edinburgh Princes St and Doncaster Frenchgate New.
For nail lovers, there’s plenty to choose from. Superdrug’s skilled nail technicians use Mylee’s TPO-free, real gel formulas to create everything from classic manis to personalised nail art, with a glossy finish that lasts for up to three weeks. With an extensive choice of colours, finishes and effects, customers can find a Mylee mani to match every mood and personal style. Mylee products are also available in Superdrug stores and online to recreate the look at home.
Brows remain another Beauty Studio favourite, with shaping and tinting offering a quick and easy way to refresh and define them. From a subtle tidy-up to a more sculpted finish, experienced beauty therapists can tailor each treatment to the customer and their desired look.
Simon Comins, chief operating officer at Superdrug, said: “At Superdrug, we want more customers to be able to enjoy professional beauty treatments without compromising on convenience or value. Our Beauty Studios bring expert, on-trend services to the high street, and as demand continues to grow, introducing online booking is a natural next step in making those services even easier to access.”
“Customers will have greater flexibility to plan their visit and secure an appointment at a time that works for them. It also brings our store and online experiences closer together, making it easier for customers to discover and enjoy Beauty Studio services in a way that suits them.”
The launch is the latest step in Superdrug’s continued online and offline strategy, creating a more connected experience across its stores and website and giving customers greater flexibility over how they discover, book and enjoy its beauty services.
Michael Bryce, CEO at HSNF, said: “We’re proud to partner with Superdrug to deliver professional treatments with Mylee. With our extensive colour range and high quality gel formulas, online booking makes it easier than ever for customers to enjoy the Mylee experience at Superdrug.”
Customers can book their next Beauty Studio appointment online via the Superdrug Beauty Studio: https://www.superdrug.com/beauty-studio

items.body:
Red Bull is giving EA SPORTS FC™ 27 players the chance to take their game beyond the screen, with Limited Edition Red Bull Wings Cup cans launching nationwide.
Available in stores from September 1st, the Limited Edition cans unlock exclusive in-game rewards and give players a route into Red Bull Wings Cup, a global EA SPORTS FC™ 27 competition offering players the chance to compete for a place at the Global Final in Miami in January 2027.
Each participating can features a QR code and unique code under the can tab, which consumers can redeem for 250 EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Season Points, an exclusive Red Bull Wings Cup Ultimate Team Kit and a Red Bull Wings Cup Loan Player Item.
Players can start preparing their Ultimate Teams from 18th September, ahead of the Red Bull Wings Cup, with redeemable in-game rewards.
From 27th September, players across the UK can register for the Red Bull Wings Cup through a series of online and offline qualifiers. PlayStation Tournament Online Qualifiers will run until 1st November, alongside University Qualifiers running through to 7th November, giving players across the country the opportunity to battle their way to the UK National Final.
Players who progress through the Playstation Tournament Open Qualifiers and Red Bull Wings Cup live activations will advance to the online FACEIT Closed Qualifiers, battling through a single-elimination bracket hosted via FACEIT.
Six of the country’s top players will then emerge from the Closed Qualifiers to head to the Red Bull Gaming Sphere in London on 14th November for the UK National Final, going head-to-head for the chance to represent the UK at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami in January 2027.
Red Bull Player Angry Ginge and EA SPORTS FC esports star Tekkz will front the Red Bull Wings Cup action throughout the campaign:
Red Bull Player Angry Ginge, said, “I’m proper excited to be part of Red Bull Wings Cup. EA SPORTS FC is a massive part of my life and content, but this is a chance to experience it in a completely different way, with anyone able to get involved and compete for the chance to take it all the way to Miami. I’m looking forward to seeing who steps up and makes it to the World Final.”
Alongside the tournament, fans will also have the chance to win a range of football and gaming prizes through the ASDA exclusive Red Bull Wings Cup 4-Pack. Prizes include a trip for two to the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami, 23 pairs of Premier League match tickets, Red Bull Wings Cup jerseys, a PlayStation 5 Pro and PlayStation DualSense controllers, as well as copies of EA SPORTS FC™ 27.
From picking up a can and unlocking exclusive in-game rewards to competing for a place in Miami, Red Bull Wings Cup brings EA SPORTS FC™ 27 and football together across the UK, giving players the chance to take their game beyond the screen and onto the global stage.
More information on Red Bull Wings Cup, including Terms and Conditions, can be found at www.redbull.co.uk/wings-cup
*A maximum of four codes can be redeemed per account. Rewards are automatically delivered within EA SPORTS FC™ 27 once the code has been redeemed.

items.body:
Waitrose St. Neots unveiled its new look store this morning following a multi-million pound refurbishment. The refreshed store offers customers an enhanced shopping experience, with a modernised look and feel, new and improved product selections, and innovative technology.
Celebrating its 40th anniversary next year, the upgraded branch features a host of new improvements:
- Upgraded Service Counters: Modernised meat and fish counters staffed by expert Partners ready to offer preparation advice, cooking tips, and recommendations.
- Redesigned Bakery: An expanded, refreshed bakery section offering daily breakfast staples and specialty artisan favourites.
- New Refrigeration: For improved energy efficiency.
- Electronic Shelf Labels: Freeing up Partners from manual updates, allowing them to dedicate even more time to delivering outstanding customer service.
- Dedicated John Lewis Click and Collect Desk: for faster collections and returns.
Branch manager, Tim Stanton, who leads a team of 140 Partners said: “This is a milestone moment for our store. We are approaching 40 years since we first opened our doors and we’re thrilled to now share a refreshed and improved store with the wonderful St Neots community. Every detail of the refurbishment, from the new bakery to modernised counters, was created with food lovers in mind, and to meet the high standards you expect from Waitrose.”
The first customers through the doors will be greeted with a complimentary glass of prosecco or orange juice, and a commemorative reusable Waitrose tote bag for their groceries, with even more food and drink tastings taking place across the weekend.
Nationwide investment
Waitrose is committed to investing in its estate, including nationwide refurbishments and new openings. This forms part of a £1bn, multi-year programme designed to offer the very best products, service and shops for customers.
The past month has also seen refurbishments of stores in Finchley, Balham and Clapham Junction, and Waitrose is on track to open two new supermarkets this year in Hale Barns (Greater Manchester) and Cricklewood (North West London). Waitrose is also refurbishing 28 shops this year and launching into airport travel retail for the first time in four new RELAY stores in Heathrow Terminal 2.

items.body:
Co-op is pleased to announce the appointment of Alex Dower as managing director of its Retail business.
Dower joins Co-op with more than two decades of senior leadership experience spanning food retail, convenience, hospitality and FMCG. He has held leadership roles at some of the world’s most recognised consumer brands, including Tesco, Holland & Barrett, Pret A Manger, Harrods, Woolworths Australia, Mars and PepsiCo, building a reputation as a leader who combines commercial success with a strong sense of purpose.
His appointment comes at an exciting time for Co-op’s Retail business as it continues to maintain business momentum, alongside The Co-op Group’s other Food and Life Services’ business channels. In his new role Dower will be directly responsible for one of the UK’s largest convenience retailers with a store footprint in over 2,300 locations, a fast-growing quick commerce operation and with an annual turnover in excess of £7.25 billion.
Throughout his career, Dower has successfully led complex transformations in customer-facing businesses operating at scale. At Holland & Barrett, where he was CEO International, he led a significant turnaround across multiple international markets, building high-performing teams, step changing the Own Brand product proposition and improving operational effectiveness, resulting in sustained sales and profit growth.
During his time as CCO at Woolworths Australia, Dower led a major transformation of the retailer’s fresh food offer, developing new customer propositions, price and promotional strategies and Partnerships that delivered significant business growth.
Dower’s breadth of experience spans some of the world’s most competitive retail markets. A common thread throughout his career has been an ability to combine customer insight, operational excellence and commercial discipline to drive sustainable growth.
As managing director, Dower will focus on accelerating Co-op Food retail growth, strengthening the customer proposition, supporting continued innovation across stores and digital channels, and ensuring the business continues to deliver value for members while remaining true to Co-op’s purpose and values.
Commenting on his appointment Kate Allum, Interim Group CEO said: “Alex brings a wealth of experience and a passion for building successful customer-focused businesses, in ways that make a meaningful difference to customers’ everyday lives. His personal values and leadership approach are fully aligned with our Co-op and I’m excited about the impact he will have in driving our Food Retail business forwards. “
Commenting on his appointment Dower said: “I’m delighted to be joining Co-op at such an important time for the business. Co-op stores are woven into communities across the UK, and I’m looking forward to working with our fantastic colleagues to make it even more relevant to members and customers every day. Co-op’s purpose and values are what set it apart, and I’m excited to build upon the strong foundations already in place, accelerating growth and innovation, while staying true to what makes Co-op so special.”

items.title: Aldi debt jumps by £100m as profit slips at discount grocer
items.summary: Aldi took on more than £100m in net debt last year, as the discount grocer’s profit slipped despite its blockbuster expansion plans.  The supermarket chain, the UK’s fourth largest, saw its net debt grow by a fifth in 2025, from £717m to £862m.  Aldi’s jump in debt comes despite the grocer’s plans to expand rapidly [...]
items.body:
Aldi debt jumps by £100m as profit slips at discount grocer
Aldi took on more than £100m in net debt last year, as the discount grocer’s profit slipped despite its blockbuster expansion plans.
The supermarket chain, the UK’s fourth largest, saw its net debt grow by a fifth in 2025, from £717m to £862m.
Aldi’s jump in debt comes despite the grocer’s plans to expand rapidly in the UK. Last week, chief executive Giles Hurley announced £900m in funding to open 40 new stores next year.
Hurley said last week that the supermarket’s operating profit held steady at £433m last year, though new company filings show its pre-tax profit slipped from £416m to £400m.
The family-owned grocer’s workforce fell from 50,655 to 49,661 in the year to December 2025, its filings revealed, suggesting it cut about 1,000 staff in the year.
Despite the falling headcount, the supermarket chain’s wage costs jumped from £1.43bn to £1.46bn.
Aldi eyes more market share
Aldi’s debt pile, while rising, remains well below that of some of its private-equity-owned rivals.
Net debt at Morrisons, which is owned by New York-based Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, jumped from £7.1bn to £7.5bn in the year to October. Asda, owned by London-based TDR Capital, has debts of £3.5bn.
While Asda and Morrisons have sought to sell off the freehold rights to some of its shops in a bid to push down their debt piles, Aldi is hoping to put more pressure on the UK’s ‘big four’ supermarkets.
Aldi and fellow German discounter Lidl have surged to dominance of Britain’s grocery market in recent decades. Morrisons is now the UK’s fifth-biggest supermarket, having been leapfrogged by Aldi earlier this year.
Aldi is within one per cent of Asda’s market share, though its control of the market has weakened from 10.8 to 10.6 per cent over the past year, according to figures from Worldpanel.
Announcing the grocer’s results last week, Hurley hit out at rival supermarkets for offering loyalty discounts, which he says give shoppers a misleading impression of value.
He told reporters: “One of the drivers of their growth is the fact that their retail prices are going up, and some of them are seeing volume decline at the same time.
“We are driving prices down, and we’re growing our volumes, and that is hugely important in continuing to reinforce our confidence around growing our business and expanding.”
Aldi UK is part of the grocery chain’s Aldi Sud branch, which is controlled by the heirs of Karl Albrecht. He co-founded the grocer with his brother, Theo, in 1946.
Aldi was contacted for comment.

items.title: Wetherspoons urges Budget 'common sense' as soaring costs send profits tumbling
items.summary: Sir Tim Martin warned that Labour's actions, notably in the last two budgets, were 'leading to job losses, closures and high street dereliction'.
items.body:
Wetherspoons urges Budget 'common sense' as soaring costs send profits tumbling
Wetherspoons has urged for common sense to prevail at the Budget after a sharp rise in employment costs and business rates hit profits.
Sir Tim Martin, chair of the pub group, urged the Government to refrain from more tax hikes, which has already led to the ‘dereliction’ of the high street.
‘The hospitality industry, as many commentators and companies have noted, has borne the brunt of government-led tax and regulatory cost increases, especially in the last two budgets,’ he said.
‘This has resulted in pubs becoming even more expensive than supermarkets, leading to job losses, closures and high street dereliction.’
Sir Tim Martin, boss of JD Wetherspoon, said taxes hikes were leading to job losses
A boost in sales thanks to the warmer weather failed to offset a 5.3 per cent jump in costs, with pre-tax profits plummeting by 28 per cent to £58.6million for the year to July 26.
‘Common sense and economic principle surely indicate that a sensible rebalancing of taxes would generate more jobs and more revenue for the government,’ Wetherspoons told investors.
Martin has repeatedly flagged substantial cost rises eating into the group's bottom line and today said rising energy, repair and employment costs had had a 'heavy influence on most other input prices' and 'rose more than sales'.
The pub chain said the cost of employing its 42,000 staff at its 792 pubs across the country jumped £46million in the year to July 26, while repair costs surged £31million and its business rates bill increased by £9million.
Martin added: 'It is to be hoped that the powers-that-be will refrain from any further increases, since pubs and restaurants pay around 40 per cent of their receipts as taxes of one sort or another - and provide immense financial support to the Treasury, as well as social support to the community.'
The hospitality giant reported a 5.2 per cent jump in total sales for the year, with like-for-like sales growth of 4.2 per cent.
It was driven by a 6.1 per cent jump in bar sales, while food sales and revenue from its hotel rooms rose 1.2 and 1.3 per cent, respectively. Fruit machine sales rose 7.4 per cent.
Wetherspoons said it had been boosted by ‘exceptional weather’, pushing like-for-like sales 8.6 per cent higher in the nine weeks to September 27.
It said it benefited from ‘substantial progress’ to increase the number of beer gardens and outside seating areas across its pubs.
Shares rose 7.38 per cent to 873p, bringing this year's gains to 17.5 per cent.
Richard Hunter, head of markets at Interactive Investor, said: 'Wetherspoon had previously warned that higher costs would place a large stain on profits, and the prediction has unfortunately played out although the group remains resolute in its ambitions.'
He added: 'Spoons has been dealt some difficult hands over the years which, for the most part, it has been resolute in turning into profit.
'The group’s value model leaves it continually bumping up against a wall of higher costs, which puts perennial pressure on margins and profits.'

items.title: Wetherspoon boss attacks Labour for ‘high street dereliction’ as profit falls
items.summary: Pub chain Wetherspoon has hit out at the government for causing “high street dereliction” by hiking taxes, as the company’s profit slipped by a quarter.  The London-listed pub group saw revenue jump by five per cent to £2.2bn in the year to July – in line with analyst forecasts – though pre-tax profit fell further [...]
items.body:
Wetherspoon boss attacks Labour for ‘high street dereliction’ as profit falls
Pub chain Wetherspoon has hit out at the government for causing “high street dereliction” by hiking taxes, as the company’s profit slipped by a quarter.
The London-listed pub group saw revenue jump by five per cent to £2.2bn in the year to July – in line with analyst forecasts – though pre-tax profit fell further than expected, by 28 per cent to £59m.
Sir Tim Martin, Wetherspoon’s chairman, blamed the Labour government for hiking business rates, minimum wages and national insurance contributions (NICs).
He said: “The hospitality industry, as many commentators and companies have noted, has borne the brunt of government-led tax and regulatory cost increases, especially in the last two budgets.
“This has resulted in pubs becoming even more expensive than supermarkets, leading to job losses, closures and high street dereliction.”
Wetherspoon is famed for its rock-bottom prices, but analysts have predicted that this could mean rising taxes and energy costs will weigh more heavily on it than some of its higher-margin rivals. The pubco’s operating margin slimmed from 6.9 to 5.4 per cent in the last year.
Heatwaves boost summer sales
The FTSE 250 pub firm blamed a five per cent increase in costs for its falling profit. The group paid £46 more in wages, £31m more in repairs and £9m more in business rates last year.
Wetherspoon’s energy costs jumped by 77 per cent to £40m last year, it told shareholders. Energy costs and packaging taxes have also “weighed heavily” on hospitality firms in recent years, Martin said.
The pub firm said its sales picked up in recent months, helped by “exceptional weather”. Like-for-like sales grew by 8.6 per cent in the last nine weeks, it said.
This has been helped by “substantial progress in recent years in increasing the number of beer gardens and outside seating areas”.
Martin claimed Wetherspoon is outperforming the wider pub sector. Like-for-like sales at the company grew by 7.7 per cent in August, compared to sector-wide growth of 0.8 per cent, according to NIQ figures.
The Wetherspoon boss reiterated his calls for John Healey to cut VAT on hospitality firms from 20 to 10 per cent.
The pub chain has backed a campaign, led by celebrity chef Tom Kerridge, which claims this tax break would be the easiest way to prevent swathes of insolvencies and job losses on the high street.
Shares in JD Wetherspoon jumped eight per cent to 880.5p in early trading.

items.title: Almost half of Fayed abuse accusers are potential trafficking victims, MPs told
items.summary: Exclusive: Met police say 70 women’s accounts have hallmarks of trafficking, suggesting case numbers could rise Almost half of the women who reported allegations of sexual abuse by Mohamed Al Fayed to the Metropolitan police are potential victims of human trafficking, MPs have been told. In a briefing for the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) for the survivors of Fayed and Harrods in July, senior Met officers said a review earlier this year found 70 survivors’ accounts bore the hallmarks of trafficking. Continue reading...
items.body:
Almost half of the women who reported allegations of sexual abuse by Mohamed Al Fayed to the Metropolitan police are potential victims of human trafficking, MPs have been told.
In a briefing for the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) for the survivors of Fayed and Harrods in July, senior Met officers said a review earlier this year found 70 survivors’ accounts bore the hallmarks of trafficking.
The Home Office has confirmed that at least five survivors were victims of international and domestic trafficking.
The Met’s figures suggested the number of confirmed cases could climb much higher, said the Liberal Democrat MP Wendy Chamberlain, a co-chair of the APPG.
“I can’t believe that wouldn’t increase,” said Chamberlain, who also compared the scale of Fayed’s abuse to Jimmy Savile’s.
The Labour MP Dave Robertson, the APPG’s other co-chair, said: “The number of women who were trafficked by Mohammed Fayed and his trafficking ring is certainly much higher.”
Some women were trafficked from Harrods to Fayed’s private offices and residence in Park Lane while others were taken out of the UK and abused overseas, senior police officers running the Met’s investigation, Operation Cornpoppy, told the APPG.
But several survivors told the Guardian that the Home Office had not recognised them as victims of trafficking because they now live abroad.
Amy, who lives in Italy, said she was trafficked from Harrods, where she initially worked on the shop floor, and her home to Fayed’s other properties. She said she was transferred to a PA role in his private residence and office at 60 Park Lane in London, where he allegedly sexually abused her, including groping her breasts and forced kissing.
She said Fayed also took her in his private car and helicopter to his estate in Oxted, Surrey, where she was sexually assaulted in a lagoon-style swimming pool located behind a concealed door.
“I would be removed from my home in Hammersmith and then be changed into clothes like Lacoste polo shirts and Bermuda shorts and boat shoes, which I absolutely hated,” said Amy. “That was robbing me of my actual identity. Whoever saw me leave my bedsit would say that’s not her. That’s a strong component of what trafficking is and was very calculating.”
In a letter sent in June to the then minister for safeguarding and violence against women and girls, Natalie Fleet, Amy raised concerns about the apparent exclusion of survivors living outside the UK from the Home Office assessment of potential trafficking victims, the National Referral Mechanism (NRM).
She received a response from the Home Office in August, which said there was not a requirement that a potential victim be resident in the UK before being referred to the NRM by the police, or another first responder organisation.
But last month Amy was informed by her contact officer at the Met that the Home Office had confirmed it would reject any referrals made for international residents.
KP Law (KPL), which represents Amy and 277 other alleged survivors of Fayed’s abuse, said nearly a quarter of those women now lived overseas.
Lucy Traynor, a senior associate at KPL, criticised the apparently inconsistent advice as to who was eligible to be recognised as a victim of trafficking.
The lawyer said: “We are still seeing individuals whose experiences meet the threshold for trafficking struggling to secure recognition through these systems which are designed to identify and protect victims. Amy’s case is a stark example. Despite the nature of what she experienced, she continues to face barriers to recognition outside the UK. That disconnect between what the Home Office has committed to and what survivors experience in practice is simply not acceptable.”
First responders including police forces and some charities can refer someone to the NRM if they suspect they are a victim of human trafficking.
The Home Oﬃce then makes an initial “reasonable grounds” decision if it believes a crime may have occurred before investigating further and making a final “conclusive grounds” decision. So far it has confirmed that five women allegedly abused by Fayed were trafficking victims.
Eleanor Lyons, the independent anti-slavery commissioner, said the Home Office’s statutory guidance explicitly stated that people needed to be in the UK to be referred to the NRM.
Lyons said this was because the process involved getting access to support including a safe house and counselling, which officials believed would be difficult to provide to people who do not live in the UK.
But she called on the Home Office to reconsider the requirement because many affected people she spoke to just wanted to be recognised as trafficking victims, adding that the situation was causing deep distress for alleged survivors of Fayed’s abuse.
“The government should be doing everything it can to make it easier to identify these women and recognise them as potential victims of modern slavery,” Lyons said. “They’re doing directly the opposite right now, which is causing further harm to the survivors.”
Survivors’ groups say more than 500 women have come forward about abuse that allegedly took place at Harrods, Park Lane, Fulham football club, the Ritz hotel in Paris, and other places owned by Fayed. The Met is investigating 165 victims who have contacted the force directly.
A Met police spokesperson said: “We were previously making referrals to the Home Office for victims living in the UK and abroad, but those relating to victims living abroad were being rejected. As a result, we have paused any further such referrals. Should the Home Office position change, we will restart those submissions. Our support to victims continues, regardless of where they live.”
A Home Office spokesperson paid tribute to “the incredible bravery” of survivors of Fayed’s alleged abuse. They added: “We are ensuring modern slavery survivors get the support they need to recover and move on with their lives.”
A Harrods spokesperson said it “supports all survivors in their pursuit of justice and continues to work closely with the Met police on its investigation”.

items.body:
Tesco F&F notches up an in-store virtual try-on first: this week's biggest retail technology stories
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Walmart, Iceland Foods, JB Hi-Fi, Vusion, Halfords, H&M, Lincolnshire Co-op, The Barcode Warehouse, JD Sports, Paul Smith, Sitoo, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
1. Tesco teams with AIUTA to test out virtual try-on technology for F&F clothing in Sandhurst Extra store
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
2. Walmart head honcho John Furner looks to draw a line in the sand on AI, technology and pricing
John Furner, President and CEO at Walmart, has written an open letter to the US retail giant's customers about AI and pricing. "For more than 50 years, our pricing principle has been Every Day Low Prices (EDLP). Prices can change. We lower them when we can pass savings along. Sometimes they rise because an item costs more to buy or transport,” he writes.
“But using someone’s income, shopping history or moment of need to charge them more would violate the EDLP promise our business model is built on. We won’t do it. YOU are at the heart of our why and our relationship with you has always been built on trust. For decades, our associates have built that trust, one interaction at a time. So, as technology improves, we’re putting the same attention on trust and serving you as we do when you walk into our stores and clubs."
He adds: "I've heard concerns about companies using that information and technology to charge you more. want to tell you where we stand: We price the product, not the person. Many of you have seen the digital shelf labels in our stores and some have asked why we have them. A shelf price should match what rings up at checkout. Digital shelf labels help us do that more consistently by displaying the right price. They also save associates time replacing paper tags. It may sound like an easy task, but as someone who has had to change those paper tags by hand over the years, I can tell you it’s a time-consuming and unrewarding task. Our associates would much rather be helping you, our customers."
AI, Furner notes, has added new ways for Walmart to serve its customers and members. But there are also questions about the information it has access to.
“Understanding our customers and members is what makes us special and allows us to better serve them. For years, that has taken place in our stores and clubs as we help each customer with their individual needs. We want to offer that same level of personalised care when our customers shop online with Sparky, our AI shopping assistant. When you engage with Sparky, that’s an invitation to serve you better, not to use your personal information to set a personalised price. We’ve never used the relationships our associates have with customers to charge more, and we won’t do that with AI,” Furner says.
He concludes: “With that in mind, I want to share three commitments you can count on as technology changes: We don't set different prices based on who you are or the time of day, and we won't. Your income, shopping history, urgency or what we think you could pay won't change the price. And whether you’re buying groceries or electronics on a hot afternoon or in a sudden rush for an item, it's never a reason to charge you more. We'll hold our shopping tools to the same promise.”
“We won't use the information you share with us on Sparky or otherwise to raise your price or hide lower priced options that meet your needs. We’ll continue to use your information responsibly and respect your choices. You decide whether to share additional details for more personalised help. We’ll continue to be clear about how we use that information, protect it and honor the choices you make. When you do share, we will focus that data on ways that better serve you. Our people will continue to oversee pricing, and we'll monitor and test our technology against these commitments.
3. H&M overhauls onsite search across more than 60 markets in technology partnership with Voyado
H&M has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” says Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, says: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”
4. Iceland Foods taps Retail Insight AI powered solution as retailer tackles growing food waste problem
Iceland Foods has partnered with Retail Insight to deploy its AI powered WasteInsight solution as part of the retailer's focus on reducing food waste.
General Manager of EMEA and APAC at Retail Insight, Martin Rigby, says: "Retailers have access to more operational data than ever before, but data only creates value when it enables better decisions. The opportunity is to move from reporting what has already happened to identifying where action is needed before waste occurs.”
"We are delighted to be working with Iceland to support its continued focus on reducing food waste. By combining AI with operational insight, WasteInsight helps surface the products and actions that matter most, enabling colleagues to intervene earlier and with greater confidence."
Iceland Foods’ Stores Director, Steve Shirley, says: "Reducing food waste remains an important priority for Iceland. We are continually looking at ways to improve how we use operational data to support our colleagues in making faster, better informed decisions in stores.”
"Working with Retail Insight will help us explore how AI driven operational intelligence can support our waste reduction objectives while improving consistency across our store operations."
5. JD Sports updates on RFID programme as Germany goes live and 1,000 stores milestone is reached
Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, has taken to social media to provide an update on the retailer’s RFID programme, which involves various countries and thousands of stores.
In a LinkedIn post, McGrath said: “This week, our final country goes live with RFID, Germany. And with that, everything we directly control will be live for phase one of our RFID programme. When I look back at what we’ve achieved, the numbers are pretty incredible: 1,000 stores directly launched in 14 months. And across the wider global group, working alongside our counterparts around the world: 2,700 stores live out of 4,800 in that same period, 192 stores a month!”
He added: “But the numbers only tell part of this story. RFID isn’t just about scanners, tags and technology. It’s about changing behaviours, processes and mindsets. We’ve done things that were uncomfortable. Challenged established ways of working. Asked people to rethink processes they’d used for years. And, most importantly, brought people with us on the journey. And we haven't done that alone.”
6. Australian consumer electronics retailer JB Hi-Fi taps Vusion digital shelf-edge tech across stores
Vusion has announced a new roll-out initiative at Australian retailer JB Hi-Fi’s stores. Under the agreement, JB Hi-Fi plans to deploy Vusion’s digital shelf-edge technology in Australia following a pilot phase, as well as a full roll-out across its New Zealand store network.
“We are focused on innovation that delivers efficiencies to our store operations and supports our teams in serving customers,” says Cameron Trainor, MD at JB Hi-Fi Australia. “Our collaboration with Vusion gives us a scalable technology platform to support store teams, strengthen execution and advance the next phase of our strategy.”
“We are very proud to support JB Hi-Fi as it takes this important step toward a more connected store network,” says Pierre Demoures, SEVP & COO at Vusion. “Australia is a key market for Vusion and JB Hi-Fi is one of the region’s most distinctive retailers. This agreement shows how connected store infrastructure can help leading retailers modernise operations while preserving the store experience that makes them unique.”
7. Fabeltics exec and CX and AI specialist Jack Roberts joins RTIH Innovation Awards judging panel for 2026

Welcome onboard, Jack!

Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.title: Would a gambling tax rise in the budget really shut shops and cost jobs?
items.summary: Most of the betting industry is urging the chancellor not to double slot machine duty to raise up to £460m more a year Gambling industry kingpins are fuming about reports that the chancellor, John Healey, is considering increasing taxes on high-street slot machines in his first budget. The influential Social Market Foundation thinktank, the most vocal advocate for a rise in machine games duty (MGD), from 20% to 40%, thinks the measure could raise between £275m and £460m annually , on top of the roughly £610m collected last year. Continue reading...
items.body:
Would a gambling tax rise in the budget really shut shops and cost jobs?
Most of the betting industry is urging the chancellor not to double slot machine duty to raise up to £460m more a year
Gambling industry kingpins are fuming about reports that the chancellor, John Healey, is considering increasing taxes on high-street slot machines in his first budget.
The billionaire owner of Betfred, Fred Done, is among industry bosses who say such a policy would force shop closures, cost jobs and ultimately fail in its objective, depriving the Treasury of taxes.
But not every figure in the gambling world agrees. Stewart Kenny, the co-founder of Paddy Power who has become a critic of his erstwhile industry, accused Done of “scaremongering”.
So who’s right? It’s complicated …
What does the industry say?
Bookies might be best known for bets on horses or football but they make big money from slot machines. The Betting and Gaming Council, an industry lobby group, commissioned a report from the accounting firm EY that estimated a duty rise to 40% could close up to 1,470 betting shops (nearly a third of the total 5,617), resulting in 15,900 job losses and a net loss to the exchequer of about £120m. Horse racing, which receives a levy from bookies’ profits, would also take a hit.
Done said he alone would be forced to close about 495 betting shops, nearly half of Betfred’s estate, with the loss of 2,475 jobs and £67m in taxes.
Entain, the owner of Ladbrokes and Coral, has written to Burnham saying it would have to make job cuts across its nationwide estate of 2,300 shops, were the policy to go ahead. Casinos and bingo halls are in the firing line too. Rank Group, which owns Mecca Bingo and Grosvenor Casinos, cautioned that a third of its venues could close, affecting 2,000 staff.
Are they crying wolf?
When dealing with bookmakers, it is wise to be sceptical.
Back in 2019, Betfred had about 1,620 shops. Since then, the company has threatened to close nearly 1,000 in response to tougher regulation or taxes. While most of the policies it objected to have come to pass, the number of shops has decreased by only about 330. Some of that is down to a broader shift to the web that has led to soaring online gambling revenues.
In one Betfred TV ad, Done encourages punters to “come and see me”. In your neighbourhood bookies? No, at Betfred.com. Meanwhile, the Done family has taken out tens of millions of pounds in dividends, including £50m in 2022 alone.
What it failed to mention is that it has been increasing its use of AI within the business since well before the tax rise. Some staff at Bet365’s Stoke HQ are understood to feel that government policy is a convenient smokescreen for good old-fashioned corporate cost-cutting.
A spokesperson said Bet365 was responding to a “highly competitive trading environment, plus increased regulatory and tax-related costs”.
So it’s all a bluff?
Well, no. The UK’s biggest gambling companies, including Betfred, Entain, Flutter and more, have all announced cuts since Reeves’s duty rise. It is impossible to say how much of this retrenchment might have happened anyway, given economic worries and structural shifts within the sector. However, it makes sense that any further increase in costs, in the form of higher taxes on slot machines, will negatively affect the gambling sector.
Simon Thomas, the chief executive of the Hippodrome Casino in London, says that fear of the tax is already hurting investment.
“We have a £6m rooftop expansion plan with full planning permission, ready to go. With MGD up in the air, we’ve had to shelve it,” he said, adding that if MGD goes up to 40%, a third of bingo halls and a third of casinos could close.
Does the government want a smaller gambling sector?
Burnham has already moved to limit the opening of new gambling premises. He has voiced particular concerns about 24-hour adult gaming centres (AGCs), high street venues packed with the sort of machines that would be more heavily taxed by an MGD increase. The rise of these “slot farms” is understood to be the main driver for any such move.
But there are question marks over whether AGCs would actually take the hit. They already have much lower overheads and looser regulation than casinos and bingo halls, which have experienced negligible growth. Last year, AGCs managed to increase their takings from £528m to £613m by packing more machines into larger venues.
So if slot machines taxes go up, in theory AGCs are best placed to survive the impact. The AGC operator Merkur has already offered to buy some of the 132 shops that Betfred put up for sale, indicating it is unruffled by the prospect of a tax rise. If others follow suit, just as bookies retrench, an MGD rise could simply lead to bookies being replaced by 24-hour slot farms.
As Treasury officials weigh up duty rises, they will have to consider the law of unintended consequences.

items.body:
Dafydd Moore exits Superdry and takes on Vice President Business Technology position at Burberry
Burberry has appointed Dafydd Moore as VP Business Technology. He joins from Superdry where he served as Director Global Technology (CIO). His CV also includes stints at Halfords, Dyson and Waitrose.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “After a fantastic chapter at Superdry, I’m excited to share that today I’m starting a new role at Burberry. A huge thank you to everyone at Superdry for the support, collaboration and experiences over the last couple of years. I’m incredibly grateful for the people I’ve worked with and everything we achieved together turning that business around. Now looking forward to the next chapter and getting started at Burberry.”
Jon-Paul Brett
Jon-Paul Brett has taken on the role of Chief Digital & Technology Officer at KFC UK & Ireland. He joins from Burberry, where he spent the past ten and a half years, most recently serving as Global Digital Director.
A spokesperson for KFC UK & Ireland said: “Our Original Recipe hasn’t changed. How we run KFC definitely has. Behind the scenes, we’re exploring how AI can empower our restaurants, giving our teams more time to focus on what matters most: our customers and our fried chicken.”
“With 70% of transactions already digital, we’re continuing to modernise our restaurants through new designs, digital kiosks, and digital drive-thrus. Creating a simpler, more convenient experience for customers, whether they eat in or take food to go. So there couldn’t be a better time to welcome Jon-Paul Brett our new Chief Digital & Technology Officer for KFC UK & Ireland.”
They added: “Jon-Paul joined us in July and has wasted no time getting stuck in. He’s been out in restaurants meeting the team members who use our tech every day, while also spending time with our Tech team and franchise partners to understand where the biggest opportunities lie to create best in class experiences for our teams and customers.”
Brett commented: “The best way to understand KFC UK & Ireland is to get close to the restaurants, teams, and franchise partners who bring the brand to life every day. Since joining as Chief Digital & Technology Officer last month, I’ve spent time across the business: meeting restaurant teams, working with our brilliant tech team, and getting to know our franchise community.”
He added: “There’s real energy across KFC; big ambition, passionate people, and a clear opportunity for technology to unlock the next stage of growth. What has stood out most is the pride in the brand, the pace in our restaurants, and the shared desire to keep improving for our customers. KFC UK & Ireland has a bold future ahead, with technology playing a critical role in shaping better experiences for our customers, employees, and franchise partners. Now the focus is on action: building the capability, pace, and partnerships that help our teams, customers, and franchise partners feel the benefit of technology every day.”
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
Lidl UK deploys new self-checkouts that show shoppers on screens across retailer’s store network
Lidl is rolling out new self-checkouts across its UK stores which play video footage back to customers while they are scanning their shopping. These will be deployed in all new stores and retrofitted into existing locations.
They will feature built in overhead cameras, vertically mounted large format screens, and LED lights to alert staff if people need help while scanning their shopping. To leave, customers must scan a receipt printed by the machine at a gate at the exit.
Roll-out is also taking place across hundreds of Lidl and Kaufland stores in Germany.
A Lidl spokesperson told RTIH: “The new self-checkouts are designed to be more customer friendly, enhancing the shopping experience while boosting efficiency.”
Lidl & Go
In July, Lidl GB announced it was expanding its Lidl & Go self-scanning trial to 37 additional stores across the UK, following positive customer feedback from an initial seven store pilot. This saw the feature become available to shoppers across Scotland, the South East and the wider South of England throughout July.
Integrated within the Lidl Plus app, Lidl & Go allows customers to scan products as they shop, track their spending and savings in real-time, and complete their purchase more seamlessly at checkout. The feature is available directly through customers' own smartphones, with no requirement for dedicated in-store scanning devices. Feedback from the initial trial has shown particular appeal among customers shopping with children and those looking for greater flexibility during their shop.
Louise Weise, Chief Customer Officer, at Lidl GB, said: “The early response from the initial phase of Lidl & Go has been really encouraging. Customers are telling us they value the control and visibility it gives them over their spend, and the flexibility to shop at their own pace. This next wave of stores brings the feature to many more customers, and we’ll continue to take on board feedback to evolve the offering as we go.”
The initiative forms part of Lidl GB's increased investment in digital innovation that also includes personalised coupons on the Lidl Plus app, alongside the introduction of Lidl Points in May which aims to provide a flexible rewards system.
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Physical stores will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

Clément Marchal ends ten year run at Sephora and starts a new chapter as Head of AI Solutions at LVMH
LVMH has appointed Clément Marchal as Head of AI Solutions. He joins from Sephora, part of the LVMH Group, where he served as Data Science & Artificial Intelligence Director. In a LinkedIn post, he said: “After ten wonderful years at Sephora, I’m very happy to share that I have started a new chapter as Head of AI Solutions at the LVMH AI Factory.”
He added: “This role continues my AI journey within the group, with a clear focus: supporting our Maisons in turning AI opportunities into impactful solutions that drive business value. A sincere thank you to the Sephora teams for ten years of trust, collaboration, and shared achievements. Thank you as well to the LVMH AI Factory team for the warm welcome, and to Gonzague de Pirey (Chief Omnichannel and Data Officer) and Martin Schoeller (Director LVMH AI Factory) for their trust as I begin this new chapter. Looking forward to what we will build together.”
TikTok Shop
Sephora recently announced its debut on TikTok Shop. Piloting in the United States from 19th September, its Drop Shop experience will feature exclusive monthly drops, showcasing curated products from some of Sephora's most popular partner brands. Each featured brand will have a dedicated moment to bring its products to life, tell its story and connect with new audiences.
Each drop will include teasers, interactive experiences, and creator led content, encouraging consumers to guess the brand in the spotlight. The experience will culminate in an official TikTok LIVE with a celebrity host, brand founders, and creators to unveil the featured products, answer audience questions, engage with viewers in real-time, and showcase products available for purchase on TikTok Shop during the LIVE.
“Beauty discovery has always been core to Sephora’s ethos, and the rise of social commerce and digital marketplaces have reinforced the need to evolve how we engage with our beauty lovers. We already have an incredibly active beauty community on TikTok, so we are excited to take the next step and pilot the Sephora Drop Shop on TikTok Shop. This platform gives us a new way to interact with our existing customers, while extending our reach to a highly immersed beauty audience. Importantly, the launch signifies a natural progression in how we continue to lead and innovate in beauty retail,” said Artemis Patrick, President and CEO at Sephora North America.
Products featured in each monthly drop will launch exclusively through Sephora's TikTok Shop, with select items later rolling out to Sephora.com, in selected Sephora stores or through other retail partners. During the exclusive launch window, customers will still be able to preview the products on the Sephora site ahead of their wider availability.
“TikTok Shop is a powerful extension of our global digital strategy and our commitment to meeting clients wherever they discover beauty. By approaching this launch with a test and learn mindset, we are not only scaling our retailtainment model in the US, but also gathering critical insights to inform our digital innovation and future roll-out across our global network,” said Anca Marola, Global Chief Digital Officer at Sephora.
“We’re thrilled to welcome Sephora to TikTok Shop. This launch brings together Sephora’s leadership in beauty discovery and curation with TikTok Shop’s unique ability to inspire and connect communities through entertainment, creators, culture and commerce. Together, we’re creating a new, more engaging journey from discovery to purchase, by reimagining how beauty lovers experience and shop their favourite brands," commented Bianca Sing, Global Head of Strategic Brand Partnerships at TikTok Shop.
