items.body:
JD Sports makes RFID progress and Amazon tops GenAI research: the retail technology week in numbers
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail technology news? Then this is the article for you. Including Fanatics, Gander, HyperFinity, Presto, Jo Malone London, Aldi UK, Deliveroo, H&M, Voyado, Destro AI, Temu, and Walmart.
3...The National Football League and Fanatics, the league's official retail partner, are set to open an NFL Shop pop-up retail store on London's Oxford Street, as American football returns to the capital for three games this October.
Located at 360-366 Oxford Street, the 1,000 sq ft store will be open from Thursday, 1st October, to Monday, 19th October, spanning all three 2026 NFL London games: the Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders on 4th October and the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars on 11th October, both at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, followed by the Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on 18th October.
Fans can shop official NFL jerseys and an assortment of merchandise across NFL teams, alongside a range of products available exclusively in London. The Oxford Street store will also host NFL Shop LIVE!, a programme of fan events. On opening night, Thursday, 1st October, NFL UK legend Efe Obada will sit down with broadcaster Neil Reynolds to talk about his NFL career and new charity project. On Thursday, 8th October, Phoebe Schecter and Neil Reynolds will record an NFL London Games special of "Inside the Huddle" in front of a live audience. Both events start at 6 p.m., with limited seating available on a first come, first served basis.
The store at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will also become an official NFL Shop from Saturday, 3rd October to Sunday, 11th October, across both Tottenham games, with a number of exclusive collections available in-store. It opens with an NFL Shop Tottenham Family Day on Saturday, 3rd October, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., with games, prizes, exclusive merchandise and special guests.
$8 million...Destro AI, which is building a shared intelligence layer for warehouse robotics, has raised $8 million in seed funding co-led by Base10 Partners and Bonfire Ventures, with participation from CoFound Partners. The funding will accelerate deployment of Destro’s platform across enterprise warehouses and expand the company’s engineering and research teams.
“Everyone is building capable robots,” says Manthan Pawar, Founder and CEO at Destro AI. “We believe the next breakthrough won’t come from another robot. It will come from the intelligence layer that enables any robot to work together. Customers aren’t buying robots; they’re investing in throughput, reliability, and business outcomes. That’s what we’re building.”
Destro has built two complementary AI systems: MothershipOS and Vision OS. MothershipOS is pitched as the shared mind outside the robot body, intelligently deciding which robot should perform which task, where, when, and how, to optimise complex warehouse workflows. VisionOS is an on-robot intelligence platform that enables complex mobile manipulation using AI models trained from human demonstrations, allowing robots to better perceive, grasp, and interact with real-world environments.
92%...Independent retailer Dike & Son Superstore says it has achieved a 92% sell-through rate on reduced products, according to its latest weekly September figures. That is up from around 73% when it joined Gander in February 2026.
The increase of around 19 percentage points follows improvements to the way the store manages reductions, alongside promotion of Gander through its Facebook page. In the latest reporting week, Dike & Son sold 1,200 of the 1,310 products it reduced.
Adam Vincent, Company Director at Dike & Son, says: “Our team has worked hard to make reductions a consistent part of how we operate and we have also used Facebook to let customers know they can find great value through Gander. Seeing our sell-through rise from around 73% in February to 92% in our latest weekly figures is a fantastic result. It shows what our colleagues can achieve when the right technology is backed by good processes in-store.”
1,000, 14, 2,700, 4,800 and 192...Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, has taken to social media to provide an update on the retailer’s RFID programme, which involves various countries and thousands of stores.
In a LinkedIn post, McGrath said: “This week, our final country goes live with RFID, Germany. And with that, everything we directly control will be live for phase one of our RFID programme. When I look back at what we’ve achieved, the numbers are pretty incredible: 1,000 stores directly launched in 14 months. And across the wider global group, working alongside our counterparts around the world: 2,700 stores live out of 4,800 in that same period, 192 stores a month!”
He added: “But the numbers only tell part of this story. RFID isn’t just about scanners, tags and technology. It’s about changing behaviours, processes and mindsets. We’ve done things that were uncomfortable. Challenged established ways of working. Asked people to rethink processes they’d used for years. And, most importantly, brought people with us on the journey. And we haven't done that alone.”
$10 million...Presto Phoenix, a specialist in voice AI for quick service restaurants (QSRs), has raised $10 million in funding from Remus Capital affiliated investors and other existing backers. The cash will be used to enable it to expand its deployments and technology.
“Over the past several months, we’ve continued to prove that voice AI can deliver meaningful results at scale across some of the most demanding drive-thru environments and menus,” says Krishna Gupta, Co-founder and CEO at Presto. “We are investing heavily in product and operations as we help more of the industry adapt to the inevitable agentic future. Every QSR brand is realising they must increase digitalisation and standardisation across their business, and Presto is the natural partner to help them do that for their largest channel - it all starts with Voice. I’m thankful to our investors for having backed us throughout.”
“We are pleased to see Presto’s progress and are fully supportive of the company and its leadership. AI is digitalising the world, and we are now seeing clear tailwinds for QSR adoption to accelerate: the labor environment, the need to standardize best practices, and the realisation that without the data there is no way to keep up with agentic leaders,” says John Tincoff from Remus Capital.
19.3%...Amazon is the most visible major online marketplace across leading generative AI platforms, according to new analysis from Onclusive examining how e-commerce brands appear in responses generated by ChatGPT and Perplexity. The study found that Amazon accounted for 19.3% of marketplace share of voice, ahead of Walmart at 14%, Alibaba at 12.6%, Shopify at 11.6% and eBay at 11.1%.
Temu recorded a share of voice of 9.7%, followed by MercadoLibre at 9.2% and Etsy at 8.2%. European marketplaces Zalando and CDiscount recorded 3.9% and 0.5% respectively.
The findings highlight significant differences in how frequently major e-commerce platforms are surfaced by generative AI tools, as consumers increasingly use AI engines to research brands, products and online shopping options. Newer platforms are already competing for AI visibility against more established players, Temu’s 9.7% share of voice is comparable to Shopify and eBay.
80% and 30%...H&M has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” says Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, says: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”
1...Victoria Square, a retail and leisure destination in Belfast, reports that Jo Malone London will be opening its first standalone location at the centre, representing the brand’s only dedicated store in Northern Ireland.
It will take 3,402 sq ft, and will offer its signature range of luxury fragrances, home scents, candles, bath and body essentials, and gifts. The new space is due to open on 1st December.
Julie King, Senior Asset Manager at Commerz Real, comments: “2026 has been a phenomenal year for us, and welcoming Jo Malone London’s first standalone store in Northern Ireland is a fantastic endorsement of the confidence leading brands have in the destination."
"Victoria Square continues to outperform the wider market because of the quality and diversity of our retail offer, the strength of our catchment, and importantly, our ability to provide brands with the right platform to succeed. We are the place to be for leading retailers looking to make a real impact in Northern Ireland, and Jo Malone London will be a great addition.”
8...From October, Aldi UK will be trialling a new partnership with Deliveroo across eight UK stores, giving customers access to its full grocery range through the on demand delivery firm’s app. Modelled on Aldi’s partnerships with DoorDash, Deliveroo’s parent company, in the United States and Australia, the latter’s riders will pick, pack and deliver orders directly from stores.
The trial is pitched as the only rapid delivery service available from a discount supermarket in the UK.
Customers will be able to order around 2,000 Aldi products, including fresh fruit and vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, household essentials and Specialbuys. They can order on-demand or choose a delivery window that suits them. A nationwide launch is currently planned for early 2027.
1 and 25…PrettyLittleThing has launched its first ever officially licensed NFL collection, as the Debenhams Group owned fashion retailer expands into sports licensing ahead of this weekend’s 2026 NFL London Games. The 25-piece collection has been designed in-house by PrettyLittleThing and spans apparel and accessories.
A PrettyLittleThing spokesperson says: “We are delighted to collaborate with the NFL on our official licensed product range. Our 25-piece collection was designed in-house and highlights the dynamic intersection between female fashion and sport fandom.”
“The timeless style and prestige of the NFL comes to life in this collaboration with PrettyLittleThing,” adds Salha Latif, Vice President, International Consumer Products and Licensing. “The range of apparel on offer celebrates what makes the NFL so distinctive, providing clothing for all fans in all settings, perfect timing ahead of the 2026 NFL London Games kicking off this weekend.”
51%...New research from HyperFinity reveals the extent to which UK adults believe bias exists in AI. It found that 18-24 year olds are twice as likely to report feeling ‘misunderstood, overlooked, or stereotyped’ by AI, compared with just 26% of those aged 55-65.
A survey of 2,000 UK adults shows that 51% believe gender bias exists today. Among 18-24 year olds, that figure rises to 70% - almost double the 37% recorded among those aged 55-65. With 72% of UK adults now using aItool daily or more, the findings show a marked generational divide in perceptions of AI, with younger adults more likely to identify bias and report experiencing its effects personally. This is also the demographic using AI most frequently.
The research reveals striking differences in how people perceive specific AI tools. 35% of UK adults associate ChatGPT with a male gender, while 46% describe Siri as female and 23% see it as gender neutral. This suggests people are forming different gendered perceptions of these tools, despite them having no obvious gender of their own.
These associations extend to how people describe the tools themselves. ChatGPT is described as an ‘advisor’ or ‘expert’ by 31% of UK adults, while Siri is more than three times as likely to be described as an ‘assistant’ than an ‘advisor’. Most strikingly, 10% of UK adults describe Alexa - the most female associated AI tool in the research, with 69% describing it as female - as a ‘servant’, compared to just 2.5% for ChatGPT.

Retail technology innovation of the week: H&M enlists Voyado to rework onsite search across markets
Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers. Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report judging panel, building up to the publication of the 2026 report later this year.
And this week we’re focusing on H&M which has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” says Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, says: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”
And honourable mentions this week to...
Tote
Tote AI has launched HQ Genie AI, with the aim of bringing a ChatGPT/Claude like experience to retail operations. It says that, instead of digging through dashboards and static reports, operators can ask questions of their live business data and get answers in seconds, with the system beginning to move beyond answering questions to monitoring operations and taking action.
This is in production with Loop Markets, Huck’s and Spinx.
Users can type questions such as what the latest discount on Diet Soda is, how many Monster Energy drinks a given store has left, what daily sales looked like over the last ten days, or the status of a specific card refund. As Tote runs the Point of Sale, HQ Genie draws on operational data from across the store, including the devices connected through Tote Device Cloud, which lets corporate help desk teams use it to spot and diagnose problems. For example, a help desk analyst can ask which devices across the chain need attention and see where issues are occurring, store by store.
Agentic workflows, now in beta, are built into HQ Genie and work to automate recurring tasks.
Hozelock
Polytag has partnered with Hozelock, a manufacturer of garden watering and outdoor products, to introduce smart QR codes across its garden product range. The deployment brings connected product experiences to the garden and outdoor sector for the first time.
By scanning the codes, Hozelock customers can access product specific guidance, including how to guides and videos, while the company gains new insight into how and where its products are being used.
The smart QR codes, powered by Polytag's platform, have been added to Hozelock products available through retailers including B&Q. When scanned, the codes can direct consumers to content tailored to their market and device language, enabling Hozelock to provide relevant information across its international markets using a single QR code.
This is particularly valuable for Hozelock's range of technical and higher value garden products, where packaging alone cannot always display the level of information customers may need. The digital connection also provides a foundation for future product level information requirements, including Digital Product Passports, allowing Hozelock to build on the infrastructure already in place as these requirements are rolled out.
The deployment also gives Hozelock visibility beyond the point of purchase. Through the Polytag platform, the company can see where and when customers are engaging with its products, providing data that was previously unavailable once a product had left the retailer.

items.body:
Retail tech stacks that include SMS and conversational messaging
The payment went through, the stock count updated, and the customer got a message saying their order was being prepared. So far, the retail tech stack has done its job. But then the customer texts back: “Can my sister pick it up for me?”
That question is quite simple. However, someone needs to receive it, find the order, and explain what the person picking it up should do. Retailers build their stacks around selling products and managing orders. SMS and conversational messaging tools can help the team handle the questions that follow.
What Belongs in a Typical Retail Tech Stack?
Retailers usually build their setup to cover one need at a time. They have to take payments, so they choose a PoS system. Online sales follow, then tools to manage stock and keep track of customers. As the business grows, the stack covers these functions:
- PoS and e-commerce
Handle in-store and online purchases, including checkouts and payments.
- Inventory and order management
Track what’s available and manage orders through fulfilment, collection, and returns.
- CRM and loyalty
Keep customer details, purchase histories, and rewards available for the team.
- Marketing, support, and analytics
Run campaigns, handle enquiries, and show how the business performs.
A single platform can cover several of these functions, so you should always check what’s already available before buying another tool.
Messaging belongs with these tools. With Clerk Chat, you can send personalised SMS campaigns and set up automatic follow-ups. Before choosing a platform, however, try the customer’s side of the conversation. Reply to a message from the shop and see where your answer ends up. Does an employee notice it in the middle of their usual work? Can they answer from the same place? Include that daily flow to see if the tool suits your shop.
Make All Tools Work Together
The real test of a retail tech stack comes when a purchase involves more than a single system. A customer buys the last pair of sneakers online and chooses to collect their package at the store. The website accepts the payment, but the shop floor team has to know that the pair is reserved. If the stock record doesn’t update, someone could sell it over the counter before the online order is picked.
Connections between tools deserve as much attention as their individual features. Sales should update inventory. Order details should reach the team preparing the purchase. Finally, customer records should reflect what was bought.
Messaging fits right in. A confirmed payment tells the customer they successfully bought the product. A separate collection message should follow as soon as an employee picks the items and sets them aside.
When reviewing the stack, follow one purchase across the systems. Did someone have to copy details or tell a colleague what happened? Those are real gaps that give you a starting point for improvement.
Get Real Use Out of Your Tools
It’s easy to book another software demo, but don’t do it unless there’s real need. Spend some time with the people processing orders. If they keep a spreadsheet outside the main system, it tells you a lot. Maybe it lists stock transfers that the software makes difficult to track, or maybe there are returns that still need approval. Find out why the extra work happens in the first place.
Sometimes the feature is already there, but nobody uses it. In other cases, the business outgrew the platform’s capacity. Those situations call for different decisions.
If you do take the demo, bring a real task into it. Ask the supplier to show how an employee would find an online purchase and process an exchange in-store. Then ask what you would pay for that setup, including extra user accounts and training.
Test How the System Handles Changes and Returns
Try a cancelled order and a partial return, since they tell loads about your stack’s efficiency. Check the updates in stock and payment records. Do they change properly?
Failed connections deserve special attention. If an update doesn’t reach another system, someone should be alerted and find a way to resolve it. Otherwise, the employees will keep working with information that’s not current, but looks that way to them.
Once the stack is running, track a few useful measures:
- Stock discrepancies
- Order preparation time
- The time it takes for customer enquiries to resolve
These things tell you whether your tools are reducing work or moving it to another place.
There’s Always Room for Growth
Start with the functions your business needs today. Check how the current setup can accommodate higher order volume or even another store. SMS and conversational messaging should grow inside these operations, with your staff able to follow each purchase and the conversations around it.
Whenever something changes, give the setup another evaluation. Maybe you added another delivery option or you’re handling a busier sales season. Check how things are going, since a process that worked for 20 orders a day can get stuck at 200. Ask your employees where the work is building up, so you can decide how to adjust the current tools or add something new.

items.title: How to audit floor safety technology in high traffic stores
items.summary: Your store can run sensors and inspection software and still be unable to show who received the entrance spill alert, or what that person did once it hit their phone during the busiest shift of the week. A floor safety tech audit follows one hazard event from detection to a named response and retained evidence. A slip-and-fall attorney may later use that trail to determine what the store knew and how it responded. Run every test in a way that keeps customers out of harm's way. Step 1: Map the store’s actual hazard zones Let traffic and recurring conditions shape the map. Walk the store itself. Don't work from a template. Start with entrances and flooring transitions, then add refrigerated-case leaks and pickup-area obstructions that appear and vanish by the hour. Every zone needs a system and an owner. Next to the responsible role and backup responder, write down how the zone gets detected and how often it gets inspected. Flag any zone that leans on informal observation alone. Arbill,
items.body:
How to audit floor safety technology in high traffic stores
Your store can run sensors and inspection software and still be unable to show who received the entrance spill alert, or what that person did once it hit their phone during the busiest shift of the week. A floor safety tech audit follows one hazard event from detection to a named response and retained evidence.
A slip-and-fall attorney may later use that trail to determine what the store knew and how it responded. Run every test in a way that keeps customers out of harm's way.
Step 1: Map the store’s actual hazard zones
Let traffic and recurring conditions shape the map. Walk the store itself. Don't work from a template. Start with entrances and flooring transitions, then add refrigerated-case leaks and pickup-area obstructions that appear and vanish by the hour.
Every zone needs a system and an owner. Next to the responsible role and backup responder, write down how the zone gets detected and how often it gets inspected. Flag any zone that leans on informal observation alone.
Arbill, citing CDC and Bureau of Labour Statistics material, attributes more than 60% of same-level fall injuries to the services, wholesale, and retail trade industries.
Those injuries become claims. When one does, a slip and fall lawyer handling a Florida or New York case will look for alert history and inspection records showing when the store knew about the hazard. Every step below builds that record.
Step 2: Inventory devices and applications with their clocks
Record each component’s operational state. One inventory has to cover the full stack: hazard sensors, inspection apps, cameras, and the alert platforms behind them. For each item, log its location, device identifier, and software version. Note the network dependency and the last time data synchronized successfully.
Trace the handoffs between systems. Send a test alert through each platform handoff, then safely disconnect a test connection and keep the failure logs.
Establish one time reference. Synchronize every clock against an approved time source. Write down time zones and daylight-saving settings so footage, alerts, and inspections line up when you match them.
Step 3: Set triggers that match store conditions
Define when the system should act. Scheduled triggers prompt inspections at set times, including opening and closing. Event triggers react to sensor readings or equipment alarms. When the weather turns wet, add scheduled checks.
Test for alert fatigue. People stop reading repeated warnings. Look for duplicate alerts and thresholds set so sensitively they trip on nearly any reading. Cut recipients who have gone inactive. Every store hazard alert should spell out an action, such as inspecting a self-checkout spill.
Step 4: Test routing and escalation under realistic conditions
Send the first alert to a named role. Make sure that person is at work, trained, and carrying a working device. Then withhold acknowledgment: leave the test alert hanging and verify it escalates to a second responsible person within the configured period.
Run a shift-change test. Trigger an alert mid-handover and confirm ownership changes without losing task visibility or history. Push it one step further: rerun the test with an absent recipient or a device left charging, and keep the backup recipient’s acknowledgment.
Retail TouchPoints covered QBE North America’s claims data from 2019 through 2022, which attributed 32% of midsize retailers’ insured losses to third-party slip, trip, and fall injuries.
Step 5: Reproduce silent and intermittent failures
Test devices without a connection. Complete a digital safety inspection offline, check local storage, then reconnect and verify the upload preserves both the event time and the synchronisation time.
Investigate missing tasks and conflicting records.
- Confirm the employee’s assigned store and shift.
- Check the connection and local queue of unsent records.
- Compare creation and acknowledgment times with the completion time.
- Review system handoff errors before recreating or closing tasks.
Do not silently recreate missing records. Keep the error record; a quiet recreation conceals the original failure.
Step 6: Review the evidence with a slip and fall attorney after an actual injury
Preserve the original records. Follow your approved incident and evidence preservation procedures. Put the relevant footage window and the floor inspection records under hold, unaltered. Alert histories and system access logs go in too.
Explain gaps; never fill them silently. Document missing footage or clock discrepancies, name the affected system, and describe your investigation steps. Do not backdate an entry or pass off an estimated time as precise.
If the injury becomes a claim, both sides examine that record. Comparative negligence rules can weigh the injured person’s own share of fault, and a documented response history is the store’s strongest material on that point.
The Evidentiary Challenges in Premises Liability Claims
Slip and fall lawsuits often stall when missing evidence fails to clarify how long a dangerous condition existed, who knew about the spill or obstacle, or whether management acted promptly. In discovery, your lawyer reviews the facility's digital and physical records, matching automated alerts, floor inspection sweeps, camera footage, and employee statements to the exact time of the fall. This timeline reveals whether store management failed to uphold its legal duty to maintain a safe environment.
When should I call a slip and fall lawyer?
Consider calling promptly after an injury if you need legal advice, because footage and other records may be overwritten under routine retention schedules. A lawyer can request preservation and explain the deadlines and legal standards that apply in the relevant jurisdiction.
How to choose a slip and fall lawyer
Focus on hiring an attorney with specific premises liability experience and a firm strategy for securing digital records, such as store audit logs and security camera footage. You should also discuss legal fees directly during your consultation. Personal injury firms generally handle claims on a contingency basis, collecting no legal fees unless they secure a recovery, though exact fee percentages, out-of-pocket litigation expenses, and repayment conditions vary by retainer agreement.
Step 7: Require proof that every alert produced a response
Define the audit trail. Connect the event and its location to the recipient’s acknowledgment. Document the action and closure, plus any reassignment or escalation history.
For a service-counter leak, that means cleanup evidence and a recorded floor check before closure.
Sample records; do not trust a dashboard total. Pull samples from different stores and shifts, including devices tested offline. Open the underlying records and match dashboard statuses against timestamps and user activity. Fail any delivered alert that lacks evidence of a completed response.
No response record, no pass.
Make the audit repeatable
Retain the test plan and its failed scenarios, along with corrective actions and follow-up results, under approved policies. Assign an owner and a retest deadline to every unresolved defect. Repeat affected tests after software updates or staffing changes, and link the earlier failure to its successful retest. Every sampled event should end with a name attached and a record you can pull.

items.title: Ivy Collection customers face rush to spend points as restaurant cancels loyalty scheme
items.summary: Diners signed up to Ivy Premier Rewards received an email on Tuesday, 29 September saying that they could no longer earn points.
items.body:
Ivy Collection customers face rush to spend points as restaurant cancels loyalty scheme
Customers of upscale restaurant chain The Ivy Collection have a limited period to spend years worth of cashback after it closed its points scheme.
Diners signed up to Ivy Premier Rewards received an email on Tuesday, September 29 saying that they could no longer earn points.
It previously offered a generous deal where members could earn 5 per cent cashback on their bill at Ivy restaurants, to be spent on future meals.
The email said they would have until October 29 to redeem any existing points, after which any unused ones would expire.
The Ivy said it was 'working on a new loyalty programme' but gave no further details.
A spokesman said: 'Our guest services team has actively been contacting members with higher balances directly to confirm they have until December 30 2026 to redeem their full value across our restaurants and to assist with table bookings to ensure every earned point is enjoyed.'
Loyalty loss: The Ivy Collection emailed customers to say their Ivy Premier Rewards points would expire at the end of this month. The original Ivy in Covent Garden is pictured here
A couple who are This is Money readers and Ivy regulars got in touch to say that they had 6,867 points on their account, worth £342.
They said they would struggle to spend such a large amount in one month and had made a complaint to the restaurant chain.
The typical main course at the Ivy's locations in London costs between £20 and £45, with starters and desserts between £10 and £15.
It extended the time they had to spend their points until December 30.
It said it would be contacting other customers with large balances to offer them an extension.
A spokesman said: 'We are immensely grateful to our guests who have participated in Ivy Premier Rewards and for the loyalty they have shown us.
'As we prepare to unveil an elevated, newly designed guest recognition programme for the new year, we want to ensure members have ample opportunity to enjoy the rewards they have earned.
'While smaller, immediate-use balances remain redeemable over the standard notice period, we recognise that guests with higher accumulated rewards may require more time.'
Founded in 1917 in London's Covent Garden, the original Ivy restaurant is well known as a celebrity haunt having hosted Winston Churchill, Laurence Olivier and Madonna over the years.
It opened its first spin-off location in 2014 and has since expanded across the country with more than 40 restaurants including in locations such as Birmingham, York and Edinburgh.
It has also opened under names such as Ivy Asia, Ivy Brasserie and Ivy Cafe.
The points programme is run via the restaurant chain's Ivy Club app.
It was launched three years ago, meaning regular customers have had time to build up substantial balances.
Singer Rod Stewart promoted the app at its launch in October 2023, as his whisky brand Wolfie's is stocked at Ivy restaurants.
As well as the cashback, other perks offered to app members included priority reservations, free dishes on their birthday and access to the Ivy Club, the members' club above the original Ivy restaurant in Covent Garden, once per year.
The Ivy chain was previously owned by British business leader and 'King of Mayfair' Richard Caring via his company Caprice Holdings.
He sold his stake in his hospitality empire to Abu Dhabi-based DIAFA for £1.4billion in April this year, in one of the biggest deals in restaurant history, but remains as executive chairman of Caprice.

items.title: Candy Realms refreshes sugar bag range
items.summary: World of Sweets has given its Candy Realms sugar confectionery range a refreshed pack design, new flavour-led varieties and a clear value proposition for convenience and independent retailers. The updated range has been developed to help retailers offer shoppers affordable, colourful and easy-to-shop treats across… This story continues at Candy Realms refreshes sugar bag range Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The updated range has been developed to help retailers offer shoppers affordable, colourful and easy-to-shop treats across a broad choice of popular sugar confectionery.
Candy Realms is available in both £1 PMP formats, giving shoppers clear price visibility at fixture, and non-PMP formats for retailers looking for greater pricing flexibility. The range includes £1 PMP bags at 160g and non-PMP bags at higher weights up to 190g. It also includes a large choice of Vegan bags including Sour Dummies, Fizzy Strawberries and Peach Rings.
The range is also home to one of World of Sweets’ best-selling products, Candy Realms Candy Watches & Necklaces.
The new-look packaging has been created to make the range work harder on shelf. Brighter colours, bolder flavour cues, larger product windows and a more consistent brand identity across the fixture to give Candy Realms greater stand-out, while helping shoppers quickly identify the product and value.
With clear product visibility and improved pack hierarchy, the updated range is designed to support impulse purchase and make shopper decision-making easier in busy confectionery fixtures.
To further refresh the fixture, World of Sweets is adding new Candy Realms varieties, including Pineapple Mix, featuring pineapple rings and fizzy pineapple pieces, and Jelly Faves, a mix of popular jelly sweets including twin cherries, cola bottles and friendship rings.
The wider Candy Realms range includes sour, fizzy, fruity and jelly options, giving retailers a broad and simple sugar bag offer that covers key shopper preferences while maintaining a strong value message.
Nat Panter, brand manager at World of Sweets, said: “Candy Realms has been developed to give retailers a commercial sugar bag range that delivers on value, variety and shelf impact.
“The range gives retailers the flexibility of both £1 PMP bags at 160g and non-PMP bags at higher weights up to 190g. That means retailers can offer clear price reassurance for shoppers through PMP packs, while also having larger non-PMP options where they want more flexibility.
“The redesign is a major step forward for the brand. The packs are brighter, clearer and more consistent, with stronger flavour cues and larger product windows to help the range stand out in busy confectionery fixtures. Combined with new varieties, Candy Realms gives retailers a simple way to refresh their sugar bag offer and drive impulse sales.”
The refreshed Candy Realms range is available through World of Sweets and Hancocks, with new varieties rolling out soon.

items.title: One year to go | Suntory Beverage & Food GB&I comments on DRS preparation
items.summary: Today marks one year to go until the launch of the UK’s Deposit Return Scheme and Suntory Beverage & Food GB&I has commented on the work needed over the next 12 months to ensure the scheme is simple and convenient for consumers from day one.… This story continues at One year to go | Suntory Beverage & Food GB&I comments on DRS preparation Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
SBF GB&I, the producer of Lucozade and Ribena, has long advocated for DRS and is preparing its business and brands for its introduction.
Chief executive Elise Seibold believes the coming year will require close collaboration between producers, retailers, government and scheme administrator Exchange for Change to get return points ready, communicate clearly with consumers and remove unnecessary friction.
“With one year to go, the priority is making the UK’s Deposit Return Scheme a simple, convenient experience for consumers from day one,” she said.
“With considerable investment, over the next 12 months, producers and retailers will work with government and Exchange for Change to get return points ready, communicate clearly with consumers and remove unnecessary friction. Experience from established schemes shows what is possible when consumers understand the system and returning a container is easy.
“We have long been advocates for DRS and we are preparing our business and our brands for its introduction. Getting the launch right means the UK will have a scheme that consumers trust, which supports higher recycling rates and shapes a more circular economy for our drinks containers.”

items.title: UK-first pink trolleys roll into Asda stores for Breast Cancer Awareness Month
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Asda has mapped out the regions with the highest rates of non-chest checking, known as ‘checking deserts’, for a UK-first initiative putting 500 pink trolleys in 10 stores across these […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
New research, released today by Asda, finds a third (33%) of the nation admit to having never checked their chests, or having a checking routine. Asda has mapped out the regions with the highest rates of non-chest checking, known as ‘checking deserts’, for a UK-first initiative putting 500 pink trolleys in 10 stores across these regions to increase awareness and stop shoppers in their tracks.
The research found people in the West Midlands (39%) were most likely to say they don’t check regularly, followed by Wales (38%), Scotland (37%), the East Midlands (36%), London (35%) and Yorkshire (31%).
Breast checking awareness remains important nationwide, with 47% of those surveyed keen to keep a closer eye on their own health and 36% wanting to be more aware of potential signs and symptoms. Yet 15% aren’t confident they would know what to do.
The new pink trollies contain chest checking posters as well as a QR code taking shoppers to chest checking guidance and signs and symptoms of breast cancer by charity partners Breast Cancer Now and CoppaFeel!.
The QR code on the trolley handles also takes shoppers straight to Asda’s Pledge-o-Meter; a live tracker of people pledging to check their chests regularly. Taking just seconds, shoppers are encouraged to pledge to check, share it with their friends and family, and choose to make a small donation to Asda Tickled Pink at the same time. Link to the Tickled Pink pledge page can be found here.
The pink trolleys are not the only way that Asda Tickled Pink is encouraging people to check their chests. Tickled Pink products are available across Asda stores this October displaying chest checking messaging, as well as around 900 million till receipts printed by Asda over the course of the year.
“Our Tickled Pink campaign has raised over £100 million in the last 30 years. We are driving awareness of breast cancer and early detection by encouraging everyone to check their chest. Together, we’re putting breast cancer awareness on everyone’s list” says Emma Betts, Charity Partnerships Manager from Asda. “We’re hoping our customers will embrace our bold new pink trolleys and sign our pledge to help us in our mission to get 1,000,000 more customers checking their chest.”
Carrie Green, associate director, philanthropy and partnerships at Breast Cancer Now, said: “The Tickled Pink partnership has achieved amazing things over the last 30 years, but with a third of Brits admitting they’ve never checked their chest, it’s clear more vital awareness work is needed. It’s fantastic to see Asda turning their trolleys pink and sharing guidance on signs and symptoms, whilst encouraging customers to check themselves regularly. The sooner breast cancer is found, the more likely treatment is to be successful, meaning chest checking can save lives.”
Natalie Haskell, CEO at CoppaFeel! said: “These pink trolleys bring a vital reminder directly into communities where people are least likely to be checking, helping to start conversations and making breast awareness part of everyday life. We’re proud to be a part of Asda Tickled Pink to reach people locally with the confidence to know what’s normal for them and act early if something changes.”
Joanna Orford, 59, from Ruislip Manor, who is supporting this year’s Tickled Pink campaign and featured in the Breast Cancer Awareness Month photoshoot, said: “I’m so excited to be supporting Tickled Pink this year and helping raise awareness. I’m very open about my breast cancer experience and the importance of being chest aware.
“After noticing a change in texture in my breast, I went to an appointment with a consultant at the hospital. I was told I had breast cancer. My first thought was my three daughters. I wanted to be strong for them and minimise the impact it would have on their lives. But as treatment progressed, I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and knew I needed to tell them.
“After a long stint of treatment, including surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, I attended Breast Cancer Now’s Moving Forward course, funded by Asda, and it was a safe space for us to share our experiences.
“Chest awareness was vital to getting the treatment I needed, and I want to share this life-saving message with as many people as possible.”
In the 1990s, 70% of women survived breast cancer for 5 or more years. Thanks to the power of research and advances in how the disease is detected, diagnosed and treated, this number is now nearly 90%. Asda Tickled Pink’s funding has fuelled this progress over the last three decades. In total it has raised over £100 million for world-class research, vital education and life-changing support.
Pink trolleys are being rolled out across selected Asda stores in ‘checking deserts’ throughout October, with stores from Llanelli to Colindale championing Breast Cancer Awareness month. Simply pick up a pink trolley and find out more about how you can begin your checking routine.
For more information, images or to speak to a representative from Asda, Breast Cancer Now, CoppaFeel! or hear from one of Asda’s storytellers contact: lauren.candler@smarts.agency

items.title: Shoppers’ healthier lifestyles influencing drink choices but ‘it’s not game over for alcohol’
items.summary: Drink sales increased by 2.9% across Europe’s six biggest grocery markets last year, as shoppers continued to cut back on alcohol but paid more for a new generation of beverages competing for social occasions and catering to healthier lifestyles. Spending on alcohol fell by 0.8%… This story continues at Shoppers’ healthier lifestyles influencing drink choices but ‘it’s not game over for alcohol’ Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Spending on alcohol fell by 0.8% in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain according to the latest analysis of the FMCG market by Circana, while sales of low- and no-alcohol alternatives grew by 7.3%.
Increased spending on sports, energy and yoghurt-based drinks, as increasingly health-conscious consumers took advantage of a wider range of products, also helped lift non-alcoholic drink sales by 5.4% to €109bn and total beverage sales to €180bn.
Beer, cider, wine and spirits sales were down 0.9%, 1.2%, 1.5% and 2.2% respectively. 43% of shoppers, and half of 25- to 39-year-olds, told Circana they were cutting back on alcohol by buying less, postponing purchases or giving up altogether.
44% said they were buying more bottled water, 31% more juices and smoothies, and 29% more tea and coffee.
Just 15% said they were buying more alcoholic drinks. This is despite heavy discounting, with around 41% of beer and 37% of alcoholic drinks sold on promotion during the year, compared with only 25% of beverages overall.
Speaking following his keynote at the Beverage Forum on 1 October, Ananda Roy, senior vice president of strategic growth insights at Circana, said: “Alcohol has been declining in popularity in the five or six years since the pandemic and this has now led to a wider range of alternatives and healthier products, which give us much more choice about what we drink at home and when we socialise.
“Younger people in particular are drinking much less alcohol and there is no evidence this will change as they get older, as the growing mix of adult soft drinks and lighter alternatives is simply becoming an increasingly normal part of everyday drinking.
“It’s not game over for alcohol manufacturers, but they need to do much more than cut prices and instead look at lighter, lower-sugar and lower-calorie products that can help beer, wine and spirits stay relevant as our drinking habits change.”
Circana also found new beverage products generated an extra €242m in sales last year, including €161m from dairy drinks and €32m each from low- and no-alcohol products and bottled water.
While spending on drinks across Europe rose last year, the amount actually sold increased by just 0.5%, as average price rises of 2.3% also drove much of the sales growth.
UK beverage sales rose by 3.2% to €54bn, accounting for 30% of spending across Europe’s six biggest markets but just 19% of the amount sold.
Some products continued to grow despite higher prices, with the amount of yoghurt-based drinks sold rising by 12.3%, ready-to-drink spirits by 12.9%, and still water and plant-based drinks by 5.2% each.
The picture for the beverage market as a whole improved during the second quarter of 2026, when average prices fell by 0.2% and the amount of beverages sold rose by 1.6%.
Circana’s data found own-label products also now account for 35% of beverage spending, with retailer brands gaining ground in categories including coffee, wine and champagne and dairy drinks.

items.body:
RAW Charging (“RAW”), the leading electric vehicle (EV) chargepoint operator for the hospitality, leisure and retail sectors, is proud to announce a landmark partnership with Sunderland AFC to deliver the largest EV charging hub in the North East as part of the club’s Ready Eco programme.
Highlights
- Largest EV hub in the North East: 20 charging bays (16 x 150kW and 4 x 300kW).
- Powered by 100% renewable energy: reinforcing RAW and SAFC’s commitment to sustainability.
- EcoReady Campaign: Premier League Club becomes one of the most sustainable in the league as part of EcoReady Campaign

Located at the Stadium of Light, the new EV hub will feature 20 ultra rapid charging bays, comprising 16 x 150kW and 4 x 300kW chargers, adding a vital new facility for the community. The hub will ensure a fast, reliable, and efficient charging experience for visitors, fans and the wider community. This initiative is a crucial step in Sunderland AFC’s Ready Eco strategy, which aims to make the club energy-sufficient from renewable sources by 2028 and achieve net zero by 2040.
The hub will be powered by 100% renewable energy, supporting SAFC’s mission to lead on sustainability in sport while aligning with RAW’s commitment to delivering future-proof charging solutions across the UK.
Visitors to Sunderland can take advantage of RAW’s state-of-the-art chargers, which allow for quick battery top-ups in just minutes. The chargers support contactless payments and are compatible with all major EV charging apps. Furthermore, customers can enjoy free charging following the opening of the hub by signing up to RAW Rewards: https://rawcharging.com/rewards. RAW is committed to excellence and has been recognised with the prestigious Zapmap Best Destination Network Award for 2026, as well as the ICC Gold accreditation, cementing RAW’s position as the EV charging partner of choice for the UK’s leading leisure, retail, and hospitality destinations.

The chargers will be branded as part of Ready Eco, further strengthening SAFC’s visibility as a leader in sustainable initiatives.
This partnership marks another major milestone in RAW’s expanding UK-wide network, following recent installations at major leisure and hospitality venues, including Cardigan Fields, Knights Park, XScape Yorkshire and Milton Keynes. By investing in this hub, RAW is making EV charging more accessible, convenient, and reliable for all drivers in the North East.
Jason Simpson, CEO of RAW Charging, said: “We are delighted to be partnering with Sunderland AFC to deliver the largest EV charging hub in the North East. This project is a major new facility for the city and aligns perfectly with our mission to support sustainable travel. By providing ultra-rapid charging powered by 100% renewable energy, we are ensuring that EV drivers have access to reliable and future-proof charging infrastructure.”
Paul Kingsmore, chief operations officer, Sunderland AFC, added: “At Sunderland AFC, we are committed to making a real difference through our Ready Eco programme, and this partnership with RAW Charging is another step towards achieving our sustainability ambitions. items.title: Boots set to be bought by billionaire Canadian family in fresh blow to London stock market
items.summary: The chemist could be sold for around £6.8billion. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said a takeover by the Westons would make it 'unlikely that an IPO of Boots would happen any time soon.'
items.body:
Boots set to be bought by billionaire Canadian family in fresh blow to London stock market
Canada's billionaire Weston family is set to buy Boots, abandoning plans for a stock market listing in a fresh blow to the City.
Sycamore Partners, which bought Boots’ US parent Walgreens Boots Alliance last year, could reach a deal as soon as next week with the former Selfridges owner.
A sale could see the British chemist valued at around £6.8billion, according to a report in The Financial Times, dashing hopes of an initial public offering, although no final decisions have been made.
Boots' return after a 19-year absence from the UK stock market would have provided a much-needed vote of confidence for the City.
In June, Australian pharmacists Sigma Healthcare, who had held 'preliminary discussions' with Boots, pulled out of talks, rekindling hopes of a float.
A takeover by the Westons makes it 'unlikely that an IPO of Boots would happen any time soon,' said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.
British chemist Boots - which began as a family herbal medicine shop in Nottingham in 1849 - could be bought by the Canadian part of the family behind Primark.
He added: ‘This would be a major blow to the London Stock Exchange which has desperately been trying to attract more companies to float in London. Boots is a major name on the high street and exactly the type of brand that could attract retail investors keen to put money into a name they know well.’
The Weston family would want to make the chemist ‘run more efficiently’ and could invest large sums into improving stores, Coatsworth added.
The Westons are best-known in the UK for the Associated British Foods empire, which contains fashion chain Primark, as well as owning department store Fortnum & Mason.
The Canadian side of the family owns the grocery chain Loblaws and pharmacy chain Shoppers Drug Mart through its Wittington Investments holding company. They sold Selfridges for £4billion in 2022.
Buyout group Sycamore Partners broke up Boots’ former owner Walgreens Boots Alliance in August last year after its £7.4billion takeover of the US group, creating the Boots Group in the process.
It includes the chemist’s UK and Irish chains, Boots Opticians and the No7 Beauty Company. Walgreens Boots Alliance boss, Italian billionaire Stefano Pessina, and his wife, Ornella Barra, continue to own a 44 per cent stake in Boots.
Earlier this year, Pessina, who originally brought together Boots and US chemists Walgreens in 2012, said Sycamore ‘will, of course, have to sell [Boots] sooner or later’.
Former Currys boss Alex Baldock took the reins at Boots, which employs 51,000 staff in Britain, bolstering optimism for a float.
Industry experts have said that Boots has become more alluring to potential buyers and investors as it cashes in on strong beauty sales.
Boots last year saw annual sales rise 3.2 per cent to £7.5billion, boosted by strong demand for its beauty products and weight-loss jabs. The business started as a family herbal medicine shop in Nottingham in 1849.

items.body:
From 1 October, Boots will offer NHS flu vaccinations to all eligible adults, including people aged 65 and over and those aged 18 to 64 with certain long-term health conditions, helping more people protect themselves ahead of winter.
Flu can cause severe illness, particularly in vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, older adults, young children, and those with underlying health conditions. Data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) highlights the effectiveness of the seasonal jab, showing that flu vaccinations significantly reduced the risk of hospitalisation by up to 40% in adults aged 65 and over during last year’s.
Claire Nevinson, superintendent pharmacist at Boots, said: “Flu can make people feel very unwell and may pose a serious risk to those considered to be vulnerable. As we head into autumns, it’s a good idea to plan ahead and ensure you have your flu jab as early as possible to help protect yourself and those around you from flu and reduce the risk of passing the virus to others this winter.”
Customers can book an appointment at boots.com or speak with their local Boots pharmacist. Those not eligible for an NHS flu vaccination can book an appointment through the Boots Private Winter Flu Jab service.
To help patients make informed decisions about their seasonal healthcare, Nevinson answers five common questions:
- Does the flu jab give you flu? 
“No, the flu vaccination contains a tiny amount of an inactive flu virus that cannot give you the flu. Some people may experience a temporary raised temperature and aching muscles, and you may feel sore at the injection site, but these side effects tend to be mild and only last for a day or so.”
- When should you get the flu vaccination?
“The best time to have a flu jab to ensure maximum protection is in the autumn months before the virus becomes more prevalent. This allows the body to obtain optimum protection. After you’ve received the jab, it usually takes around 10 to 14 days for optimum protection so it’s best to book your vaccination as early as you can.”
- Do you only need a flu vaccination only once in your life?
“No, protection from the flu vaccination declines with time and the types of flu virus in circulation change so the vaccination is updated each year. This is why it’s important to get the flu vaccination every year.”
- Does the flu vaccination have side effects?
“Yes, like any vaccination, it is normal to experience mild side effects after receiving a flu vaccination. These side effects are a result of your body’s natural immune response as it builds protection against the flu virus. The most common side effects, such as a sore arm, fever or fatigue are generally mild and tend to resolve within one to two days. To help your body recover and ease any discomfort, you can consider taking paracetamol if it’s suitable for you, stay well-hydrated, and ensure you get plenty of rest.”

Ted Baker, the iconic British lifestyle brand celebrated for its distinctive design, character and quintessential British wit, today announced its return to standalone retail in the UK with the opening of Ted Baker Tailored on 2 October.
Located in the heart of London’s financial district, Ted Baker Tailored represents an evolution of the brand’s UK retail presence, building on the menswear heritage on which it was founded.
Rooted in the traditions of British tailoring and reimagined for today, the collection creates complete wardrobes for those who value style and attention to detail. From impeccably cut suiting to elevated everyday essentials, each piece combines timeless quality with contemporary design, crafted with purpose and worn with confidence.
“This opening is an important milestone for Ted Baker in its home market and a reaffirmation of the brand’s British heritage and the enduring relevance of the category where it all began,” said Henry Stupp, president, lifestyle EMEAI at Authentic, the brand’s owner. “We’re building on the qualities that have long distinguished Ted Baker, its approach to tailoring, craftsmanship and distinctly British point of view, while evolving the brand for today’s consumer. London is the natural place to begin, and we see this opening as a defining step in the brand’s next chapter.”
The store brings Ted Baker to life through an immersive retail environment where product, design and storytelling come together. Unexpected details and characterful touches are woven throughout the space, creating a contemporary expression of the wit and personality that have long set Ted Baker apart.
“Having designed and produced Ted Baker suiting for many years, Suit Direct has a deep understanding of the brand and its distinctive approach to British tailoring,” said Tim Murphy, CEO of Suit Direct. “Ted Baker Tailored represents an exciting new chapter in that partnership – bringing together our expertise in craftsmanship, attention to detail and contemporary style in a dedicated retail space. We’re proud to bring this new experience to London and look forward to welcoming customers.”

items.title: Early preparation key to smooth DRS rollout for retailers, says RVM maker
items.summary: With just 12 months to go until the UK’s deposit return scheme (DRS) goes live, the decisions retailers make now will shape how effectively deposit return works for their stores. Tomra, the global reverse vending machine (RVM) manufacturer, says the countdown is on and retailers… This story continues at Early preparation key to smooth DRS rollout for retailers, says RVM maker Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Tomra, the global reverse vending machine (RVM) manufacturer, says the countdown is on and retailers now have an important window to turn their plans into practical next steps.
From 1 October 2027, consumers will pay a refundable deposit when buying eligible single-use drinks containers and receive it back when the empty containers are returned for recycling. Retailers across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland selling drinks included in the scheme will have new responsibilities, including charging a refundable deposit on eligible drinks bottles and cans and operating return points unless an exemption applies.
“The businesses that act now will be best placed for a smooth transition when the scheme comes into effect,” says Sondre Henningsgård, managing director for Tomra Collection UK.
“This is an important opportunity for retailers to become deposit return ready. Over the next year, attention will increasingly turn to the practical aspects of implementation – staff training, customer communications, deciding on return point locations and establishing operational processes.
“Retailers don’t need to have every answer today, but having a clear plan in place will make the transition significantly easier.”
Henningsgård says it’s clear from recent discussions with retailers that many are developing their understanding of the DRS scheme and beginning to plan how it will work for their stores, operations and customers.
“Right now, stores of all sizes are weighing up the right solutions and balancing those with how to make best use of valuable space, estimating what sort of volume their returns will be, deciding between manual and automated take-back and looking at how they integrate these plans with their current operations.
“Retailers need time to assess their options carefully and make the right long-term investment. With one year to go, now is the time to define what success looks like for their business and to start preparing for DRS.
“Retailers should look beyond machine size and upfront price and consider the full operation, including capacity, reliability, customer experience and service support.
“A reverse vending machine will become part of everyday store operations for many years, so retailers are not simply choosing a machine, they are choosing the partner they will rely on to keep deposit return running.”

items.title: What the high street can learn from betting’s digital migration
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Retail boardrooms have spent a decade debating the same question: how many stores do we actually need, and what are they for? While that debate rumbles on, one consumer category has already lived through the entire cycle, from counter service to app-first, and come out the other side with a settled answer. The British betting […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Retail boardrooms have spent a decade debating the same question: how many stores do we actually need, and what are they for? While that debate rumbles on, one consumer category has already lived through the entire cycle, from counter service to app-first, and come out the other side with a settled answer.
The British betting industry digitised earlier, faster and more completely than almost any other high-street business, and the way its operators handled the transition holds practical lessons for retailers weighing their own channel mix.
A sector that digitised first
The numbers tell the story plainly. According to the Gambling Commission’s industry statistics for April 2025 to March 2026, the sector generated £17.5 billion in gross gambling yield, up 4.4% year-on-year. Within that, the remote casino, betting and bingo segment produced £8.3 billion, growing at 6.9%, while all land-based sectors combined managed £4.9 billion and growth of just 1.1 %. Online is now both the larger channel and the source of virtually all the growth.
The physical estate has adjusted accordingly. Great Britain counted 8,423 betting shops in September 2018, on the Commission’s own figures. The latest count is 5,617, down 3.6% in a year and roughly a third in under a decade. Total licensed gambling premises now stand at 8,081. That is not a collapse; it is a managed contraction, and the distinction matters.
The retail parallel
Retail is traveling the same road at a gentler gradient. ONS figures put internet sales at more than a quarter of total UK retail sales, and high-street footfall has continued to fall year on year through 2026, according to BRC-Sensormatic data. The strategic question facing a fashion chain or a grocer in 2026 is the one betting operators faced in the mid-2010s: when the till migrates to the phone, what is the shop for?
The betting industry’s answer was not “nothing”. The operators that navigated the shift best did not simply race to close premises; they rebuilt the estate around a different job description, the same omnichannel logic that retail’s own strategists now advocate: the shop as brand presence, service point and acquisition channel, with the app as the engine of range and revenue.
The operator that kept its shops
A useful case study comes from outside Britain. Hollywoodbets, a South African operator that entered the UK market in 2019 and holds a Gambling Commission license for its British arm, opened its first betting branch in Durban in 2000 and grew into a household name at home through physical shops, around 84 of which still trade across South Africa’s provinces.
What changed is where the growth sits. The company still operates its retail branches, but the engine is now its digital estate, where product ranges, from sports markets to the online slots lobby on its international platform, expand at a pace no counter service could match. A shop has finite counter space and opening hours; a digital lobby adds products the way an e-commerce site adds SKUs. The physical branches did not disappear when that became true. Their role changed: local visibility, cash customers, and a brand anchor in communities where the company built its name.
What transfers to retail
Three lessons from betting’s migration travel well beyond it.
Treat footfall as marketing, not just revenue. Betting shops stopped being judged purely on over-the-counter takings long ago; they earn their keep partly as brand presence. Retailers doing the same arithmetic often find a store’s contribution to local online sales changes the closure calculus.
Let the digital channel carry the range. The physical estate holds the edited, high-conviction offer; the long tail lives online, where shelf space is free. Betting operators learned this early because their product count exploded online while shop counters stayed the same size.
Build the loyalty loop across both. The most valuable customer is the one who uses both channels. McKinsey’s omnichannel research found omnichannel customers purchase up to 70 percent more often than their offline-only peers, which is precisely the behavior a well-run cross-channel estate is designed to produce.
The caveats that keep it honest
Not everything transfers. Betting is a tightly regulated category, and part of its shop decline reflects regulation as much as consumer preference, a pressure most retailers do not face. And the products themselves are not comparable to a basket of groceries: gambling is adult entertainment with real financial risk, which is why its digital growth has been accompanied by ever-stricter player-protection rules rather than pure growth-hacking.
But as a preview of where a channel shift ends up, the sector is hard to beat: a smaller, repurposed physical estate; a digital channel carrying the range and the growth; and the winners being the operators who treated the two as one business rather than rivals. The high street’s future may look more like that than either the doomsayers or the store-forever romantics expect.
Gambling products referenced in this article are for adults aged 18 and over. Anyone concerned about gambling can contact GamCare’s National Gambling Helpline on 0808 8020 133, free and confidential, 24 hours a day.

items.body:
Crafted to deliver a multi-sensorial taste journey, Ferrero Collection Experience brings together four flavours across a single box, each built on a delicate, crispy wafer shell and finished with its own coating and decoration.
The range is now available in Tesco and Sainsbury’s stores, rolling out across further grocery retailers in September.
THE RANGE
Ferrero Collection Experience 20 pieces
Ferrero Collection Experience features a selection of premium, unwrapped chocolate specialities in four flavours – Cappuccino, Cocoa, Hazelnut and Salted Caramel. Combining exciting flavours and contrasting textures, it offers a multi-sensorial taste experience that is perfect for sharing a refined chocolate discovery together.
THE FOUR FLAVOURS
Each box contains 20 chocolates across four flavours:
- Cappuccino – A silky swirl of milky coffee filling enclosed in a delicate, crispy wafer shell and a luscious coating. Each piece elegantly crowned in fine dark chocolate.
- Cocoa – A crispy wafer shell, enrobed in fine dark chocolate, embraces a velvety cocoa filling; artfully crafted into an elegantly adorned chocolate delight.
- Hazelnut – An irresistible chocolate speciality: smooth hazelnut filling lies at the heart of a delicate, crispy wafer shell, all wrapped in fine milk chocolate and crowned with an artful swirl.
- Salted Caramel – A crispy wafer and a rich dark chocolate shell surrounds a smooth, salted caramel flavoured filling, elevated by a delicate decoration on top.
Emma Armer, marketing director at Ferrero UK, said: “Ferrero Collection Experience is the next stage in the journey for the Ferrero Collection brand. We’ve created a refined multilayered taste experience, including our signature wafer combined with a delicious smooth filling. With five well-loved flavours including cappuccino and salted caramel, there is something for everyone to enjoy.”
The 20-piece box is available now, with a larger 35-piece box rolling out for Christmas from September/October, featuring five flavours. The collection is completed with an exclusive Almond variant, featuring a crispy wafer shell enrobed in silky white chocolate, a sumptuous almond filling and elegantly finished with delicate milk chocolate drizzles.

items.title: St Pierre launches Sandwich Roll Duo

St Pierre, one of the UK’s leading premium bakery brands, is expanding into lunchtime occasions with the launch of Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls, two new sandwich carriers designed to help retailers capitalise on changing consumer habits and growing demand for premium lunch solutions. The launch marks St Pierre’s entry into the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
St Pierre, one of the UK’s leading premium bakery brands, is expanding into lunchtime occasions with the launch of Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls, two new sandwich carriers designed to help retailers capitalise on changing consumer habits and growing demand for premium lunch solutions.
The launch marks St Pierre’s entry into the sandwich roll segment and supports the brand’s ambition to broaden usage beyond traditional burger and hot dog occasions. Lunch is already a significant growth opportunity for the brand, with lunch occasions growing 46% year on year, driven by a 42% increase in in-home lunches. Lunch now accounts for 27% of all St Pierre occasion spend.
The opportunity extends beyond the brand itself. Worldpanel data values the UK lunch occasion at £26.4bn, while consumer behaviour continues to evolve. As shoppers move away from traditional sliced bread, one in five lunchtime sandwiches now features an alternative carrier such as a roll or bun, the highest level recorded in five years. Rolls themselves are also at a five-year high in terms of their share of lunch occasions.
Developed specifically to tap into this trend, the new range gives retailers an opportunity to bring greater variety, premiumisation and differentiation into the sandwich fixture while helping shoppers elevate everyday lunches without compromising on convenience.
St Pierre Soft Pretzel Rolls combine the distinctive flavour of a pretzel with a softer texture and the convenience of a pre-sliced format. Made in France, the rolls offer shoppers a simple way to bring something different to lunchtime.
St Pierre Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls pair the brand’s signature soft brioche with aromatic Mediterranean herbs, creating a flavour-led sandwich carrier suitable for a wide variety of hot and cold fillings.
Both products are HFSS compliant, pre-sliced for convenience and available in four-packs. Each roll weighs 67g, with an RRP of £2.50 per pack.
Alison Palmer, head of brand development at St Pierre Groupe, comments: “Lunch represents an exciting growth opportunity for St Pierre and a natural next step in our journey to broaden the occasions where shoppers can enjoy our products.”
“Consumers are increasingly looking beyond traditional sliced bread for formats that offer something a little more interesting, while still being quick and easy to prepare. Our Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls bring premium taste, variety and versatility to the lunchtime occasion, making it easier for shoppers to elevate everyday lunches.”
“For retailers, the launch creates a clear opportunity to drive trade-up, bring greater differentiation and incremental value to the bakery fixture and support category growth, by offering shoppers something genuinely new within a high-value meal occasion.”
St Pierre Soft Pretzel Rolls are available now in 320 Tesco stores, 248 Asda stores and rolling into 320 Sainsbury’s stores from 14 October.
St Pierre Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls launched in 254 Asda stores from 14 September.
Both products have an RRP of £2.50 for a four-pack.

Now in its fourth year, the industry-wide campaign, facilitated by the Fed, will run throughout October, celebrating… This story continues at More than 850 retailers get behind Home News Delivery (HND) Month 2026 Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Now in its fourth year, the industry-wide campaign, facilitated by the Fed, will run throughout October, celebrating the vital community service provided by news retailers and their delivery teams while helping stores attract new customers and grow their home delivery rounds.
A total of 858 retailers have registered for this year’s campaign, with strong support also coming from across the newspaper and magazine industry.
Customers will be able to take advantage of a range of HND subscription offers throughout the month.
These include six issues of the Financial Times for £15; six months half price from Reach, the Daily Mail and i Paper; a seven-day Telegraph print subscription for £78 or weekend subscription for £34.74; and savings of up to 68% on the Guardian and the Observer.
Magazine publishers Frontline and Marketforce are also supporting HND Month, with 12 magazine titles participating, extending the campaign beyond newspapers and giving customers the opportunity to receive their first magazine issue free through HND.
Participating retailers will have plenty of opportunities to benefit too, with more than £10,000 worth of prizes available during October.
At the heart of the activity is the return of the £200 Daily Prize Draw, with one registered retailer selected every day throughout the month.
Winners will be announced at 10am each day on the HND Month website and will have three days to claim their prize. Once verified, winnings will be credited directly through the retailer’s wholesale news account.
Fed national president Hemanshu Patel said the campaign was an opportunity to recognise the work of retailers and delivery teams while encouraging more customers to experience the convenience of having newspapers and magazines delivered directly to their homes.
He said: “HND Month shines a spotlight on the tireless efforts of retailers and delivery teams, and the valuable community service they provide every day. It also presents a great opportunity for retailers to attract new customers and grow their home delivery business.
“Home news delivery remains a vital backbone for many retailers and for the wider industry. The support we’ve received from publishers and wholesalers has been extremely encouraging, demonstrating what can be achieved when we work together for everyone’s benefit.
“To all retailers, thank you for your continued hard work and for participating in HND Month. I wish you every success throughout the campaign and hope you enjoy a very successful month.”
Throughout October, participating retailers are being encouraged to actively promote the customer offers, make the most of the campaign material available and use HND Month as an opportunity to showcase their delivery service to potential new customers.
The Fed is also asking retailers to share photographs of their displays and stories about their delivery rounds so their work can be celebrated throughout the campaign.
Retailers taking part should check the HND Month website every day during October for prize draw winners, competitions, giveaways, campaign updates and retailer stories.
