items.body:
Twinings has launched But First, Tea, a major new long-term brand campaign designed to reposition tea’s role in modern life and make it a more active wellbeing choice.
Built around the instinctive phrase ‘But first, tea’, the campaign celebrates the moments when people choose tea before taking on what comes next. Heroing the breadth of the Twinings range, from infusions such as Sleep, Glow, Digest and Moment of Calm to the brand’s Sparkling Tea collection, the campaign shows how different blends can support different occasions. In doing so, it reframes tea from a passive comfort into a simple active choice that helps people prepare, reset and reconnect throughout the day.
The launch marks the next chapter in Twinings’ brand evolution. The brand is bringing more new buyers into tea than any other brand, has helped rejuvenate the category by recruiting younger consumers and with more under 35s buying Twinings than any other brand.
But First, Tea builds on that momentum, with a strategic ambition to unlock new consumers, create new tea drinking occasions and drive further category growth by making tea – and Twinings – an even more active part of modern wellbeing.
The platform follows Twinings’ summer GenTea campaign, which explored tea’s evolving role among younger consumers, finding that almost half of Gen Z turn to tea rather than alcohol as their new ‘Dutch courage’. But First, Tea takes that insight further, presenting tea as a drink that helps people feel ready for the day, the unexpected and the moments that matter.
One of Twinings’ most significant marketing investments
But First, Tea is supported by one of Twinings’ most significant marketing investments, with launch activity spanning TV, outdoor media, paid social, creator content, retail media and shopper activation. The integrated platform brings one distinctive idea to life across every touchpoint, building recognition and relevance wherever consumers consider reaching for tea.
The media strategy brings the campaign’s central idea – owning ‘the moment before the moment’ – to life by placing Twinings at the start of experiences people look forward to. Activity includes premium BVOD (Broadcaster Video on Demand) around entertainment, drama and sport; host-read integrations on Davina McCall’s Begin Again podcast; and playful out-of-home creative tailored to different moments throughout the day.
The integrated campaign was developed with Starcom as strategic media partner and Leo Burnett leading the final creative execution. Publicis Commerce developed the retail activation strategy, while MHP Group, Splendid Communications and Whalar supported across earned, social and creator activity. System1 provided the testing and insight throughout creative development, providing valuable insights to shape and strengthen its effectiveness.
Bringing the platform into product experience
Twinings also refreshed premium packaging across its Green Tea and Infusions range, introducing individual string and tag teabags with notes inspired by everyday tea rituals. The detail extends the campaign idea into the product experience, connecting the advertising platform with relatable moments when people reach for a cup of tea.
As part of the OOH launch, Twinings will feature real customer stories selected from more than 12,000 submissions on a billboard in London’s White City for a weekend in October. Capturing moments when people turn to tea for comfort, confidence or a pause, the stories bring the But First, Tea platform to life through real experiences. The creative execution was led by Studio La Plage, the production arm of MHP Group.
Gill Close, marketing director at Twinings UK & Ireland, said: “We believe tea has a key role to play in a world where people are looking for simple, positive ways to invest in their wellbeing. At Twinings, we are already bringing new energy to the category, attracting more and younger consumers who are discovering what tea has to offer, and we want to grow the category even further. But First, Tea is about reminding people of the simple difference tea can make and giving them more reasons to choose it throughout their day.”

items.title: ZRO launches the UK’s first connected surplus food system

Rather than navigating multiple specialist providers independently, ZRO connects expertise, infrastructure and commercial routes across the food hierarchy, assessing each surplus stream individually to identify the highest-value viable […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
ZRO, the UKs first connected surplus food system, officially launches today, giving manufacturers, retailers and brand owners a coordinated way to identify better outcomes for surplus food.
Rather than navigating multiple specialist providers independently, ZRO connects expertise, infrastructure and commercial routes across the food hierarchy, assessing each surplus stream individually to identify the highest-value viable outcome.
ZRO is a new proposition, bringing the full range of surplus food routes together through one connected system for the first time. However, the capability behind it is firmly established. Built on decades of SugaRich Group operational experience, ZRO connects specialist businesses already embedded within food manufacturers’ operations and supply chains. In the UK alone, SugaRich Group operations recovered more than 800,000 tonnes of surplus food in 2025 – giving ZRO proven scale, credibility and capability from the outset.
The approach is already delivering measurable results. In a recent pilot project with a leading UK biscuit manufacturer, applying the ZRO approach increased food-to-food outcomes from 0% to more than 30% within ten months, creating more than £156,000 of additional value from 438 tonnes of surplus material.
As businesses face growing pressure to improve resource efficiency, strengthen supply chain resilience and retain more value from food already produced, ZRO provides a practical framework that prioritises keeping food in the human food chain wherever possible.
One system, five pathways
Until now, businesses have often needed to work with multiple providers to explore different options for surplus food. ZRO connects the expertise, infrastructure and specialist capabilities needed to assess each surplus stream and identify the highest-value viable outcome across five pathways:
- Prevent – using SugaTrak data and insight to identify where surplus arises and help reduce it at source.
- Redistribute – directing suitable surplus food to people through Company Shop Group’s redistribution network.
- Reformulate – turning suitable surplus ingredients into new food products through ZRO Group Ltd.’s food-to-food capability.
- Repurpose – converting suitable former foodstuffs into quality-assured animal feed ingredients through SugaRich and AB Nutrition.
- Recover – using Mobius’ total waste management capability to manage remaining materials responsibly and recover value wherever possible.
The value of ZRO lies not in any single pathway, but in connecting them so that each surplus stream can be directed towards the best viable outcome.
From Sweetdreams to ZRO Group Ltd
The launch marks the next stage in the evolution of a Northumberland business with more than 30 years’ experience creating value from surplus confectionery and food ingredients.
Formerly known as confectionery manufacturer Sweetdreams Ltd, the business became ZRO Group Ltd in June 2026, reflecting its broader role as the UK operating business developing and delivering the ZRO system, commercial proposition, partnerships and proof.
In the UK, ZRO draws on specialist capability across the wider SugaRich Group, including SugaRich, Mobius, AB Nutrition and ZRO Group Ltd, alongside trusted external partners where collaboration adds value.
As part of Ravago, this combines the specialist expertise and agility of the SugaRich Group with the scale, infrastructure and international reach of a global organisation operating in more than 60 countries.
Food stays food
At the heart of ZRO is one simple principle: if something was made to be food, its highest value is to stay food.
Matthew Stephenson, managing director, ZRO Group Ltd, said: “For too long, surplus has been approached as something to manage once the original route to market disappears. We see a much bigger opportunity: to retain as much of the value already created in that food as possible.
“Every surplus stream is different, so there shouldn’t be a predetermined answer. The right outcome might be prevention, redistribution, reformulation, repurposing or recovery. What matters is having the expertise and routes available to make that decision intelligently.
“ZRO connects those capabilities through one system. It gives businesses a simpler way to explore better outcomes while keeping food as food wherever it is safe and viable to do so. That is where we believe the next opportunity for the industry lies – not simply managing surplus more efficiently but rethinking what it can still become.”
Company Shop group brings established redistribution expertise to ZRO
Company Shop Group joins ZRO as its founding redistribution partner, providing established expertise, infrastructure and national scale for surplus suitable for redistribution.
Partnering with the UK’s longest-standing surplus redistributor Company Shop Group, the redistribution pathway ensures that food and drink perfectly fit for human consumption can be sold to communities who need it most. Company Shop Group redistribute over 117 million items of surplus each year to their network of Surplus Supermarkets and social enterprise Community Shop, making them a well-established partner with the scale and infrastructure required to maximise this pathway for businesses within the ZRO system.
Chris Burns, group managing director, Company Shop Group, said: “We are continually looking at ways we provide practical, easy-to-implement solutions for industry as we advance our mission to help create a world where no product needlessly goes to waste. We are thrilled to be the founding redistribution partner in this industry-first partnership, providing a clear route for businesses to redistribute their surplus as well as alternative pathways as part of the ZRO system.”
Alex Keogh, managing director, SugaRich Group, said: “For decades, businesses across the SugaRich Group have helped customers recover value from surplus food in different ways. ZRO brings those capabilities together through a single commercial framework – an important evolution for our business, and in our ambition to lead the industry towards better outcomes for surplus food.”

items.body:
Aldi has been named Multiple Fruit & Veg Retailer of the Year at the 2026 FPC Fresh Awards for a second year running.
The award is determined through a combination of consumer voting, input from across the fresh produce industry and assessment by an expert judging panel using market data and sector expertise.
Whilst it is a blended approach to decide the winner, consumer satisfaction heavily weights the final decision via the public vote, where shoppers were asked to judge retailers on choice, value for money, freshness, quality and customer service.
The award comes as Britain’s biggest discounter continues to invest in quality and value across its range, with £340 million invested so far this year to reduce prices on more than 1,000 products.
The retailer is also strengthening its supplier relationships, with a commitment to source at least half of its British produce through long-term supplier agreements by 2027, giving producers and manufacturers greater confidence to invest in capacity and home-grown production.
Julie Ashfield, chief commercial officer at Aldi UK, said: “This award means so much because it comes from the people who shop with us week in, week out.
“Our suppliers play a huge part in making that possible, and we’re incredibly grateful for their support, particularly during what has been a very challenging year for fresh produce.
“Despite difficult weather conditions, our growers have continued to deliver exceptional quality fruit and vegetables for our customers while working closely with us to maintain the great value we’re known for.
“It’s fantastic recognition of what we and our suppliers work hard to deliver every day: quality fresh produce at prices that work for our customers.”

items.title: Billionaire Weston family closes in on £7bn Boots takeover
items.summary: The Canada arm of the billionaire family behind Primark is inching towards another deal, as it closes in on a £7bn takeover of Boots from its private equity owners. The Westons are in advanced talks to buy the UK pharmacy chain from Sycamore Partners, ending hopes of a potential London IPO. Discussions are ongoing, a [...]
items.body:
Billionaire Weston family closes in on £7bn Boots takeover
The Canada arm of the billionaire family behind Primark is inching towards another deal, as it closes in on a £7bn takeover of Boots from its private equity owners.
The Westons are in advanced talks to buy the UK pharmacy chain from Sycamore Partners, ending hopes of a potential London IPO.
Discussions are ongoing, a person familiar with the matter said, but a deal is expected to be reached as soon as next week, the Wall Street Journal first reported.
The two sides have been in talks regarding a sale over the last few months after Boots was severed from its former parent company, Walgreens Boots Alliance.
An earlier bid from the Weston’s for Boots was rejected after its offer for the high street chain was reduced.
The Weston’s, a Canadian business dynasty, are one of the world’s richest families. The UK arm owns brands including Fortnum & Mason and Primark-owner Associated British Foods.
Battle for Boots
Boots’ future has been thrown into question in recent months. Sycamore weighed up a potential London listing for the pharmacy chain after purchasing it for £18bn last year.
Talks between the two parties over a sale ground to a halt this summer after the conflict in the Middle East and wider economic shocks damaged business confidence.
Sycamore previously held talks with Sigma Healthcare, an Australian pharmacy group, before they pulled out.
Purchasing Boots would mark a return to the UK for the Canadian branch of the family, after they sold department store Selfridges in 2022 for £4bn.
But the pharmacy chain has struggled in recent years, and was forced to close hundreds of UK stores in an attempt to alleviate economic pressures squeezing British high streets.
Sycamore Partners has been contacted for comment. Boots declined to comment.

items.title: Boots owner ‘closing in on sale to Canada’s Weston family for $9bn’
items.summary: Deal would mark return of Canadian family to UK after it sold Selfridges department store for £4bn in 2022 Business live – latest updates The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn). Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week. Continue reading...
items.body:
The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn).
Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week.
If successful, it would mark the return of the Canadian branch of the Weston family to the UK high street, having previously owned Selfridges.
The family later sold the department store chain for £4bn in 2022. The Westons are widely known throughout Canada for owning the grocery store Loblaws and the pharmacy chain Shoppers Drug Mart.
The UK branch of the family, which operates its businesses through a separate investment vehicle, is known for holding a majority stake in Primark through the parent company Associated British Foods.
News of the prospective Weston deal comes months after Sycamore tried and failed to sell Boots to the Australian pharmaceutical group Sigma Healthcare in a deal that would have valued the business at $10bn this summer.
Sycamore has been widely expected to spin off and sell Boots – alongside other parts of the group – after its takeover of the Walgreen Boots Alliance last year. It as has already split the group into five stand-alone companies.
Boots, which was founded in Nottingham in 1849 by John Boot, has changed hands several times in the past 20 years. After a merger with Alliance Unichem in 2006, the combined company was taken over by the private equity firm KKR in 2007, before Walgreens first took a 45% stake in 2012 and then completed a takeover at the end of 2014.
Boots – which has 1,800 stores across the UK – employs about 51,000 people, including about 6,000 at its headquarters in Beeston, three miles south-west of Nottingham.
This summer it reported that revenues had risen 3.2% to £7.5bn in the year to the end of August 2025, with pre-tax profit up by 25% to £337m. It said strong demand for weight loss jabs and beauty products had helped increase its profits.
Boots declined to comment.

items.summary: The sale process for the mall was launched earlier this year, drawing interest from the likes of Mike Ashley's Frasers Group.
items.body:
Owner of Bluewater shopping centre to buy Gateshead's Metrocentre in £516m deal
The owner of the Bluewater shopping centre in Kent has struck a £516million deal to buy the Metrocentre in Gateshead.
London-listed Landsec, which also owns Liverpool One, told investors it had exchanged contracts to buy 100 per cent of the Metrocentre from Tynehawk Holdings as it expands its retail portfolio.
Tynehawk is the holding firm for a consortium of investors who took control of Metrocentre after previous owner Intu collapsed in 2020.
It launched the sale process earlier this year, drawing interest from the likes of Mike Ashley's Frasers Group.
The FTSE 100 property group will fund the deal through a £500million equity issue, including a retail offer to UK investors, as well as existing debt.
Shares in Landsec fell 1.52 per cent to 615p in early trading.
Metrocentre attracts more than 16million visitors every year, generating retail sales of £650million from 282 stores.
Landsec's takeover deal also includes an adjacent retail park with 15 units.
The owner of Bluewater has struck a deal to buy Metrocentre in Gateshead
The deal is conditional on dissolving a legacy legal entity from Metrocentre's collapsed former owner Intu, a process expected to take place next month, and on consent from bondholders.
Landsec chief executive Mark Allan said: 'Growing our investment in major retail destinations remains our highest conviction call, given the high income yields and attractive income growth on offer for the right assets.
'Our acquisition of Metrocentre represents a rare opportunity to obtain 100% control of a top-10 UK shopping centre.'
The acquisition marks a further shift away from office developments towards retail space for Landsec, having previously announced plans to invest £1billion in major retail assets.
The property company also agreed on terms for a separate acquisition worth about £100million to further consolidate its retail portfolio but gave no further details.
Completion of both deals will see major retail destinations account for 46 per cent of Landsec's annualised rental income.
Earlier this week Landsec announced that it had sold 123 Victoria Street, a central London office block, for £211m - a 20 per cent discount to its listed price.
Landsec said it had seen 'strong customer demand' this financial year, with lettings growth over the five months to August 31. It expects to deliver net rental income growth of between 3 and 5 per cent for the year to March 2027.

items.title: High street tax burden ‘costing jobs and pushing up prices’, says BRC
items.summary: Retail and hospitality have the highest effective tax rates of any sector in the UK, leading to fewer jobs for young people, foregone investment, and higher prices for customers, according to new analysis from the British Retail Consortium (BRC). The study compared the taxes and… This story continues at High street tax burden ‘costing jobs and pushing up prices’, says BRC Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The study compared the taxes and profits paid in 11 main sectors of the economy.
It found the two sectors paid a combined £62bn in taxes in 2025/26 through business rates, employer National Insurance Contributions (NICs), VAT, and other government taxes.
Retail and hospitality are two of the nation’s largest employers, providing millions of jobs across every postcode.
They are the largest source of entry-level and flexible jobs, and a gateway to employment and training for those without qualifications or previous experience.
However, the 2024 Budget added billions to their employment costs. As a result, retail lost 122,000 jobs in just two years, while employment in hospitality fell by 93,000 people.
For every £1 of pre-tax profit made by the sector, retailers paid the equivalent of 72p in business taxes, while for hospitality businesses this figure was 82p in the pound: these are the highest rates for any sector, well above the 50p average effective tax rate of all eleven main sectors of the economy, including the 40.5p tax rate of the banking industry. Hospitality and retail’s effective tax rates rose further in 2026/27.
High streets are particularly exposed to the impact of rising business taxes. The presence of retail and hospitality businesses are what keep high streets vibrant and job opportunities available.
Yet they pay a disproportionate level of business rates relative to other industries and together cover almost a third of the total raised by the tax. The consequence is 1 in 7 high street properties across the country lie empty.
Higher taxes leave high street businesses with less money to invest in jobs and local communities and put further upward pressure on prices for shoppers.
With inflation currently at 3.1%, well above the Bank of England’s 2% target, further tax rises risk adding to the cost-of-living pressures facing households.
Ahead of the Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are calling on the chancellor to put local communities first and reduce the cost burden on these two sectors, including removing high street retail and hospitality businesses from the government’s business rates high-value multiplier.
Doing so, said BRC, will help protect the millions of people working there and support those who would be hit by higher prices if these warnings are ignored.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium, said: “The chancellor faces a choice: to continue to pile taxes onto our high streets and the millions of households that rely on them, or to give these businesses the breathing space needed to create jobs, deliver growth, and hold down prices.
Millions of people rely on retail jobs across the country, but the overwhelming tax burden puts those people at risk, with over 100,000 jobs lost in the last two years.
“For every £1 of pre-tax profit made by retail, the equivalent of 72p is now paid in business taxes. This punishing tax burden has clear consequences: job losses, shuttered shops, and a missed opportunity to drive growth in every postcode.
“For the benefit of high streets, young people and shoppers everywhere, the chancellor should use the Budget to deliver a clear path to reducing the rates burden, now and in the future.”

items.title: Vaping Products Duty: What retailers need to know | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy
items.summary: The UK vaping industry is undergoing significant regulatory changes, with recent bans on disposable vapes and potentially major changes to display and packaging regulations. Retailers are having to navigate an increasingly complex set of rules, and from today (1 October 2026), things are going to… This story continues at Vaping Products Duty: What retailers need to know | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Retailers are having to navigate an increasingly complex set of rules, and from today (1 October 2026), things are going to get more challenging.
This year’s budget will see the implementation of the Vaping Products Duty, a new duty that needs to be paid on all vaping liquids, alongside related requirements for vaping duty stamps.
Non-compliant retailers could face fines of up to £10,000.
So, what do retailers need to do and how could the changes impact their businesses?
What is happening on 1st October?
The most noticeable change for consumers and retailers will be the introduction of a new duty on vape liquid. This is charged according to the volume of the liquid and is set at £2.20 per 10 ml, equivalent to 22p per ml. This applies to all vaping liquids, whether they contain nicotine or not, with the standard VAT rate of 20% continuing to apply.
Engage with your customers
Retailers should understand how the new duty could affect the price of the products they sell and be prepared to explain the changes to customers. Retailers should explain that this is a government duty and that all responsible retailers will be implementing the same changes and the same price increases.
Know what to look for
The new rules won’t just affect retail prices; there are also important changes to how vaping products must be labelled and sold. The UK Vaping Duty Stamp will be a small rectangular security label measuring 18 mm × 42 mm. It must be attached to the outermost retail packaging and positioned so that opening the product damages either the stamp or the packaging. After 31 December, all stamps must include a digital code that can be scanned for authentication and supply-chain traceability.
Sell-through period
The government has allowed a six-month sell-through period during which retailers may still sell existing stock that was imported or manufactured in the UK prior to 1st October and is therefore not stamped. This sell-through period ends on 31 March 2027. From 1st April 2027, all vaping products must have a valid stamp.
Review existing stock
Retailers should review current stock and calculate how much unstamped stock may need to be sold by the deadline. They should maintain an audit trail of invoices and delivery documents to prove that the products were imported or manufactured before 1st October 2026.
Engage with suppliers
Retailers should engage suppliers to confirm that any stock received after the October deadline will be compliant and have duty-paid stamps. If retailers believe they may have a surplus of stock that they will be unable to sell by the March 2027 deadline, they should discuss the possibility of returning it to their suppliers in exchange for compliant replacement products.
What should retailers do with unstamped stock?
If retailers are unable to exchange stock with their suppliers, they can consider running clearance discounts or bundle deals to clear unstamped stock before the deadline. Any stock not sold by 1 April 2027 cannot legally be sold without a duty stamp, meaning unsold inventory must be returned or responsibly recycled.
Retailers caught selling unstamped products after the grace period could face significant penalties. HMRC can seize non-compliant stock and issue fines of up to £10,000, with penalties increasing for repeat offences. In the most serious cases, businesses could also face criminal investigation, an unlimited fine or imprisonment.
How can I dispose of unsold or unsellable stock?
- Do not bin unsold stock: E-liquids and electronic components cannot go into standard general commercial waste or regular bins.
- Waste contractors: Use licensed waste carriers or specialised electrical recycling providers, such as local recycling centres, to safely handle surplus hardware.
- Work with your suppliers: Arrange a plan with your suppliers for suitable disposal.
- Check official guidelines: Review updates to the GOV.UK Vaping Products Duty guidance for compliance requirements.
Dr Marina Murphy, is head of external affairs UK and scientific affairs at Haypp

items.body:
Embracing opportunities in data and AI at pace: the biggest retail technology stories from September
September is done and dusted, October is up and running, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful month for the retail technology space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from September, including Tesco, AIUTA, Morrisons, Kingfisher, VoCoVo, The Range, Rainbow, Hanshow, The Entertainer, THG Commerce, Primark, Boots, TikTok Shop, Waitrose, and Trust Retail.
1. Tesco teams with AIUTA to test out virtual try-on technology for F&F clothing in Sandhurst Extra store
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
2. Home improvement retailer Kingfisher taps AI tech driven personalisation as it ups profit target
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
3. UK grocery giant Morrisons names former Kingfisher executive Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer
Morrisons has appointed Dr Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joins from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
He will take overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He will report directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh when he takes up the role on 1st October.
“Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way,” says Baitiéh.
“Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact.”
Ghasempour says: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”
4. Boots pilot launching on TikTok Shop in partnership with THG Commerce on 28th September
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
5. Waitrose keeps the faith with Trust Retail through to 2031 as inventory tech roll-out expands
Waitrose has extended its partnership with Trust Retail, a Trust Payments business, for a further five years, taking the relationship through to November 2031 as the supermarket prepares to accelerate the roll-out of Trust Retail’s inventory management technology across its store estate.
The technology was first trialled in a Waitrose store in March 2026 and is now live across eight stores. A wider roll-out is scheduled to begin at the end of September, with approximately 125 stores expected to be live before Christmas and the remaining Waitrose estate scheduled to follow by March 2027.
Trust Retail’s inventory management technology gives Waitrose partners a real-time view of stock, replacing processes that previously relied on batch updates. Transactions are reflected immediately across connected inventory and accounting systems, providing a more accurate and up-to-date view of stock throughout the trading day.
Using handheld devices, store partners can access current inventory information to support day-to-day activities including replenishment, stock management and markdown decisions.
6. Redefining the omnichannel landscape: RTIH's latest Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List goes live
The latest edition of the RTIH Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List is here! The list has seen a surge in popularity over the past few years, to the point that we’ve decided publishing it once a year is no longer enough. Here, then, is the second edition for 2026, with some names dropping out of the top 100 and some new names coming in (the latter are flagged as new entries for ease of reference).
Including the likes of retailers, brands, technologists, analysts, and consultants, the list celebrates individuals who are helping to redefine retail in a fast moving omnichannel age.
We use a variety of sources to select our top 100, including feedback from industry observers, research within our own networks, direct or third–party nominations via our website, and social media tools.
In addition to social presence, we also take into account award winners and judges, event speakers, books published, media appearances, and people building innovative companies, solutions etc in the retail space.
We hope you enjoy reading through the top 100 and, as always, if you would like to give feedback or believe that there are some glaring omissions, please feel free to get in touch.
Many thanks to 3D Cloud, which provides 3D product visualisation software trusted by top furniture and DIY retailers, for sponsoring the list.

UK toy retailer, The Entertainer, has appointed THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, as its new digital commerce partner. The multi-year tie up will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital experience, with the aim of creating a more intuitive, inspiring and personalised journey for families, gift buyers and adult toy and collectible enthusiasts.
THG Commerce will deploy AI enabled shopping assistance, conversational discovery and intent led search capabilities to help customers explore thousands of products and find the right choice more intuitively. These capabilities draw on the wider THG Ingenuity collaboration with Google Cloud, which harnesses Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini.
Alongside smarter search and discovery, the new experience will bring together richer content, curated product journeys and personalised recommendations to inspire customers throughout the purchasing journey. THG Commerce will deliver a new web and mobile experience, together with an enhanced Click & Collect journey designed to create a more seamless connection between digital discovery and
The Entertainer’s nationwide store network.
The new platform is expected to launch in spring 2027 and has been designed to provide a foundation for future opportunities across loyalty, retail media and social commerce as The Entertainer continues to develop its omnichannel customer proposition.
8. Late to the online party Primark announces plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain
This follows the purchase of an automated fulfilment facility in Sheffield. A famous online laggard, the retailer went live with a Click and Collect service in 2022, but owner Associated British Foods (ABF) now says there is "opportunity for profitable growth" through home deliveries.
The move, which was denied following media reports earlier this year, comes as Primark prepares to split from ABF. This is likely to complete in December 2027 and is expected to create two new FTSE 100 companies, with analysts predicting that Primark could be valued at as much as £9 billion, and the food part of the business £4 billion.
“This is a really big day for us here at Primark, with two significant announcements: Our decision to bring home delivery to Great Britain and expanding our franchise business. Exciting times ahead,” said Eoin Tonge, CEO at Primark.
A spokesperson for the retailer commented: “Our stores will always be at the heart of Primark. But a lot has changed in online retail in recent years, from how customers shop and their expectations for online delivery. Combined with the digital progress we’ve made, and particularly the success of Click & Collect, we’re confident the time is right to give customers in Great Britain even more choice in how they shop with us.”
9. The Range to roll-out VoCoVo headsets across all 283 locations following one-store trial
VoCoVo has announced a partnership with home, leisure and garden retailer The Range, that will see Series 5 (S5) Pro Headsets and Call Points rolled out across all 283 of its stores. This follows a one-store trial over the course of a year.
The Range colleagues will get instant, hands free communication through the headsets, replacing disruptive loudspeaker calls and reducing the need for them to search the shop floor for one another. The technology will help deliver faster, more responsive customer service by reducing waiting times at tills, service desks and across the shop floor.
Colleagues can contact managers and team members immediately for price and stock checks, quickly coordinate requests and assign tasks in real-time, while two-way Call Points will allow customers to request assistance at the touch of a button and connect with available colleagues.
A Store Manager at The Range says: “The headsets have made a hugely positive impact in-store for both colleagues and customers. Customer service has noticeably improved as queries are answered faster, stock checks are smoother and warehouse to shop floor communication is instant. This has already streamlined Deliveroo and Click & Collect, and I can see the headsets becoming invaluable during patio season. They’ve become essential to daily operations."
“The very impressive results already achieved in our store have laid the groundwork for much bigger savings across the store network. I can’t wait to see colleagues benefitting from the same technology.”
Beth Worrall, CEO at VoCoVo, says: “The initial trial with The Range has shown how they can achieve significant time and cost savings while maintaining outstanding service levels and the optimum in-store experience at the same time. We’re looking forward to working alongside the team to implement the technology across all its stores.”
10. Chinese retailer Rainbow opens its first Hanshow powered Store Digital Twin supermarket in Shenzhen
Rainbow, a Chinese omnichannel retailer, has opened its upgraded Shahe sp@ce supermarket in Shenzhen. Developed in collaboration with Hanshow and Rainbow's technology subsidiary Lingzhi Digital Technology, the project marks its first Store Digital Twin implementation, bringing together real-time store visibility, decision support and operational execution within a live retail environment.
Located in Shenzhen's Nanshan District, the Shahe sp@ce location has served the local community for nearly 17 years. In 2026, the wider Shahe Rainbow development was upgraded into an urban lifestyle destination that brings together retail, dining, services and entertainment. The move reflects Rainbow's broader ambition to expand the role of physical retail beyond transactions and create a more engaging destination for the surrounding community.
The newly opened sp@ce supermarket, built around Rainbow's "City • Garden • Food Hall" concept, features nine experiential areas designed around different food, lifestyle and community occasions. The store also incorporates Rainbow's intelligent fulfilment centre, supporting more efficient home delivery services and aiming to strengthen the connection between in-store shopping and its broader omnichannel retail model.
As its first Store Digital Twin enabled supermarket, the store brings together more than 17,000 IoT devices and AI capabilities to provide greater visibility into store conditions and support more timely operational decisions and actions.

items.body:
Halfords taps Blink technology as it takes wraps off new internal communications platform
Halfords has unveiled Pulse, the retailer’s new internal communications platform, powered by Blink. Designed to connect colleagues across the entire Halfords Group, Pulse brings together communications, recognition, resources, and key tools into one mobile first experience.
A spokesperson for Halfords said: “Whether colleagues are serving customers in our stores and garages, supporting operations in our distribution centres, or working behind the scenes from our support centres, the Blink platform provides a simpler way for our One Halfords Family to stay informed, connected, and engaged.”
“A huge thank you to the Blink team for their partnership throughout the project. Their expertise, innovative solutions, and collaborative approach have helped turn a shared vision into reality, and their support has been invaluable from planning through to launch. We're also incredibly grateful to the many Halfords colleagues who have contributed to bringing Pulse to life - this has been a true cross-functional, team effort driven by a shared ambition to create a better colleague experience for everyone.”
They added: “Today is just the beginning, and we're excited to see colleagues across the group start connecting, sharing, recognising, and celebrating together on Pulse. Helping our One Halfords Family stay connected and keep the nation moving, together.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Mobile retail will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
Boots UK lands on TikTok Shop as Kingfisher taps AI: the top retail technology plays from September
RTIH brings you its stand out technology deployments from September, including Lincolnshire Co-op, The Barcode Warehouse, H&M, Voyado, HyperFinity, JD Sports, Asda, Vusion, VoCoVo, The Range, Primark, Tapestry, Morrisons, Instaleap, Waitrose, Trust Retail, Rainbow, Hanshow, Skechers, KNAPP, The Entertainer, THG Commerce, and Iceland Foods.
Lincolnshire Co-op
The Barcode Warehouse is working with Lincolnshire Co-op on the roll-out of a new self-checkout solution. Lincolnshire Co-op, which operates more than 220 outlets across Lincolnshire and neighbouring counties, including food stores, pharmacies, post offices and travel branches, is expanding self-service checkout options across its food store estate as part of its investment in enhancing customer experience.
Andy Warman, Chief Commercial and Transformation Officer at Lincolnshire Co-op, says: “The introduction of self-checkouts across our food stores represents an important step in enhancing the shopping experience for our customers. Working with The Barcode Warehouse, we have delivered a solution that provides greater convenience, reduces queuing times, and gives customers more choice in how they shop. This investment reflects our ongoing commitment to continuing to deliver high standards of customer service and embracing innovation technology that adds value for our communities.”
The Barcode Warehouse has supplied and supported the retailer's in-store technology estate for more than three years. Today, it supplies Point of Sale equipment, handheld devices for stock management and pricing updates, reduced to clear printing solutions and managed services support across the business.
Iceland Foods
Iceland Foods has partnered with Retail Insight to deploy its AI powered WasteInsight solution as part of the retailer's focus on reducing food waste.
General Manager of EMEA and APAC at Retail Insight, Martin Rigby, says: "Retailers have access to more operational data than ever before, but data only creates value when it enables better decisions. The opportunity is to move from reporting what has already happened to identifying where action is needed before waste occurs.”
"We are delighted to be working with Iceland to support its continued focus on reducing food waste. By combining AI with operational insight, WasteInsight helps surface the products and actions that matter most, enabling colleagues to intervene earlier and with greater confidence."
Iceland Foods’ Stores Director, Steve Shirley, says: "Reducing food waste remains an important priority for Iceland. We are continually looking at ways to improve how we use operational data to support our colleagues in making faster, better informed decisions in stores.”
"Working with Retail Insight will help us explore how AI driven operational intelligence can support our waste reduction objectives while improving consistency across our store operations."
H&M
H&M has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” says Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, says: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”
Tesco
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
Boots UK
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
Asda
Asda and InPost have announced a new partnership that will see up to 700 of the latter’s parcel lockers installed across the former’s UK store estate. This will give Asda customers a new way to send, collect and return parcels while they shop, and is pitched as one of InPost’s most significant UK retail partnerships to date.
The lockers will be installed across a mix of Asda superstores, supermarkets and Express locations.
Joseph Sutton, Director - Express, Fuel & Wholesale, says: "Our unmatched mix of services is a key part of what sets Asda apart, and we know customers increasingly value the convenience of being able to tick off multiple tasks in a single trip. We're delighted to be partnering with InPost to bring parcel lockers to up to 700 locations nationwide.
This roll-out gives customers a fast and flexible way to collect and return parcels, seamlessly fitting around their weekly shop and making everyday life a little easier."
Paul Smith
Paul Smith has completed its roll-out of Sitoo’s cloud native unified commerce and PoS platform for fashion and lifestyle retailers across 31 stores in eight countries. In a LinkedIn post, Sitoo said: “A major milestone with an amazing customer!”
It added: “After months of close collaboration, it’s fantastic to see Sitoo now live across all Paul Smith stores and markets - and even more exciting to think about what comes next. A huge thank you to the brilliant teams at Paul Smith and Sitoo who made this milestone possible. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together and excited to continue working closely as our partnership grows. Here’s to the next chapter!”
Kingfisher Group
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
VILLOID
StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.
Tapestry
Tapestry is bringing Coach and Kate Spade into Google's AI shopping ecosystem, making products purchasable directly from Google Search, including AI Mode, and the Gemini app. Now, when shoppers discover a Coach or Kate Spade item while using Gemini or AI Mode, a "Buy" button appears inline. After selecting their product, customers can complete checkout in just a few taps using Google Pay. This eliminates the need for website redirects.
"Consumer behaviours are always evolving. At one time, discovery happened in a store window or a magazine. Then, it happened on social media. Now it's happening inside a conversation with AI," says Joanne Crevoiserat, Chief Executive Officer at Tapestry. "Our goal is for shoppers to find and engage with our brands at the moment when inspiration strikes, whether it be when a consumer passes by one of our stores, peruses our websites, or chats with AI.”
Tapestry has implemented the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), an open industry standard for agentic commerce backed by several tech and e-commerce companies.
"We built this layer to work with our existing operations today, but it's truly protocol agnostic, so we can quickly move into new AI environments as consumer behaviours evolve," says Yang Lu, Chief Information and Digital Officer at Tapestry. "That's possible because of the strategic investments we've made in technology capabilities and infrastructure as well as the strength of our data and consumer insights engine."
UCP powered checkout is now live in the US, with plans to expand across geographies in the future.

Guess
GXO Logistics and Exotec have deployed Exotec’s Skypod system at GXO's Venlo, Netherlands, facility, home to fashion brand Guess. The installation includes 127 Skypod robots, 60,000 rack locations, eight goods-to-person picking stations and 200 metres of conveyor network.
The system is also capable of processing up to 70,000 pieces per day, achieving throughput of up to 2,200 order lines per hour during peak periods.
With the deployment of the automated solution, GXO says it is enhancing fulfilment operations for Guess across EMEA and Asia by increasing throughput, improving productivity and supporting future growth.
Mark Donné, Operations Manager, GXO Venlo, says: "The impact has been evident from day one. Our automated solution with Exotec, tailored specifically for Guess, has helped take our operation to the next level, enabling faster processing, greater predictability and a smoother workflow across the site. As our business with Guess continues to grow, we have the scalability and flexibility needed to support future demand."
Wim Vermeir, Senior Sales Executive Benelux, Exotec, comments: "Fashion logistics doesn't tolerate approximation - high SKU counts, seasonal spikes, and EMEA wide distribution require precision engineering, not off-the-shelf automation. With GXO, we designed a system built specifically for those demands, and the throughput numbers speak for themselves. The result is a highly efficient operation that supports both current performance and future growth."

Morrisons
Instaleap, a company providing software for e‑commerce fulfillment and last mile operations that was recently bought by Instacart, and Morrisons have announced a new partnership.
“We’re proud to partner with Morrisons, one of the UK’s most respected grocery retailers, as they continue to strengthen their omnichannel offering,” says Antonio Nunes, Head of Instaleap. "Consumers now increasingly expect ordering from their local supermarket to be as easy as ordering take-away. Meeting that demand at scale - efficiently, reliably - takes technology built specifically for grocery. That's exactly what we're giving Morrisons."
“We’re constantly looking for ways to make online grocery shopping easier and more convenient,” says Charlotte Exell, Group Online Director at Morrisons. “More of our customers are choosing to shop from us through one of our immediacy partners and they expect an efficient, dependable service every time. Working with Instaleap powers our online operations behind the scenes, helping us deliver fresh groceries directly to our customers’ doors quickly and reliably.”

implementation, bringing together real-time store visibility, decision support and operational execution within a live retail environment.

VoCoVo has announced a partnership with home, leisure and garden retailer The Range, that will see Series 5 (S5) Pro Headsets and Call Points rolled out across all 283 of its stores. This follows a one-store trial over the course of a year.
The Range colleagues will get instant, hands free communication through the headsets, replacing disruptive loudspeaker calls and reducing the need for them to search the shop floor for one another. The technology will help deliver faster, more responsive customer service by reducing waiting times at tills, service desks and across the shop floor.
Colleagues can contact managers and team members immediately for price and stock checks, quickly coordinate requests and assign tasks in real-time, while two-way Call Points will allow customers to request assistance at the touch of a button and connect with available colleagues.
A Store Manager at The Range says: “The headsets have made a hugely positive impact in-store for both colleagues and customers. Customer service has noticeably improved as queries are answered faster, stock checks are smoother and warehouse to shop floor communication is instant. This has already streamlined Deliveroo and Click & Collect, and I can see the headsets becoming invaluable during patio season. They’ve become essential to daily operations."
“The very impressive results already achieved in our store have laid the groundwork for much bigger savings across the store network. I can’t wait to see colleagues benefitting from the same technology.”
Beth Worrall, CEO at VoCoVo, says: “The initial trial with The Range has shown how they can achieve significant time and cost savings while maintaining outstanding service levels and the optimum in-store experience at the same time. We’re looking forward to working alongside the team to implement the technology across all its stores.”
JD Sports
HyperFinity has partnered with JD Sports to design and deliver a personalisation programme that aims to equip the retailer with a clear evidence base for its loyalty strategy.
It has designed a personalisation engine and trialled this to build a framework for JD Sports UK. The solution was trialled to prove: The value of ‘buy again’ category offers to assess how active customers respond to identify the optimal spend multiplier incentives; The optimal incentive mix for high and low spenders for cash-based rewards versus spend multipliers; The ability to drive incremental basket spend through cross-sell offers aligned to previous purchase history, testing product affinity and which category follow-ons drive incremental spend.
According to those involved, the trials established that relevance consistently outperforms simply increasing incentive value, and that higher spenders respond better to spend multipliers, while lower spenders react similarly to both. Alongside this, they identified that campaign spacing must be tailored to individual behaviour to avoid offer fatigue.
The partnership delivered a significant material impact on topline performance, including an uplift in total in-store loyalty sales across JD Sports UK during the trial period. Based on the results, JD Sports has identified a multi-million pound opportunity to grow in-store loyalty sales within the first year of scaling the programme.
In addition to the analysis, HyperFinity delivered a suite of assets, including measurement dashboards, customer segmentations, campaign templates, and product seasonality and affinity insights, enabling JD Sports to continue building on the programme.
Asda
Asda has completed the roll-out of eSELs across its Asda Express petrol stations, Asda Express locations and Asda petrol station estate, with the deployment covering over 550 stores.
In a LinkedIn post, Anthony McCarron, Projects, Propostions & Comms Manager at Asda, said: "This is a massive achievement across so many internal and external stakeholders, so thank you - big shout to Daniel Pelissier for leading this project from start to finish on time and on budget."
"Our Vusion eSELs, installed by our delivery partner Renovotec, are delivering a real step change for customers and colleagues. Thank you to Elecomm, MADIC UK, and Evolve for the infrastructure support in achieving this huge milestone for our convenience stores."

Former River Island Chief Information Officer Simon Pakenham-Walsh joins The Premier League
Simon Pakenham-Walsh has joined The Premier League, the top tier of England’s football pyramid, as Chief Technology and Data Officer. He was previously at River Island where he served as CIO. His CV also includes stints at Sweaty Betty (CTO) and Wolverine Worldwide (VP of Consumer Technology).
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “It is a privilege to join such an iconic organisation, and I am thrilled to bring together my passion for sport with my experience in technology and data. I look forward to learning from colleagues across the business and contributing to the ongoing success of the Premier League. I'm excited for the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead.”
SJ Grabiec
River Island recently appointed SJ Grabiec as Customer Director. She joined from AllSaints where she had spent the past 15 years, most recently serving as Global Head of Customer (CX, CS & CRM).
She said: "I’ve just passed the four week mark in my new role at River Island. After almost 15 years with AllSaints, it felt like the right moment to step back and reflect on a really important chapter in my career."
She added: "I’m genuinely the most grateful to AllSaints. It’s an incredible brand with incredible people. Leaving wasn’t easy, but I do so with a lot of respect, appreciation and love for the talent and people there, as well as everything I experienced and learned."
At River Island, she steps into a Director level role covering paid media, CRM and growth retention, as well as customer product, customer operations (including contact centre, payments and post-purchase), and CX and UX.
Grabiec added: "I’m loving it, a big thank you to everyone who has made me feel so welcome. I’m supported by three expert Heads of Department, and their strong operational and technical teams who are driving the customer and marketing vision."
"What’s stood out for me at River Island is the energy and ambition across the business, along with a real love for the brand. People genuinely care about it, and you can feel that straight away. The long tenures here also say a lot about the positive work culture, and that’s something I’ve already felt since joining. It’s a great place to be, and I’m excited for what’s ahead."

Streetwear brand Stüssy enlists Relex Solutions to connect global merchandise and inventory planning
Stüssy is partnering with RELEX Solutions to connect forecasting, replenishment and merchandise financial planning across its global operations. RELEX will support the streetwear brand across stores, e-commerce and distribution centres (DCs).
Stüssy designs and markets men’s and women’s apparel and accessories, with products sold through its own stores as well as skate, surf, department and specialty retailers. The company operates a business spanning North America, Europe and Asia. As it grows its global operations, connecting demand, inventory and financial planning across channels have become increasingly important.
RELEX will support forecasting and replenishment alongside open to buy and merchandise financial planning. This will give teams better visibility into demand and lost sales, helping sharpen future buying decisions and improve sales and seasonal sell-through through stronger demand forecasting. Stüssy has selected Neos by Argon, a RELEX partner, to help bring the planning approach into operation across its network.
“Stüssy knows where it wants to take its planning organisation and has set a clear bar for what success looks like,” says Frank Lord, Chief Revenue Officer at RELEX Solutions. “Better visibility into customer demand will help the team make more informed buying decisions and plan with confidence and we’re excited to support them as they build for the next stage of growth.”
So hot right now
RELEX Solutions is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

THG Fulfil expands AutoStore global tie up to offer systems via both CapEx ownership and RaaS model
THG Fulfil, a fulfilment operating system from THG Ingenuity, has announced the expansion of its distribution partnership with AutoStore. The expanded tie up extends its distribution authorisation beyond a robotics as a service (RaaS) model to include traditional CapEx ownership, with the aim of giving brands and retailers greater commercial flexibility when investing in warehouse automation.
THG Fulfil operates 796 AutoStore robots across its own fulfilment network and has integrated the AutoStore system with its own proprietary WCS, to deliver over 11,000 bins to picking stations per hour and cut average pick wait times by 78%. That experience underpinned its recent AutoStore build for Footasylum, comprising 85 AutoStore R5 robots across more than 96,000 bin locations, storing the retailer’s entire live SKU range.
The expanded agreement gives THG Fulfil global distribution rights for the entire AutoStore product range under the CapEx model, while its RaaS offering covers a selected range of AutoStore products, including R5 Pro and R5 Pro+ robots, CarouselPort, ConveyorPort and VersaPort.
Tom Killeen, COO at THG Ingenuity, says: “Automation should never force brands to choose between control and cash flow. Our AutoStore distribution offering was originally built around a RaaS model because, for many of our clients, protecting capital while scaling automation was the right call.”
“But as more ambitious brands are ready to own their automation outright, we wanted to give them that option too, without losing any of the design, integration, software and operational expertise that comes with working with THG Fulfil. It provides CFOs with the ability to assess the merits of both a RaaS and CapEx route, so we can meet brands and retailers wherever they are in their automation journey.”
Russell Holmes, Sales Director UK & I, AutoStore, says: “Giving customers greater flexibility in how they invest in automation helps them scale in a way that fits their business. By expanding our partnership with THG Fulfil to include both CapEx and RaaS models, we can support more businesses in choosing the commercial approach that best fits their operational and financial priorities.”

The NFL lands on London’s Oxford Street as Fanatics opens pop-up store for 2026 London games
The National Football League and Fanatics, the league's official retail partner, are set to open an NFL Shop pop-up retail store on London's Oxford Street, as American football returns to the capital for three games this October.
Located at 360-366 Oxford Street, the 1,000 sq ft store will be open from Thursday, 1st October, to Monday, 19th October, spanning all three 2026 NFL London games: the Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders on 4th October and the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars on 11th October, both at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, followed by the Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on 18th October.
Fans can shop official NFL jerseys and an assortment of merchandise across NFL teams, alongside a range of products available exclusively in London. The Oxford Street store will also host NFL Shop LIVE!, a programme of fan events. On opening night, Thursday, 1st October, NFL UK legend Efe Obada will sit down with broadcaster Neil Reynolds to talk about his NFL career and new charity project. On Thursday, 8th October, Phoebe Schecter and Neil Reynolds will record an NFL London Games special of "Inside the Huddle" in front of a live audience. Both events start at 6 p.m., with limited seating available on a first come, first served basis.
The store at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will also become an official NFL Shop from Saturday, 3rd October to Sunday, 11th October, across both Tottenham games, with a number of exclusive collections available in-store. It opens with an NFL Shop Tottenham Family Day on Saturday, 3rd October, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., with games, prizes, exclusive merchandise and special guests.
"NFL Shop has become part of the London Games experience, and this year we're taking it further," says Salha Latif, Vice President of Global Consumer Products at the NFL. "Alongside a number of exclusive collections, fans can join our NFL Shop LIVE! events on Oxford Street and visit an official NFL Shop at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, giving them more ways to connect with the game and the teams they love."
"Every October, London comes alive with fans from across the league as they travel to the city for these games," says Stephen Dowling, International President at Fanatics. "Oxford Street is one of the most famous shopping destinations in the world, and with three games across three weekends, our stores give every fan, whichever team they support, the chance to get official NFL gear and exclusive London products to add to their experience. Our best collaborations tell a story about the place they're made for, and this year's London range is no exception."
