items.title: M&S links up with Sephora to lure younger shoppers
items.summary: Beauty specialist will open branded areas in 100 Marks & Spencer stores and will sell its products on chain’s website Business live – latest updates Marks & Spencer is has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract younger shoppers. The French retailer is set to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year. Continue reading...
items.body:
Marks & Spencer is has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract younger shoppers.
The French retailer is set to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year.
Seophora relaunched in the UK in 2023 with huge fanfare and now has about 18 stand-alone British stores. The company is owned by LVMH, the luxury goods group led by Bernard Arnault, who with his family is among the world’s richest people with a $171bn (£129bn) fortune, according to Forbes.
The company has rapidly expanded on its second attempt to enter the UK market after closing a handful of stores in 2005, having failed make a dent in a competitive sector. The deal with M&S marks a new strategy in its expansion plans.
Analysts have said Sephora’s work with up-and-coming brands and collaborations with high-profile influencers on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube has helped the brand reach its target female audience of 24- to 36-year-olds.
John Lyttle, the managing director of M&S’s fashion, home and beauty division, said: “Beauty is an important category for M&S, with the potential to attract new customers to shop with us and give existing customers the opportunity to shop with us more often.”
“Combining Sephora’s specialist expertise with the strength of the M&S brand, our store estate and our growing digital platform,” Lyttle said. “Alongside this, we will continue investing in our own-label beauty categories where we have established strength and customer trust.”
Retailers have been battling to grab a share of the beauty market after the disappearance of many department stores. In recent years a swathe of UK department stores have closed, including Debenhams, Beales and about half the House of Fraser chain.
Sephora’s self-service model – which allows consumers to touch and test makeup and perfume without the help of shop staff – is seen to appeal to younger shoppers, who may test in store and buy online. The tie-up could provide increased competition for the specialist health and beauty chains Boots and Superdrug.
Lyttle said the deal was part of M&S’s wider transformation plan, which involves £700m of investments in revitalising stores, modernising its supply chain and distribution system, and further improvements in products.
The group, which employs more than 65,000 people, has 227 full-line stores – containing food, clothing, homewares and beauty – after closing dozens of old and out-of-place outlets. More will shut over the next two years and a handful of new outlets are opening with the aim to have 200 full-line stores in the UK.
M&S’s food arm is expanding rapidly, with 18 food-only stores opening this year as it heads for a target of 420, compared with 335 directly operated outlets. Franchise partners run another 466 in the UK and more overseas.
Sarah Boyd, the managing director of Sephora UK, said: “Together, we can redefine what high street beauty means for customers across the UK, bringing the very best curated brand and beauty experience to the M&S stores.”
She said the group would introduce its beauty advisers to M&S stores to “provide a truly personalised experience, and to reach customers in more communities where they already live, shop and spend their time”.

Jo Malone London announces the next chapter in its UK retail expansion, officially launching within Space NK.
From today, Tuesday 29th September 2026, the British fragrance and lifestyle house will be available in 26 Space NK stores nationwide and online at SpaceNK.com, bringing a curated edit of its most-loved scents to Space NK’s highly engaged beauty community.
Known for its joyfully British spirit, elegant craftsmanship and unexpected approach to fragrance, Jo Malone London brings its unrivalled olfactive offering to Space NK, encouraging discovery among consumers with a carefully considered edit that offers the perfect introduction to the world of Jo Malone London. The selection includes much-loved icons such as Lime Basil & Mandarin, English Pear & Freesia, Pomegranate Noir and Wood Sage & Sea Salt, alongside new favourites Sea Salt & Bergamot and Cypress & Grapevine Cologne Intense.
Speaking on the launch, Lizzie Brady, vice president general manager, Jo Malone London UK, says: “Launching with Space NK marks an exciting new chapter for Jo Malone London in the UK. Renowned for its carefully curated approach to beauty and highly engaged community, Space NK is a natural partner for us. This partnership gives us the opportunity to introduce Jo Malone London to new and existing consumers in a distinctive environment, through a considered edit of our most-loved scents, while staying true to the elevated experience and sense of discovery at the heart of our brand.”

items.title: M&S and Sephora partner to bring a new beauty destination to high streets across the UK
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. M&S today announces a strategic partnership with Sephora to create Sephora at M&S, a new beauty destination launching in selected M&S stores and on M&S.com from spring 2027. The partnership is an important next step in the transformation of M&S Fashion, Home and Beauty, offering customers more of the beauty brands they love and a […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
M&S today announces a strategic partnership with Sephora to create Sephora at M&S, a new beauty destination launching in selected M&S stores and on M&S.com from spring 2027.
The partnership is an important next step in the transformation of M&S Fashion, Home and Beauty, offering customers more of the beauty brands they love and a stronger specialist experience.
By bringing together Sephora’s beauty expertise, brand relationships and focus on discovery with M&S’s trusted brand, national presence and omnichannel platform, the partnership will make a specialist beauty experience accessible to more customers in more places. M&S will bring Sephora to 100 high streets and retail parks across the UK.
The new, transformed beauty offer will help attract new customers and give existing customers more reasons to shop with M&S more frequently.
For Sephora, the partnership marks the next step in its UK growth story, extending its prestige beauty experience into more communities through the UK’s most trusted brand*. Building on Sephora’s destination store, boutique and digital formats, the shop-in-shop retail model will give more customers access to curated brands, expert advice and the beauty discovery experience for which Sephora is known.
Customers can expect a carefully curated mix of established beauty favourites, emerging brands and exclusive products across skincare, makeup, fragrance, haircare and bodycare.
Specialist beauty teams will support customers in stores while M&S.com will offer a broader online range with home delivery and Click & Collect from M&S stores nationwide. The final brand line-up will be confirmed closer to launch, alongside details of new-to-M&S names and selected Sephora exclusives.
John Lyttle, managing director, Fashion, Home & Beauty at M&S, said: “We’re transforming Fashion, Home and Beauty at M&S, creating a better experience for our customers and building a more efficient, more profitable business. Our new partnership with Sephora is the next step in this transformation. Beauty is an important category for M&S, with the potential to attract new customers to shop with us and give existing customers the opportunity to shop with us more often.
“Our partnership with Sephora will sit at the heart of our future beauty offer, combining Sephora’s specialist expertise with the strength of the M&S brand, our store estate and our growing digital platform. Alongside this, we will continue investing in our own-label Beauty categories where we have established strength and customer trust.”
Catherine Spindler, president of Europe & Middle East, Sephora, said: “Sephora’s ambition has always been to continually evolve how we bring our expertise in beauty to market, adapting our global model to reflect the needs and opportunities of each region. In the UK, this has seen us build a deliberately complementary ecosystem across our digital and app proposition, large-format ‘Temples of Beauty’ and, most recently, our curated boutique concepts that debuted in London this summer.
“Our UK launch has been such a huge success, that we wanted to go further and faster. Our partnership with M&S is the next evolution of this strategy, introducing a retail model that complements our existing formats and allows us to build on the strength of the Sephora brand in the UK. By combining our global expertise in prestige beauty with M&S’s established retail infrastructure, we are creating a more diversified and scalable model for growth, while continuing to evolve the way customers can access the Sephora experience.”
Sarah Boyd, managing director, SEPHORA UK said: “Since bursting on to the scene in the UK, we have always believed that becoming part of the communities we serve means more than simply opening stores and having a great online experience. We have taken a deliberately local approach to every city we enter, from celebrating local culture and creators to tailoring our opening moments and marketing to reflect the people who live there. This personalisation has been a huge part of our success thus far, and now partnering with M&S, a brand so trusted, loved and deeply ingrained in British life is not just a great honour and privilege, but also an extremely exciting next step in our expansion journey.
“Together, we can re-define what high street beauty means for customers across the UK, bringing the very best curated brand and beauty experience to the M&S stores to complement their food, fashion and home expertise. We are excited to introduce our incredible Beauty Advisors to the stores to provide a truly personalised experience, and to reach customers in more communities where they already live, shop and spend their time.
“This partnership marks an important milestone in our continuing drive to become a truly winning formula on the UK High Street.”

items.title: Reform Senedd member visits Fed retailers in Tenby, West Wales
items.summary: Members of the Federation of Independent Retailers (The Fed), Vince and Fiona Malone, welcomed Senedd member Claire Archibald to their Tenby Store to show the vital role their shop and post office plays in their West Wales Community. After a career in healthcare, Archibald was… This story continues at Reform Senedd member visits Fed retailers in Tenby, West Wales Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
After a career in healthcare, Archibald was elected to the Senedd in May this year, elected to the Ceredigion Penfro constituency as a Reform candidate.
The meeting highlighted the social value of shops and post offices, with particular emphasis on the 650 post offices across Wales.
The Malones, of Morrisons Daily – Tenby Stores and Post Office, emphasised the particularly high cost of business – through a mix of high business rate costs and high commercial costs and energy bills – and how they make it increasingly difficult to sustain small retail businesses, despite their social value.
Mr and Mrs Malone also highlighted the launch of the Deposit Return Scheme for recycling bottles and cans when it goes live in October 2027 and the work the Fed is undertaking to help small shops prepare.
They also shared concerns about potential complexities in Wales linked to bringing glass into the scheme, which is scheduled to fully take effect after a longer four-year transition period until October 2031.
The Fed members also raised their concerns about retail crime and rogue trade on the High Street and reiterated the particular priority the Fed places on enhancing resources for Neighbourhood Policing and Local Authority trading standards.
Archibald said: “It was an extremely positive meeting and I look forward to working with Vince and Fiona in the future. I hope to meet with them again in the Senedd at some point and will also try and stop by the shop when I am in Tenby in the future!”
Vince and Fiona Malone added: “We would like to thank Claire for visiting us and for engaging openly on the issues affecting our business and community. The ball is now in the hands of the Senedd to ensure that these concerns are acted upon.”

items.title: Crew Clothing warns on consumer confidence as profit stalls
items.summary: Crew Clothing has warned that it could suffer from a significant slowdown in consumer confidence, as the retailer saw profit stall last year. The high street clothes seller said it is bracing for a potential drop-off in spending, as inflation fears caused by the Iran war tighten shoppers’ budgets.  In a statement the firm said: [...]
items.body:
Crew Clothing warns on consumer confidence as profit stalls
Crew Clothing has warned that it could suffer from a significant slowdown in consumer confidence, as the retailer saw profit stall last year.
The high street clothes seller said it is bracing for a potential drop-off in spending, as inflation fears caused by the Iran war tighten shoppers’ budgets.
In a statement the firm said: “The retail landscape remains a challenging trading space for many.
“Although Crew’s customers have shown great resilience in the past, the business remains cognisant of potential slowdown in consumer spending as a result of rises in the cost of living and economic pressures.”
The retailer’s pre-tax profit remained flat at £25.5m in 2025, despite turnover jumping by a fifth to £151m. The firm’s cost of sales rose by eight per cent to £44m.
Crew Clothing said its website outperformed its high street business last year, as online sales jumped by 30 per cent, compared to 21 per cent growth in its stores.
Retailers have warned that the summer’s record temperatures drove shoppers away from high streets, though online sellers benefited from the extreme heat.
‘Middle England’s Ralph Lauren’
Crew Clothing’s consumer confidence warning comes as the retail industry ramps up pressure on the government to boost high street businesses at next month’s Budget.
Andy Burnham has suggested he could cut business rates bills for smaller shops, but large retailers have warned that the Prime Minister must not hike taxes for big shops to fund this move.
Retailers have also urged the government to roll back recent hikes to employer national insurance contributions and the minimum wage, promising they will hire more young people if the cost of employment falls.
Crew Clothing was founded by Devon-based windsurfing instructor Alistair Parker-Swift in 1993.
In 2017, Parker-Swift and private equity firm Livingbridge sold their stakes in the retailer to US-based clothing manufacturer Exquisite Apparel.
The clothing group is controlled by Menoshi ‘Michael’ Shina, who led a group of investors in the £22.6m takeover of suitmaker Moss Bros in 2020.
Former Crew Clothing chief executive David Butler, who quit in 2023, had described the retailer as “middle England’s Ralph Lauren” as he set out plans to open new stores in market towns and coastal resorts.

New global research also reveals that 63.2% of consumers have […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Global AI-first cloud communications platform Infobip predicts that around 193 million messages will be sent from businesses to consumers across Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2026 in the UK. That’s as AI and conversational channels transform how consumers discover products, receive offers and access support.
New global research also reveals that 63.2% of consumers have used an AI assistant or chatbot while shopping during the past 12 months.
Black Friday is no longer a single shopping event. Infobip’s research shows that globally, the shopping season now begins weeks earlier and continues through the entire customer journey. Nearly six in ten respondents will have started holiday shopping by early November, while only 19% wait until Black Friday week itself. This extended shopping window is creating new pressure for retailers to engage customers earlier, with better timing, more relevant offers and frictionless support across the channels consumers already use.
AI is becoming a central part of that journey. According to the research, 63.2% of global consumers have used an AI assistant or chatbot for shopping in the last 12 months, with 21.9% using one frequently. Among consumers willing to use AI for shopping, 73.4% would use it to compare products and 67.8% would use it to find deals matching their preferences.
The data also suggests that while email remains a dominant channel for deals and updates in the UK, conversational and mobile channels are becoming increasingly important for time-sensitive, personalised retail engagement. Rich Communication Services (RCS) are predicted to see the biggest increase in volume in the UK, by over 280% this Black Friday.
James Stokes, Head of UK and Nordics at Infobip, said: “Black Friday is no longer a single day or even a single week. It has become an extended conversation between consumers and brands, beginning with discovery and continuing through purchase, delivery and support. AI gives retailers the opportunity to make those conversations faster, more relevant and more personal. The winners will be the brands that understand when, where and how each customer wants to engage.”

St. Ewe Free Range Eggs is continuing to drive premiumisation within the egg category with the national launch of its Rich Yolk Luxuriously Large 10-pack, which will roll out to 244 Tesco stores from 21st September.
The launch comes as consumer demand for premium eggs continues to grow, with shoppers increasingly willing to pay more for quality. According to the latest NielsenIQ data, 10-pack eggs are now the fastest-growing format in the category by value (+20%), followed by 12-packs (+12.3%), highlighting a clear shift towards larger premium packs as household demand for eggs continues to increase.
At the same time, consumers are buying eggs more frequently than ever before. Nielsen Homescan data shows the average shopper now purchases eggs 17.3 times per year, while spending per shopping occasion has increased by 7.5% year-on-year, demonstrating continued investment in the category despite wider economic pressures.
The new Rich Yolk Luxuriously Large 10-pack has been developed for consumers looking for a premium everyday egg, offering rich golden yolks, larger eggs and the quality synonymous with the St. Ewe brand.
Anthony Frankland, Head of Retail at St. Ewe Free Range Eggs comments: “This is an exciting new launch for everyone at St. Ewe. As shopper purchasing behaviour continues to evolve, it’s important that we do the same and ensure our range reflects what consumers are looking for. The data shows a growing demand for premium, high-quality egg products in larger volumes, and that’s exactly what this launch delivers. I can’t wait to see the standout packaging on shelves in-store and online.”
Bex Tonks, CEO and Farmer at St. Ewe Free Range Eggs, said: “We’re seeing a real shift in the way consumers shop the egg category. People are buying eggs more often, and they’re increasingly choosing to invest in higher-quality products that deliver on taste, versatility and eating experience. The launch of our Rich Yolk Luxuriously Large 10-pack into Tesco is another important milestone for the brand and reflects the continued premiumisation we’re seeing across the category. Consumers are recognising the value of great-quality eggs and looking for products that elevate everyday meals, whether that’s breakfast, baking or cooking from scratch.”
The Tesco launch builds on continued momentum for the St. Ewe Rich Yolk range, which has become increasingly popular with shoppers looking for richer flavour, vibrant golden yolks and premium quality.
The listing also reinforces St. Ewe’s strategy of driving innovation and premium growth within the category while responding to changing consumer shopping habits.

items.title: Usdaw welcomes home secretary’s ‘continuing commitment’ to tackling retail crime
items.summary: Retail trade union Usdaw welcomed the speech to Labour’s annual conference in Liverpool by Shabana Mahmood, home secretary, where she highlighted Labour’s achievements on retail crime and the government’s continuing commitment to neighbourhood policing. As part of her address to delegates, Mahmood's said: “Across the… This story continues at Usdaw welcomes home secretary’s ‘continuing commitment’ to tackling retail crime Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
As part of her address to delegates, Mahmood’s said: “Across the country, certain crimes, particularly those that tear at the fabric of a local community are still too high. Like shop theft, which though now falling, is still far too high.
“To achieve fairness in every community, we need to do some things we know work, like neighbourhood policing. Which was hollowed out under the Conservative government but which we know cuts crime and deters criminality.
“I am proud to say that this government has put 3,800 more officers into neighbourhoods across the country.”
Commenting after the speech, Joanne Thomas – Usdaw general secretary, said: “We very much welcome Labour’s investment in neighbourhood policing, to help tackle crime and anti-social behaviour in communities and town centres.
“Usdaw’s latest interim survey results show the level of attacks on retail workers remains high. It is shocking that nearly three-quarters of those working in retail are regularly facing abuse from customers, with far too many experiencing threats and violence.
“This is a hugely important issue for our members, and they are saying loud and clear that enough is enough.
“Labour’s investment in more uniformed officer patrols in shopping areas and neighbourhoods adds to the government’s extensive action to tackle retail crime. The Crime and Policing Act will deliver a much-needed protection of shop workers’ law; end the indefensible £200 threshold for prosecuting shoplifters, which has effectively become an open invitation to retail criminals; along with Criminal Behaviour Orders.
“There is also new funding to tackle the organised criminals responsible for the increase in shoplifting.
“We continue to call on the government to urgently bring these new measures into force, to give the police the tools to deal with the problem and help protect retail workers.”

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Summer may be over, but for retailers now digging into how the season performed, a new analysis of ONS weekly retail footfall data offers a useful benchmark. The study uncovers the stability of week-to-week shopper numbers across the UK’s regions over summer, finding Scotland to have some of the biggest variations in footfall for the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Summer may be over, but for retailers now digging into how the season performed, a new analysis of ONS weekly retail footfall data offers a useful benchmark. The study uncovers the stability of week-to-week shopper numbers across the UK’s regions over summer, finding Scotland to have some of the biggest variations in footfall for the second year in a row
The research, from point of sale provider Epos Now, used the ONS/BT Active Intelligence weekly footfall figures for June-August 2025 and 2026 to compare differences in annual performance. The study then measured two factors for each UK region (aside from Northern Ireland) to assess how footfall is performing; how much weekly footfall values varied relative to their average level over the period (stability), and how footfall this summer compared to the 2023 levels ONS index against (growth).
Scotland sees biggest variations in footfall, but growth is high
Scotland’s weekly footfall varied by 6.55% on average in summer 2026 and 6.22% in summer 2025. Footfall started summer 2026 slightly below its 2023 baseline before climbing to 20% above it by mid-August, which could have been driven by the likes of Edinburgh Fringe Festival, as one possibility. However, looking at how footfall is performing against 2023 averages that the ONS index against, on average Scottish retail saw weekly footfall increase by 5.49%. In comparison, in 2025 Scotland’s footfall grew by 2.84% on average each week over summer.
London’s footfall booms
Looking at footfall in London, the region’s weekly footfall was 17.5% above the 2023 average. The region also had fairly stable figures, with footfall varying by 3.44% away from its summer average, and was at its highest through 29th June – 19th July.
East of England’s footfall shows stability
The East of England demonstrated some of the most stable weekly footfall figures, with it varying weekly by 2.4% on its summer average. Alongside this, the region also saw growth of 4.71% on weekly footfall from 2023’s indexed average. However, this is down from the 7.3% weekly average footfall growth the region saw in 2025.
North East, North West, and Yorkshire show declines
Despite having low variations in weekly footfall, the North East, North West, and Yorkshire recorded declines in weekly footfall against their 2023 baseline through summer 2026. The North West saw average weekly footfall fall by 2.6% from 2023’s average, whilst the North East saw a 4% decline and Yorkshire a 5% decrease.
| Region | 2026 variation | 2026 Average weekly footfall vs 2023 baseline | 2025 variation | 2025 Average weekly footfall vs 2023 baseline | 
| UK total | 2.56% | 5.69% | 2.47% | 3.45% | 
| England | 2.54% | 6.02% | 2.56% | 3.48% | 
| East of England | 2.42% | 4.71% | 2.45% | 7.25% | 
| North East | 2.62% | -4.16% | 2.82% | 0.35% | 
| North West | 2.80% | -2.61% | 3.26% | 0.41% | 
| Yorkshire and The Humber | 2.81% | -5.37% | 3.69% | -0.49% | 
| East Midlands | 2.88% | 1.54% | 3.39% | 4.17% | 
| West Midlands | 3.10% | 1.40% | 3.28% | 4.06% | 
| South East | 3.33% | 2.56% | 2.30% | 2.54% | 
| London | 3.44% | 17.53% | 4.13% | 5.13% | 
| Wales | 4.22% | 1.03% | 3.34% | 5.04% | 
| South West | 4.49% | 1.06% | 3.35% | 3.32% | 
| Scotland | 6.55% | 5.49% | 6.22% | 2.84% | 
Jacyn Heavens, CEO at Epos Now, comments, “Footfall across retail has seen fluctuations through the summer months caused by extreme heat and seasonal sporting events, however, the number of regions showing growth on the 2023 averages that the ONS benchmark against shows promising hope for highstreets, retail parks and the like. As we move into the golden quarter of the year for retail, it’s important that retailers focus on understanding and using their real time sales data to forecast for the likes of footfall, stock, and staffing.”

items.title: Selfridges boss calls on Burnham to restore tax-free shopping for tourists as group returns to profit
items.summary: André Maeder, chief executive of Selfridges, said the performance demonstrated the retailer's 'resilience amid a challenging economic and retail environment'.
items.body:
Selfridges boss calls on Burnham to restore tax-free shopping for tourists as group returns to profit
Selfridges returned to profit in its last fiscal year as its boss reiterated his call to restore tax-free shopping for international visitors.
The high-end department store chain said stronger in-store sales and tighter cost control helped it deliver a sharp improvement in its annual performance.
The business posted a pre-tax profit of £13million for the 52 weeks to January 3, 2026, against a £15.9million loss a year earlier.
Revenue rose seven per cent to £830.8million, while the firm's operating profit jumped 88 per cent to £79.7million as it benefited from higher margins and increased sales across its stores.
The results represent a marked turnaround for Selfridges, which last year reported its fifth consecutive annual pre-tax loss after revenues fell to £775million. The prior reporting period covered 48 weeks, rather than 52.
André Maeder, chief executive of Selfridges, said the performance demonstrated the retailer’s 'resilience amid a challenging economic and retail environment'.
Pressure on the PM: The boss of Selfridges wants the government to resume tax-free shopping for international visitors
He said those challenges had been 'made more difficult by policy choices, such as the abolition of tax-free shopping for international visitors.'
He added: 'We are therefore hugely encouraged to see this back on the political agenda and urge the government, under new prime minister Andy Burnham, to bring back tax-free shopping, boosting high streets and unlocking growth across the whole of the UK.'
The VAT Retail Export Scheme allowed overseas visitors to get a VAT refund on items they had bought in the UK and took home in their luggage.
The scheme was scrapped for non-EU visitors under the previous Conservative government in 2021, while it was also not extended for EU visitors.
Now, the Conservatives have said they would reintroduce tax-free shopping for international visitors.
Leader of the Conservatives, Kemi Badenoch, who was a Treasury minister when the tax relief was abolished, said businesses were being 'let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away'.
But Labour accused the Conservatives of 'a spectacular U-turn'.
Research by the Centre for Economics and Business Research this month said fully restoring tax-free shopping for tourists could attract up to 2.35million extra visitors and generate £4.1billion in extra spending.
The report also estimated that for every £1 of VAT refunded, this could generate £1.54 in other taxes.
Andy Burnham is facing pressure from large UK retail and luxury brands, like Burberry and Mulberry, to reintroduce tax-free shopping for international visitors by bringing back the VAT refund scheme that was abolished in 2021.

items.body:
Opening on 29th September 2026, the new store will bring the brand’s signature luxury style to Trafford Centre, reinforcing continued retailer confidence in one of the UK’s leading retail and leisure destinations.
Founded in Stoke-on-Trent in 1924, Belstaff is known for clothing designed for a life in motion, with its signature waxed cotton and leather outerwear at the heart of the brand. Its arrival at Trafford Centre will bring the brand’s enduring icons and seasonal collections to customers from across Greater Manchester and the wider North West.
Occupying 900 sq ft, the new store will showcase a selection of Belstaff clothing, outerwear and accessories through the brand’s ‘Future Garage’ concept, which was conceived in collaboration with Scandinavian architecture and interior design studio Specific Generic. The concept draws on Belstaff’s motoring heritage while reimagining it for a new era. Its clean, minimalist interior will combine modular fixtures, stainless steel rails and digital displays, balancing old and new to create a flexible, contemporary retail environment.
A dedicated evergreen fixture will spotlight Belstaff’s iconic waxed-cotton and leather pieces, using material details and key dates to reveal the stories behind them. Blending the functional language of a modern garage with references to Belstaff’s manufacturing legacy, the concept will create a distinctive setting within Trafford Centre’s premium fashion line-up.
The opening builds on Trafford Centre’s continued leasing momentum, including recently announced lettings and expansions involving high-profile retailers such as Suitsupply, lululemon, Garage and UNIQLO. This activity reflects sustained occupier confidence in the destination’s performance and long-term investment strategy.
Kate Pearson, portfolio leasing director at Pradera, said: “Belstaff’s arrival strengthens Trafford Centre’s premium fashion line-up with one of Britain’s most distinctive heritage brands. The signing also demonstrates the momentum behind our leasing strategy and the continued confidence in Trafford Centre as a destination where brands can reach new audiences and grow their presence across the region.”
Lee Elliott, commercial director at Belstaff said “This is an exciting new opening for Belstaff, which has a historic connection to the North of England – its founders Eli Belovich and Harry Grosberg first conceived the idea for the brand in nearby Manchester. As Belstaff’s sixth full price store in England, it’s perfectly placed to better service its loyal customers in the region, while welcoming new ones.”

items.body:
Echo Falls is doubling down on one of its biggest launches of the year, taking Blue Raspberry into a new 275ml RTD format as the brand looks to turn the flavour’s runaway success into an even bigger retail opportunity.
A first for Echo Falls, the 275ml format will roll out across ASDA, Morrisons, Co-op, as well as B&M and Savers, following a blockbuster start for Blue Raspberry 750ml. More than two million bottles have sold into wholesale and convenience since launch, while the brand’s campaign has generated 9.7million views and reached 2.8million consumers – giving the new RTD the advantage of arriving with both awareness and appetite already firmly established.
The new format is the next step in growing that opportunity. While 750ml has established Blue Raspberry in the take-home fixture, 275ml brings the flavour into more immediate, impulse-led missions, spanning festivals, events and social occasions, with a ready-to-enjoy format that can work across both the chiller and ice bucket. Its electric-blue liquid carries through the standout of the original, giving the smaller bottle the same instant recognition that has helped fuel Blue Raspberry’s success to date.
Blue Raspberry was developed as a deliberately different proposition for BWS, tapping into the flavour, colour and occasion-led choices increasingly shaping drinks discovery and borrowing from behaviour already evident across RTDs and flavoured spirits. Its performance since launch points to the scale of the opportunity when those more familiar, accessible cues are brought into a category that can still be difficult for younger adult shoppers to navigate.
Taran Dhillon, Echo Falls brand manager at Vinarchy, said: “One of the most encouraging things about Blue Raspberry has been that its success hasn’t been confined to one channel or one type of shopper mission. We’ve seen it perform through convenience and grocery, while the consumer response has shown us the flavour has a life well beyond the weekly shop.
“We already know people want Blue Raspberry; now we can put it into a format that changes where and how it can compete. It means we can take a proposition that has performed incredibly strongly in take-home and put it shoulder-to-shoulder with the RTDs and flavoured drinks already winning more immediate drinking occasions. The response has moved quickly, so it makes sense that we do too!”
Blue Raspberry is now available at ASDA, Morrisons, Co-op, B&M and Savers with an RRP of £3.25

items.body:
Heinz Beanz has today announced a new partnership with Team Grassroots to support youth football teams across the UK, helping ensure the next generation of players have everything they need to get match ready.
For grassroots teams, matchday can be tricky. Many teams rely entirely on volunteers, and on a busy weekend you’re lucky if there’s someone available to run the line.
That’s why Heinz is partnering with Team Grassroots, one of the UK’s leading independent organisations supporting community football. Together, they are helping make matchdays a little easier for youth teams across the UK by ensuring they have a Proper Warm Up.
As part of the partnership, Heinz will distribute more than 10,000 training bibs, 8,000 footballs and 1,000 ball carriers to grassroots youth teams for players aged 6 and above across the country.
By providing essential equipment where it is needed most, Heinz and Team Grassroots are supporting the coaches, volunteers, parents and players who are at the heart of the grassroots game.
Why Heinz?
For generations, Heinz Beanz have been a familiar part of footballer’s routines, from muddy Sunday mornings to the very highest levels of the game, including some of England’s biggest stars. For the next generation of Britain’s footballing stars, a pre-
match helping of Beanz on Wholemeal Toast can provide a range of nutrients including vital carbs, fibre, and protein for the game they love. Which means while they’re hungry to play, they won’t be playing hungry.
Alessandra de Druille, head of meals, Kraft Heinz, said: “For decades, Beanz have played a memorable role in fuelling the next generation. That’s especially true in football culture across Britain. Whether it’s a quick breakfast before a Sunday morning kick-off or a pre-match ritual followed by some of the country’s biggest players, Beanz have long been part of the journey of fuelling the future, and grassroots football is where that journey begins for so many. Through our partnership with Team Grassroots, we’re proud to help provide the equipment teams need to give young players the best possible start.”
Paul Kirton, Founder, Team Grassroots, said: “The Proper Warm Up campaign is a brilliant fit for grassroots football. Matchdays are powered by volunteers, parents, coaches and players who give up their time in all weathers, so partnering with Heinz – a brand already synonymous with warmth, comfort and bringing people together, feels completely natural. It’s a fun, authentic partnership that understands the grassroots game and gives something meaningful back to the people who make it happen every week.”

items.title: Revive VAT-free shopping to boost high streets, Selfridges urges Burnham
items.summary: Selfridges has called on Andy Burnham to reinstate VAT-free shopping for international tourists as part of his push to revive British high streets and boost regional growth. The luxury department store chain hit out at then-Chancellor Rishi Sunak’s decision to abolish VAT-free shopping in 2021, adding that it is “encouraged” to see the policy back [...]
items.body:
Revive VAT-free shopping to boost high streets, Selfridges urges Burnham
Selfridges has called on Andy Burnham to reinstate VAT-free shopping for international tourists as part of his push to revive British high streets and boost regional growth.
The luxury department store chain hit out at then-Chancellor Rishi Sunak’s decision to abolish VAT-free shopping in 2021, adding that it is “encouraged” to see the policy back on the agenda.
André Maeder, Selfridges Group’s chief executive, said that “difficult retail and macroeconomic environments” have been made “more difficult by policy choices, such as the abolition of tax-free shopping for international visitors.”
He added: “We are therefore hugely encouraged to see this back on the political agenda and urge the government under new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, to bring back tax-free shopping, boosting high streets and unlocking growth across the whole of the UK.”
Burnham is facing significant pressure from luxury brands, including listed fashion house Burberry and bagmaker Mulberry, to reinstate tax-free shopping for tourists.
Earlier this month, business leaders welcomed the Conservatives’ pledge to bring back the policy if they re-enter government.
Writing in City AM, shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith said the return to tax-free shopping would allow the UK’s “retailers, hotels, restaurants and attractions to put their best foot forward”.
Bosses from hospitality and retail giants including Fortnum & Mason, Fullers, Claridge’s – alongside TV chef Angela Hartnett – praised the move.
They said: “As some of the leading businesses in tourism, retail and hospitality, we welcome this pro-growth, pro-jobs announcement from Kemi Badenoch and her team.
“With its heritage and the quality of our products and service, Britain is well placed to compete with the world’s finest destinations.”
Selfridges online sales slip
The comments came as Selfridges posted an 88 per cent jump in profit to £24m last year, as revenue across its four UK locations grew by seven per cent to £831m.
Selfridges said its profit growth was helped by its shift in focus towards selling higher-margin products. Revenue across the group, including sales from brand partners, came in at £1.6bn.
The group’s push towards selling more profitable products caused a dip in its online sales, but the department store chain highlighted its efforts to improve the experience at its sites in London, Birmingham and Manchester.
Selfridges was sold by the billionaire Weston family, who own Primark and AB Foods, for £4bn in 2022. Thailand-based retail conglomerate Central Group owns 60 per cent of the company while Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund owns 40 per cent.

items.body:
Australian consumer electronics retailer JB Hi-Fi taps Vusion digital shelf-edge tech across its stores
Vusion has announced a new roll-out initiative at Australian retailer JB Hi-Fi’s stores. Under the agreement, JB Hi-Fi plans to deploy Vusion’s digital shelf-edge technology in Australia following a pilot phase, as well as a full roll-out across its New Zealand store network.
“We are focused on innovation that delivers efficiencies to our store operations and supports our teams in serving customers,” says Cameron Trainor, MD at JB Hi-Fi Australia. “Our collaboration with Vusion gives us a scalable technology platform to support store teams, strengthen execution and advance the next phase of our strategy.”
“We are very proud to support JB Hi-Fi as it takes this important step toward a more connected store network,” says Pierre Demoures, SEVP & COO at Vusion. “Australia is a key market for Vusion and JB Hi-Fi is one of the region’s most distinctive retailers. This agreement shows how connected store infrastructure can help leading retailers modernise operations while preserving the store experience that makes them unique.”
Through Vusion’s native integration with Cisco Meraki, JB Hi-Fi will connect the former’s platform to the wireless infrastructure already deployed in its stores, with a view to reducing additional infrastructure requirements while simplifying roll-out and helping limit both operational costs and the environmental footprint of the deployment.
So hot right now
Vusion is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.title: Retailers keep prices low despite rising cost pressures
items.summary: Shop price inflation decreased to 1.4% year on year in September, against growth of 1.5% in August, according to the BRC-NIQ Shop Price Monitor. This is above the 3-month average of 1.3%. Food inflation decreased to 2.5% year on year, against growth of 2.8% in… This story continues at Retailers keep prices low despite rising cost pressures Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
This is above the 3-month average of 1.3%.
Food inflation decreased to 2.5% year on year, against growth of 2.8% in August while non-food inflation decreased to 0.8%.
Fresh food inflation decreased to 2.6% year on year in September, against growth of 3.0% in August and ambient food inflation decreased to 2.2%.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the BRC, said: “Shop price inflation edged down this month, with food inflation falling as competition between retailers continued to deliver value for shoppers.
“Promotions helped bring down meat and dairy prices, though poor harvests across Europe pushed up fruit prices and high global commodity prices kept chocolate and confectionery prices elevated.
“In non-food, strong discounting reduced the cost of back-to-school essentials, including books, stationery, footwear and electricals.
“Retailers have absorbed wave after wave of extra costs, but there is a limit to what businesses can shoulder. With higher business rates set to hit in April, alongside rising employment costs, energy bills and packaging taxes, the Budget is a fork in the road.
“The chancellor can help keep prices down by freezing the rates rise and removing shops from the business rates surtax, or risk pushing even more costs onto consumers.”
Mike Watkins, head of retailer and business insight, NIQ, said: “Shoppers reset spend in September and sales growth slowed after the hot summer. So many retailers have maintained promotions, and some have introduced price cuts to help drive demand, all of which is helping to keep inflation lower than a year ago.
“Q4 is expected to bring tighter household budgeting so retailers will still need to absorb cost increases wherever possible.”

items.body:
Empowering the people at the till: how modern Point of Sale is transforming the store experience
There is a conversation happening in retail boardrooms and conferences around the globe, and it goes something like this: "We've invested heavily in digital. We've optimised our supply chain. We've consistently delivered a product range that resonates with our customers. So why does the total experience with our brand still feel lacking?"
The answer, more often than not, comes down to one thing: the legacy tools used by many retail store employees today are simply not fit for purpose, resulting in a store experience that falls short of current expectations.
For decades, the PoS has been treated as a glorified cash register - a transaction processing machine bolted to a counter, running software that looks like it belongs in a 1990s IT department.
Retailers have poured investment into customer facing digital technologies whilst leaving their store colleagues to wrestle with clunky interfaces, incomplete customer data and siloed systems that cannot talk to each other. The result is a workforce that is perpetually on the back foot, unable to deliver the kind of connected, knowledgeable service that today's shoppers now see as table stakes.
But the tide is turning. A new generation of PoS solutions - cloud native, mobile first and built with the colleague and customer in mind - is beginning to close the gap between what retailers promise and what their frontline teams can actually deliver.
Perhaps most significant about this shift to modern PoS is the virtuous cycle it creates: when retailers invest in their store staff through better technology, customers benefit almost immediately.
Colleague experience is customer experience
There is a growing recognition across the retail industry that the quality of the customer experience is directly shaped by the experience of the colleagues delivering it, and that technology plays a central role.
Every time a customer asks whether an item is available in a different size at a different store, every time they want to know their loyalty points balance, every time they need a return processed without drama - in that moment, everything hinges on the tools the colleague has in their hands.
When those tools are inadequate, store employees cannot do their jobs well. They make apologetic faces and disappear to the back of the house to check stock. They ask customers to wait whilst they call another store. They say, "The system won't let me do that." None of this is the employee's fault. It is a technology failure that plays out as a people failure, and the customer, rightly or wrongly, blames the brand.
Modern PoS changes this dynamic fundamentally. When a store colleague has a device with real-time inventory visibility across the entire network and detailed product information, including ratings and reviews, they stop being a transaction processor and start being a trusted advisor.
When the PoS surfaces a customer's purchase history, preferences and loyalty rewards at the moment of engagement, the store employee can have a personalised conversation rather than starting from zero. When the checkout process is fast, flexible and frictionless, the colleague can focus on the human side of the interaction rather than battling the technology.
Reducing friction is not a small thing
One of the most significant yet often underestimated benefits of modern PoS is how dramatically it reduces cognitive load for store employees. Legacy systems often require staff to memorise arcane key combinations, navigate menus three or four levels deep, or switch between multiple applications or devices to complete a single transaction. This is not just inefficient - it is genuinely stressful, particularly during peak trading periods when queues are long and every second counts.
Good technology should make hard things easy. Mobile first PoS platforms, designed with intuitive interfaces that mirror the mobile apps colleagues use in their personal lives, can be learned in minutes rather than hours or weeks. This has major implications for onboarding and seasonal staffing - two persistent pain points for retail operations.
When a new team member can be productive on day one rather than day ten, the entire store benefits. Experienced colleagues are not pulled away to oversee training. Managers can focus on coaching rather than troubleshooting. And importantly, customers do not have to suffer through uncertain, hesitant checkouts from someone still finding their feet.
The shift to mobile first PoS also liberates colleagues from the constraints of the fixed till. Colleagues can approach customers on the shopfloor, assist them and complete the transaction right there, without ever directing them to a queue. This not only improves throughput; it fundamentally changes the nature of the interaction from transactional to relational.
Insight at the point of human connection
Perhaps the most transformative capability that modern PoS brings to the shopfloor is unified customer data - delivered at precisely the right moment, in a format that is actually usable.
Retailers have spent years building rich customer profiles through loyalty programmes, e-commerce platforms and CRM (customer relationship management) systems. Yet historically, this data has not been made available in a way that store colleagues could easily access "in the moment" when serving shoppers.
The employee interacting with a customer in-store had no idea that person had browsed three pairs of trainers online that morning, that they had £45 in unredeemed loyalty rewards, or that they had returned two items in the past month that turned out to be the wrong size. All of that context was invisible, and so the colleague was flying blind.
Modern PoS solutions break down these walls. When customer data flows seamlessly from all touchpoints to the Point of Sale, colleagues gain a 360-degree view of each shopper. They can acknowledge loyal customers meaningfully.
They can make product recommendations grounded in actual purchase behaviour rather than guesswork. They can resolve issues - "I see you had trouble with sizing recently; let me help you find something that will work." - in ways that feel thoughtful rather than scripted.
This kind of service does not just satisfy customers; it builds genuine loyalty. Research consistently shows that shoppers who receive personalised, knowledgeable service in-store are more likely to return, to spend more and to recommend the brand to others. The return on investment for getting this right is not a rounding error - it is a commercial advantage.
When store employees trust the system, customers trust the brand
There is a subtler benefit to modern PoS that does not always make it into the ROI calculations but deserves to be talked about nonetheless: colleague confidence.
Working with technology that works, that is reliable, fast and does what it promises, changes how employees carry themselves on the shopfloor. When store staff know that the inventory data they are quoting is accurate, they make promises with conviction rather than hedging.
When they know that all transactions, even complicated ones, including mixed cart, endless aisle or in-store returns for online orders - can be handled with ease, they approach it without the anxiety that often creeps in with legacy platforms.
That confidence is palpable to customers. It is the difference between a colleague who says, "We have that in size ten at a nearby store - I can order it for you and have it delivered to your home" and one who says, "I think we might have it, but the system isn't always accurate, so…"
Retailers sometimes underestimate how much colleague confidence shapes customer perception. Shoppers pick up on uncertainty and hesitation. They interpret it, often unconsciously, as a signal about the brand. Building technology that colleagues can genuinely rely on is therefore not just an operational investment; it is a brand investment.
The modern PoS imperative
All of this points to something the retail industry needs to confront more directly: investing in modern store technology is not a cost of doing business - it is a strategic priority.
For too long, the IT budget conversation in retail has centred on the digital domain - the website, the app, digital marketing. The store has been chronically underfunded, with staff routinely handed the technological equivalent of a blunt instrument and expected to perform surgery with it. The consequences show up in staff turnover, in customer satisfaction, and ultimately in revenue.
The good news is that the business case for modern PoS has never been clearer. Frictionless transactions mean higher throughput and lower queue abandonment. Better data served up directly in the PoS UI results in higher conversion rates and larger basket sizes. Improved staff experience means lower turnover and fewer resources spent recruiting and onboarding.
And a genuinely excellent in-store experience means something that no website can replicate: the kind of human connection that keeps customers coming back - not because they have to but because they want to.
Aptos ONE: A modern PoS for modern store experiences
Aptos ONE is more than just a modern Point of Sale - it's a powerful platform that enhances every aspect of the customer journey by empowering store employees.
Cloud-native and mobile-first, Aptos ONE PoS is trusted by some of the world's most recognised brands, including The North Face, Skechers, and New Balance, to deliver exceptional experiences, streamline operations and future-proof their retail business.

items.body:
JD Sports updates on RFID programme as Germany goes live and 1,000 stores milestone is reached
Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, has taken to social media to provide an update on the retailer’s RFID programme, which involves various countries and thousands of stores.
In a LinkedIn post, McGrath said: “This week, our final country goes live with RFID, Germany. And with that, everything we directly control will be live for phase one of our RFID programme. When I look back at what we’ve achieved, the numbers are pretty incredible: 1,000 stores directly launched in 14 months. And across the wider global group, working alongside our counterparts around the world: 2,700 stores live out of 4,800 in that same period, 192 stores a month!”
He added: “But the numbers only tell part of this story. RFID isn’t just about scanners, tags and technology. It’s about changing behaviours, processes and mindsets. We’ve done things that were uncomfortable. Challenged established ways of working. Asked people to rethink processes they’d used for years. And, most importantly, brought people with us on the journey. And we haven't done that alone.”
Working with its brand partners, JD Sports has also helped take RFID coverage from around 40% of product to 73% and that number continues to grow as more brands recognise the potential RFID offers across their own retail formats and supply chains.
“The more products that carry that digital identity, the more powerful the data and the opportunity becomes for stores, supply chains, inventory visibility and ultimately the customer experience. But none of this happens because of just technology. It happens because of people. I’m incredibly proud of my small but hugely impactful team. The commitment, energy and determination you’ve shown throughout this roll-out has been exceptional,” McGrath commented.
“And a massive thank you to our in-country champions, the people who visited stores, stood alongside colleagues, solved problems, supported teams and helped turn a technology roll-out into real operational change. You were the ones who helped make it stick.”
McGrath concluded: “From the first proof of concept to thousands of stores now operating with RFID, and from 40% to 73% of products tagged, this has been one hell of a journey. Germany, you’re up. One more country. One more milestone.”

Musgrave ramps up Irish quick commerce push with Snappy Technologies Order Aggregation platform
Musgrave Northern Ireland, part of the Musgrave Group, an Irish convenience retail, wholesale and food service business, whose brands include SuperValu and Centra, has expanded its rapid grocery delivery offering through a partnership with Snappy Technologies, powered by the company’s Order Aggregation (OA) platform.
This connects its stores with leading rapid delivery marketplaces, with five company owned SuperValu and Centra stores across Northern Ireland now available on Just Eat and Uber Eats. A further 13 company owned stores are expected to launch in the next phase of the roll-out across September.
With the OA platform, Musgrave can manage orders from multiple online marketplaces through a single, streamlined solution. The technology enables retailers to manage key functions including orders, menus, promotions and stock across multiple channels.
Head of Operational Support for Musgrave Northern Ireland, Barry McVeigh, says: "We're always looking at ways to make shopping easier and more convenient for our customers, and this partnership with Snappy Technologies is an important step in that journey. By connecting our SuperValu and Centra stores to leading delivery platforms such as Just Eat and Uber Eats, we're giving customers greater flexibility in how they shop, whether that's picking up essentials or ordering groceries for the week ahead.”
“The technology also provides a streamlined solution for our store teams, allowing us to manage orders efficiently across multiple channels while maintaining the high standards of service our customers expect. We're excited to expand the roll-out across Northern Ireland in the coming months as demand for rapid grocery delivery continues to grow."
Andy Batt, VP of Snappy Technologies, says: “Musgrave is taking an ambitious approach to q-commerce, and we’re excited to support its strategy. The rapid growth of q-commerce is creating a significant opportunity for retailers but reaching customers across multiple different marketplaces can also introduce additional operational complexity. Our OA platform is designed to remove this complexity, giving retailers a simpler way to manage marketplace activity while expanding digital reach.”

items.body:
Amazon the most visible major online marketplace across leading generative AI platforms, new research
Amazon is the most visible major online marketplace across leading generative AI platforms, according to new analysis from Onclusive examining how e-commerce brands appear in responses generated by ChatGPT and Perplexity. The study found that Amazon accounted for 19.3% of marketplace share of voice, ahead of Walmart at 14%, Alibaba at 12.6%, Shopify at 11.6% and eBay at 11.1%.
Temu recorded a share of voice of 9.7%, followed by MercadoLibre at 9.2% and Etsy at 8.2%. European marketplaces Zalando and CDiscount recorded 3.9% and 0.5% respectively.
The findings highlight significant differences in how frequently major e-commerce platforms are surfaced by generative AI tools, as consumers increasingly use AI engines to research brands, products and online shopping options. Newer platforms are already competing for AI visibility against more established players, Temu’s 9.7% share of voice is comparable to Shopify and eBay.
LLM visibility - share of voice
- Amazon 19.3%
- Walmart 14%
- Alibaba 12.6%
- Shopify 11.6%
- eBay 11.1%
- Temu 9.7%
- MercadoLibre 9.2%
- Etsy 8.2%
- Zalando 3.9%
- CDiscount 0.5%
Share of voice measures a brand’s visibility relative to competitors within the scope of the analysis, based on the frequency with which each marketplace was mentioned across AI generated responses. Amazon also achieved the highest average prominence score, at 92%, compared with 84% for Walmart. Prominence measures how early a brand first appears within an AI-generated response, with a higher score indicating that the brand tends to be mentioned closer to the beginning of the answer.
The analysis also suggests that visibility within generative AI is closely associated with brands’ wider media presence. Marketplaces with greater volumes of traditional media coverage generally also recorded higher LLM visibility. Amazon ranked first across both measures, with a 19.3% share of AI visibility and 16.4 million media mentions, while Walmart ranked second for AI visibility at 14% alongside 5.6 million media mentions.
Christophe Asselin, Senior Insights Manager at Onclusive, says: “Generative AI now forms another layer of brand discovery alongside traditional search, social media and other digital channels. What stands out from this analysis is how quickly a new hierarchy of brand visibility is forming within generative AI. The major marketplaces are not appearing equally, and the gap between the most and least visible brands is already significant.”
“For businesses, the challenge is no longer simply whether they appear in AI generated answers, but how consistently they are surfaced, how prominently they feature and how they compare with competitors. As more consumers use AI tools to research brands, products and services, that visibility is likely to become an increasingly important part of the digital discovery landscape.”

items.body:
Subscription benchmarks 2026: the best retention tool is a working billing system
By George Kapernaros, Founder of YOCTO, a retention agency for DTC and subscription brands. Figures are first-party data measured across 100+ DTC and subscription accounts over the first eight months of 2026, with every rate recomputed from raw platform counts on one set of definitions.
We tested which number in our data best predicts whether a subscriber is still there deep into the relationship.
It was not the discount. It was not the checkout design, or the size of the programme, or any marketing measure we tried.
It was whether the card clears on the first attempt.
The Leak Nobody Budgets For
First-attempt payment success has a median of 86.0%. At the typical brand one scheduled charge in seven fails before retention gets a say. At the weakest it is closer to one in five.
What separates brands is what happens next. Recovery within the first retry cycle runs from 28.1% at the worst to 64.1% at the best.
Same failed card, more than double the rescues. The entire difference lives in settings the customer never sees: when retries fire, whether card details update automatically, what the reminder says and when it arrives.
It is unglamorous configuration work, and by our numbers it outperforms anything you could send instead.
Why Churn Benchmarks Cannot Show You This
A subscription puts the same question to the customer every time it bills. A brand shipping weekly asks about fifty times a year. A brand shipping quarterly asks four.
In our data, billing frequency tracks annual churn closely. The weekly brand will always look worse on a calendar, not because it keeps customers less well, but because it asks more often.
Annual churn across these accounts runs from 26.8% to 81.4% once pauses are counted as churn. That range says as much about billing calendars as it does about retention, which is why we stopped leading with it.
Count Orders, Not Months
Counted by order, every brand faces the same test, because every order is a decision. The median shares still active are:
- 3rd order: 77.0%
- 4th order: 53.3%
- 5th order: 41.0%
- 6th order: 34.1%
Switching to this measure reverses the league table. Food and beverage brands post the worst annual churn of the three industries measured, at a 63.6% median, and the best long-run retention, keeping 46.3% of subscribers to a sixth order.
Supplements and wellness brands sit mid-table on churn and keep 21.5%. The calendar had been marking the food brands down for billing often.
Two Things Worth Doing This Week
Pull your first-attempt success rate before briefing another campaign. If it sits below 86%, or your first-cycle recovery is under 40%, that is a larger and faster win than anything in the content calendar.
Judge retention by orders survived. Compare only against brands on your own billing rhythm, and treat any calendar-based benchmark as a comparison of schedules rather than of retention.
Full percentile ranges for every metric above, plus the definitions used, are in our subscription e-commerce statistics report.
