items.body:
An in-depth look at the best tattoo shop PoS system out there on the market today
Running a tattoo studio means juggling far more than the needle. On any given day you are taking deposits, chasing no-shows, splitting tips and commissions between artists, logging consent forms, keeping jewelry and aftercare stock on the shelf, and still trying to actually get paid without a stack of mismatched apps. A good tattoo shop PoS system pulls those jobs into one place - payments, booking, client records, and reporting - so the front desk runs itself and the artists can focus on the work.
The trouble is that "PoS" means very different things depending on who is selling it. Some tools are booking calendars with a card reader attached. Others are full retail engines that happen to have an appointments tab. This roundup looks at five platforms worth putting on your shortlist, what each one is genuinely built for, and where each tends to fit best.
This is an editorial overview based on publicly available information from each provider, not a hands-on review. It's intended as a starting point for comparing your options - always check the current features, pricing, and terms directly with each company before you commit.
1. Vibe Retail - a true retail POS tuned for the studio counter
Vibe Retail is a cloud-based point-of-sale platform built for modern retail businesses, and it earns the top spot here for studios that sell as much across the counter as they do at the chair. Where many tattoo tools start life as a booking calendar, Vibe starts as a genuine PoS and inventory engine and layers the studio workflow on top - which is what makes it worth weighing up as a tattoo shop PoS system rather than a scheduling app with payments bolted on.
On the studio side, it lets you assign specific rooms, stations, and artists to bookings, send consent forms alongside appointment reminders, and protect revenue with built-in no-show policies. Commission structures are configurable per artist, with each service transaction automatically attributed to the right team member. The retail side is where it pulls ahead: inventory for aftercare, merchandise, and piercing jewelry, with custom variants for colors, lengths, and sizing, plus low-stock alerts and reordering.
Published pricing runs from $19/month (Essential) to $97/month (Pro, the tier that unlocks appointments and staff management) and $1,399/month (Ultimate). Onboarding includes a dedicated migration specialist, and it runs on existing tablets, desktops, and card readers.
Best for: studios that also run a real retail counter - jewellery, aftercare, merch - and want one system for both.
Standout feature: retail-grade inventory with per-variant tracking, sitting alongside artist-level commission attribution.
2. Square - the low barrier all-rounder
Square is one of the most widely used payment tools in the trade, and for good reason: it is quick to start, familiar to clients, and free to trial. For tattoo and piercing shops, Square combines an online booking site with drag-and-drop scheduling that lets you colour code and assign specific stations and artists to bookings, plus cancellation and no-show policies, waitlists, and automated confirmations and reminders.
Payments are its strong suit. You can take mobile payments straight from a phone with no extra hardware, and it supports tap, chip, card-on-file, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App Pay, and Afterpay, with customisable tipping at checkout. Team management, payroll, inventory for retail and aftercare, and email and text campaigns for promotions and aftercare are all part of the wider platform, and hardware options run from the Square Handheld up to the Square Register.
Square publishes a free trial, and a custom priced Square Pro tier for businesses processing more than $250,000 a year; most day-to-day cost comes from per-transaction processing, so confirm current rates for your volume.
Best for: solo artists and smaller studios that want to be up and running today with minimal setup.
Standout feature: genuinely no-hardware mobile payments, useful for conventions, guest spots, and pop-ups.
3. Lightspeed - retail depth for merch-heavy shops
Lightspeed positions itself as an all-in-one piercing and tattoo shop PoS solution, and its heritage is retail, so inventory is where it shines. It offers real-time stock tracking across channels, custom tags, categories, and product variants, reorder points and low stock alerts, and multi-vendor purchase orders - handy for a studio that carries a deep range of jewelry, needles, ink, and aftercare and wants tight control over reordering.
Beyond stock, Lightspeed covers point of sale, appointment scheduling with online and in-person booking, customer management, and employee management with payroll integration. Payments run through the platform with credit, debit, and mobile support, PCI compliance, and end-to-end encryption, advertised with "competitive rates with no hidden costs or installation fees." Marketing is built in too, with automated email and SMS campaigns for promotions, reminders, and loyalty, plus customer segmentation and reporting you can slice by time, location, and customer type.
Lightspeed does not publish pricing on its tattoo and piercing page; it offers a free trial and invites you to talk to an expert for a quote.
Best for: established or multi-location studios with a serious retail footprint and complex inventory.
Standout feature: deep, multi-vendor inventory management with purchase orders and reorder points.
4. DaySmart Body Art - the body art vertical specialist
DaySmart Body Art is purpose-built for the body-art trade and markets itself as an all-in-one studio management solution to help shops "ditch the pen and paper." Its focus is the client relationship and the calendar rather than the retail counter. Online appointment booking is front and centre, backed by an appointment reminder system built to cut no-shows, two-way texting, and integrated payment technology to speed up checkout.
The compliance side is a genuine strength for tattoo and piercing work: digital consent and release forms, plus secure client data and purchase history. Around that sit text and email marketing, reputation management for soliciting reviews, payroll and employee management, business reporting, gift cards, a website builder and booking site, and a QuickBooks Online integration. It also ships native iOS and Android apps, so owners can run the shop from a phone.
DaySmart does not list specific prices on this page but says it has options to support any business level, from a single artist to a multi-artist operation, and offers a free 14-day trial with no credit card required.
Best for: studios that live and die by the appointment book and want strong forms, reminders, and marketing.
Standout feature: digital consent forms and client history built specifically around body-art workflows.
5. Tattoo Studio Pro - tattoo specific software with an integrated POS
Tattoo Studio Pro is built specifically for tattoo and piercing studios rather than adapted from a generic retail tool, and its integrated PoS reflects that. Checkout is unified - credit, debit, mobile payments, and cash in one place, handling deposits, tips, and retail purchases together - and it runs on Stripe's payment infrastructure. Online booking is tied directly to payments, so deposits are collected automatically at the time of booking, with SMS reminders to reduce no-shows.
For the studio's day-to-day, it offers digital client profiles with session history, digital consent forms attached to client records, real-time inventory tracking, and automatic commission tracking broken out by artist. Financial reporting breaks revenue down by artist and service type, tracks sales tax, and integrates with accounting software. It runs on iOS, Android, Mac, and web with no separate hardware required, working on the tablets you already own.
Pricing is transparent and aimed at smaller studios: plans start at $29/month for solo artists, with PoS, booking, client management, forms, SMS, and reporting included and "no per-feature fees." There is a 30-day free trial, and new studios are offered six months free.
Best for: tattoo first studios that want deposits, forms, and commissions handled in one purpose-built tool.
Standout feature: deposits collected automatically at booking, tied straight into the POS and per-artist commission tracking.
How to choose the right POS for your studio
The best system is the one that matches how your shop actually makes money. Start with the split between chair work and retail. If a meaningful share of your revenue comes from selling jewelry, aftercare, and merchandise, a retail grade platform with real inventory depth - variants, reorder points, purchase orders - will save you more than a booking-first tool ever could. If almost everything you earn happens at the chair, a calendar led, forms heavy system may serve you better.
Then work through the jobs that are specific to a studio. Can it collect and track deposits, and keep them straight across artists and locations? Does it calculate commission splits automatically, or will someone be doing that by hand every payout? Are consent and waiver forms digital and tied to the client's record? Will it reduce no-shows with reminders and clear cancellation policies? Does it run on the hardware you already own, and work on a phone or tablet for conventions, guest spots, and pop-ups?
Finally, weigh the money honestly. Some providers publish flat monthly pricing; others quote on request or earn most of their revenue from per-transaction processing fees. A low headline price with high processing rates can cost more than a higher subscription with keener rates, depending on your volume. Map each option against your real monthly turnover, take advantage of the free trials, and confirm the current numbers before you commit.
Frequently asked questions
What software do most tattoo artists use? There is no single standard. Many solo artists start on Square because it is quick and familiar, while busier studios move toward purpose-built platforms such as DaySmart Body Art or Tattoo Studio Pro, or to retail-grade systems like Vibe Retail and Lightspeed when merchandise and inventory matter. The right choice depends on how much of your income is chair work versus retail.
Does a tattoo shop need a full PoS, or just a card reader? A card reader takes payments; a PoS runs the business. If you only ever take one payment at a time and sell nothing else, a reader may be enough. Once you are managing deposits, commissions, stock, consent forms, and reporting, a full point-of-sale system usually pays for itself in time saved and mistakes avoided.
Can one system handle both booking and payments? Yes - that is the point of most modern tattoo PoS platforms. Every system in this list connects the calendar to the checkout to some degree, which is what allows deposits to be collected at the time of booking and tied to the right artist and appointment.
How do POS systems help with no-shows and deposits? They let you set cancellation and no-show policies, take a deposit automatically when the appointment is booked, and send automated reminders by text or email. Deposits are then recorded against the client and appointment, so nothing gets lost or double-counted.
How much should a tattoo shop POS system cost? It varies widely. Published plans in this category start around $19–$29 a month for the smallest tiers and rise with users, locations, and features; some providers quote on request or charge mainly through per-transaction processing. Always compare the subscription and the processing rates together against your own monthly volume.
The bottom line
There is no universal "best" here - the right tattoo shop POS depends on your mix of chair work and retail, the size of your team, and how much you value published, predictable pricing. Vibe Retail leads this list for studios that want a true retail POS with studio workflows on top; Square wins on speed and simplicity; Lightspeed on inventory depth; DaySmart on body-art-specific booking and forms; and Tattoo Studio Pro on tattoo-first design at a low entry price. Trial two or three, and let your own numbers decide.
This article is a general guide, not financial or purchasing advice. Prices, processing fees, plan features, and other figures are indicative only - they vary between providers and change over time. A PoS system is a meaningful commitment for any tattoo studio, so always confirm current pricing, transaction fees, contract terms, and the full agreement with any provider before you sign up.

items.title: Aldi boss says some of rivals' loyalty discounts 'dupe' customers
items.summary: Aldi is the only major supermarket chain that doesn't operate a loyalty scheme, which are hugely popular and used by millions of shoppers.
items.body:
Aldi boss says some of rivals' loyalty discounts 'dupe' customers
- Published
Aldi's UK boss has accused rival supermarket chains of duping customers in some cases with loyalty discounts that start with "unrealistically high prices" and then drop.
Chief executive Giles Hurley said discounts are helpful "when they're real and when they show realistic reductions", but hit out at what he said were unrealistic reductions which "dupe customers".
Aldi is the only major supermarket chain that doesn't operate a loyalty scheme, which are used by millions of shoppers.
The UK's official competition watchdog investigated supermarkets' loyalty pricing schemes in 2024 and concluded shoppers "almost always make a genuine saving".
Former Asda buyer and retail consultant Ged Futter told the BBC Hurley's comments were a "a distraction from the fact is that Aldi is under pressure in the UK".
He said Aldi was "on a meteoric rise until about two years ago" but that it is "now growing behind the main supermarket pack".
"The price gap isn't as clear as it once was," he added.
Hurley, who has made similar comments on discount schemes in the past, was speaking as Aldi reported a 5% increase in sales to Â£19bn for 2025 from 2024.
However, operating profits had fallen slightly over the same period, which the retailer said was due to higher staff pay as well as investments in infrastructure and prices.
Hurley said the business was attracting new customers despite fierce competition across the sector.
"We are the only retailer where the price of your weekly shop is actually cheaper this summer than last summer," said Hurley
He said the business was focussed on "everyday low prices, not short-lived offers that disappear the following week".
"Promotions can supplement every day low prices when they're meaningful, when they're real and when they show realistic reductions.
"However, when promotions start with unrealistically high prices â and come down to prices which aren't that competitive and dupe customers â we would view that as loyalty that isn't supportive, that isn't transparent and doesn't help customers plan and budget."
Aldi said it had spent Â£340m this year on cutting prices. The German-owned chain also announced plans to open 40 new stores next year as part of a Â£900m investment programme and expand long-term agreements with British suppliers.
Hurley said recent droughts and global events had highlighted vulnerabilities in food supply chains, arguing that boosting domestic production should be a national strategic priority, helping to reduce the UK's exposure to shocks that can push up food prices.

items.title: Aldi to invest £900m in UK and open 40 more stores next year
items.summary: Supermarket chain declares ‘increasing confidence’ in its growth plans after posting record annual revenue of £19bn Business live – latest updates Aldi says it is stepping up investment in the UK with plans to spend £900m and open more than 40 stores. The company, which operates 1,092 budget supermarkets in the UK and Ireland, revealed sales rose 5% to a record £19bn last year. It opened 40 stores but profits slipped by £2.6m to £433m as it cut prices despite cost inflation. Continue reading...
items.body:
Aldi says it is stepping up investment in the UK with plans to spend £900m and open more than 40 stores.
The company, which operates 1,092 budget supermarkets in the UK and Ireland, revealed sales rose 5% to a record £19bn last year. It opened 40 stores but profits slipped by £2.6m to £433m as it cut prices despite cost inflation.
Giles Hurley, the boss of Aldi’s UK and Irish arm, said the German-owned business had “increasing confidence around growing our business”, claiming it already was the third largest UK supermarket in terms of items sold and customer numbers.
Asda is classed as the UK’s third largest supermarket by value of sales, just ahead of Aldi. Leeds-based Asda is less than one percentage point ahead of its rival, with a market share of 10.6% in mainland UK, according to the latest data from Worldpanel.
Aldi will open 42 stores this year, with 30 opening in the next 10 weeks. It plans a similar number next year, stepping up investment by about £100m to £900m. In the longer term it is aiming for 1,500 outlets in the UK and Ireland.
“We could probably grow faster but we need to find the right sites in the right locations and have to go through a planning process which can, at times, be challenging,” Hurley said.
He said consumers were “feeling the pinch” against a backdrop of persistent inflation, and the “continuity and clarity” of Aldi’s range of cheap groceries had attracted 425,300 more customers.
He said the outlook for grocery inflation, which stood at 2.8% in August, according to the British Retail Consortium, was difficult to assess until the impact of drought and extreme heat on UK crop yields was clear.
He said the industry was “not seeing systemic food shortages” but the climate crisis was creating “a real challenge” for food producers. He urged the government to treat the UK’s food system as “a national strategic priority” because “relying on imports leaves us exposed”.
Hurley claimed Aldi was the only grocery chain reducing prices. He said the loyalty discount schemes offered by many rival chains, including Tesco and Sainsbury’s, were “definitely a roll of the dice for customers and questions remain about how much of the value [they offer] is perceived rather than real”.
He said Aldi was winning over customers because it remained the cheapest place to shop in the market and it would continue to invest to maintain that position by cutting prices.
However, Aldi does not reveal sales performance in established stores – those open for more than a year – making it difficult to gauge how much growth is just the result of expansion.
Aldi’s growth is much slower than than that of its rival Lidl, which is gaining market share with a loyalty scheme while allowing shoppers to order online and pick up in a store.
Aldi has signed a deal withDeliveroo under which the courier firm’s workers will pick, pack and deliver Aldi groceries sold through its app.
The supermarket chain said it had committed to sourcing at least half its products through long-term supplier agreements by next year, giving its producers and manufacturers greater confidence to invest and make Britain’s food system less reliant on imports.
Aldi said it spent £14bn with British suppliers in 2025 and about 80% of its sales came from them.

items.title: Costs piled on by Labour risk sending jobs and investment into reverse, warns high street chief
items.summary: Business is at a 'tipping point' as costs being piled on by Labour risk sending jobs and investment into reverse, the boss of high street chains Monsoon and Accessorize has warned.
items.body:
Costs piled on by Labour risk sending jobs and investment into reverse, warns high street chief
Business is at a ‘tipping point’ as costs being piled on by Labour risk sending jobs and investment into reverse, the boss of high street chains Monsoon and Accessorize has warned.
Nick Stowe said the company behind the two brands had already cut the number of new stores it is investing in this year to 10, from 25 last year.
Writing for the Daily Mail, Stowe said: ‘It’s because rising costs mean the investment case doesn’t add up.’
It comes after Labour hiked employer national insurance and minimum wages as well as enacting a botched business rates reform. Firms are also facing a sharp rise in energy bills.
Stowe said: ‘Retailers are not asking to be insulated from every increase in the cost of doing business. We have already navigated significant shocks and cost increases, and are paying more tax than ever.
‘But Government does need to recognise the cumulative impact its decisions have on whether businesses invest and hire and recognise when those decisions reach a tipping point and employment and investment goes into reverse. We’re at that point.’
The company behind Monsoon and Accessorize invested in fewer stores this year
The comments come after figures last week from the British Retail Consortium showing a fall in consumer confidence, which will add to pressure on the high street.
Separately, a survey from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) revealed that a persistent downturn in sales had prompted retailers to cut back order volumes at the fastest pace on record since the poll began in 1983.
Stowe urged Chancellor John Healey to use next month’s Budget to cancel business rate hikes next year. And he echoed a calls from across the sector to spare larger stores from a shake-up of the rates system that is designed to level the playing field between physical retailers and online rivals.
Many fear that a reform targeting larger premises – that is designed to target huge warehouses used by the likes of Amazon – could backfire on big ‘anchor’ stores.
Stowe said: ‘Larger stores are significant investments in town and city centres, they are the anchors around which other retailers build their businesses.
‘Making them disproportionately more expensive risks discouraging exactly the kind of investment Government says it wants and threatens the core of our high streets.’
It comes after the bosses of B&Q owner Kingfisher and department store chain John Lewis also urged Labour to avoid targeting larger stores.
Mike Ashley, the billionaire behind Frasers Group, has said the Government would be ‘simply delusional’ to heap more pressure on big retailers.
We are already seeing what happens when costs go up
By Nick Stowe, chief executive of Monsoon and Accessorize
Andy Burnham has made reviving Britain’s high streets a priority for his Government. But unless next month’s Budget tackles the rising cost of running a store, that ambition is going to be very hard to achieve.
For retailers deciding whether to open stores, invest or walk away from locations where the numbers no longer add up, cost is the make-or-break factor.
So to help revive the high street, there is one obvious place where the Government can have an immediate impact: business rates.
Monsoon chief executive Nick Stowe
At Monsoon and Accessorize, we want to keep investing in physical retail.
We are continuing to open stores because we believe in the high street and know that, when the right ingredients are there, everyone wins: our business grows, we create jobs, and we play our part in creating thriving town centres.
But every decision to open a store ultimately comes down to whether the numbers add up. And in too many parts of the country (mainly those most in need of jobs and investment) that calculation is becoming harder.
We’re now rejecting more stores than we’re moving forward with. Last year we invested in 25 new stores; this year we’ll invest in 10.
That isn’t because we don’t have the capital to invest. It’s because rising costs mean the investment case doesn’t add up.
Retailers have already shouldered £6.5 billion in additional employment costs over the past two years, alongside rising energy bills and spiralling transport costs. With business rates rising as well, the cumulative cost burden is becoming unmanageable.
At the same time, customers are becoming more cautious. Latest BRC figures show consumer confidence weakening ahead of the Budget.
Confidence in the economy fell six points in September, with people more pessimistic about their own finances and expecting to spend less as a result. As spending declines while costs increase, retailers are squeezed even harder.
Business rates are particularly difficult because they are a fixed tax on having a physical presence. Whether a store is thriving or struggling, the bill still needs to be paid.
Rates are also set centrally, so mayors and local authorities have no say in the level of tax, and no way to encourage businesses into their area to support jobs and redevelopment.
What can be done now? Most important: stop the situation from getting worse. The Chancellor should cancel next year’s inflation-linked increase and freeze the business rates multiplier, ensuring no shop sees its bill rise in April simply because of inflation.
The Government should also remove shops from the higher multiplier, the higher level of rates that ratchets up the tax.
Larger stores are significant investments in town and city centres, they are the anchors around which other retailers build their businesses.
Making them disproportionately more expensive risks discouraging exactly the kind of investment Government says it wants and threatens the core of our high streets.
We are already seeing what happens when costs become too difficult to absorb. Retail has lost 122,000 jobs in just two years, while the number of part-time retail jobs is now at its lowest level on record.
Retail remains Britain’s largest private sector employer and, for many people, provides that vital first step into working life. When stores disappear, jobs and opportunities disappear with them.
Retailers are not asking to be insulated from every increase in the cost of doing business. We have already navigated significant shocks and cost increases, and are paying more tax than ever.
But Government does need to recognise the cumulative impact its decisions have on whether businesses invest and hire and recognise when those decisions reach a tipping point and employment and investment goes into reverse. We’re at that point.
Freezing the multiplier and removing shops from the higher multiplier would provide some immediate breathing room. We then need the hard work on meaningful reform of a system that places too much of the tax burden on retailers simply because they have a physical presence.
That reform must reduce the overall burden without leaving individual stores paying more as a result.
Andy Burnham has been clear that he wants to breathe new life into Britain’s high streets. Retailers are ready to play their part, investing across the country and creating good jobs.
But ambition alone is not enough: the Government needs to prove that it is committed to providing the breathing room it talks about, in this case by not making the rates burden worse.
Next month’s Budget is the moment for the Government to show that it really wants to partner with businesses, that it understands how to help revive local communities, that it is committed to creating jobs.

items.title: Boss of Beaverbrooks urges government to give businesses ‘a bit of a break’
items.summary: Jeweller reports flat sales and fall in underlying operating profit as retailers anticipate October budget Business live – latest updates The boss of the family-owned jeweller Beaverbrooks has called on the government to give business “a bit of a break” by halting cost increases amid flat sales and falling profits. The retailer, founded in 1919, revealed a 9% fall in underlying operating profit to £7.8m last year after an increase in employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and the legal minimum wage introduced by the former chancellor Rachel Reeves . Continue reading...
items.body:
The boss of the family-owned jeweller Beaverbrooks has called on the government to give business “a bit of a break” by halting cost increases amid flat sales and falling profits.
The retailer, founded in 1919, revealed a 9% fall in underlying operating profit to £7.8m last year after an increase in employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and the legal minimum wage introduced by the former chancellor Rachel Reeves.
Anna Blackburn, the managing director of Beaverbrooks, said she was positive about the performance against the backdrop of a challenging retail market: “Everything we hear in the jewellery industry [suggests] this is a pretty strong performance,” she said.
Total sales slipped 0.1% to £217m at the group, which operates 56 Beaverbrooks and four Loupe stores as well as 22 outlets for specific brands including watchmakers Omega, Breitling, Tudor and TAG Heuer.
Blackburn said she wanted to see the government help boost consumer confidence and provide stability by tackling unemployment and inflation and not adding new taxes in next month’s budget as retailers prepare for Christmas.
She said: “[The government] can’t increase business costs much more. Give business a bit of a break and stimulate some growth and confidence. A long-term, joined-up strategy is critical.”
Blackburn said Beaverbrooks was outperforming its rivals in tough conditions as it continued to invest in its stores and staff, modernising its online operation and developing new products.
“Our business has remained strong for 107 years because we believe in the high street and the importance of exceptional products and customer service.”
The group has just opened its fourth Loupe watch boutique, in Sheffield, and is investing in revamping its outlets in Manchester’s Trafford Centre and Lakeside in Essex in the year ahead.
Blackburn’s comments come after the since-departed boss of the John Lewis department store chain, Peter Ruis, said the chancellor’s budget would come at a “critical period” for retailers and he wanted to see more help on business rates.
The boss of fellow retailer JD Sports has also said Reeves’s move to increase employer NICs at the same time as a chunky rise in the legal minimum wage had been “really a wrong movement” and pushed retailers to use more technology and hire fewer young people.
The government faces a tricky budget as the high price of oil and government borrowing put the squeeze on its finances – and on household bills.
The chancellor, John Healey, is reportedly considering shifting more green subsidies from energy bills into general taxation, examining fuel duty and targeting help at the poorest households.

items.body:
H&M overhauls its onsite search across more than 60 markets in technology partnership with Voyado
H&M has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” says Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, says: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
CX will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
Lowe's takes flight and Boots reaches new audiences: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Paul Smith, Sitoo, Tesco, Asda, InPost UK, Aldi UK, Deliveroo, Instacart, Dollar General, Co-op, Lager 157, Amazon, Best Buy Canada, Fanatics, Kingfisher, LeMieux, LolaLiza, and Revolut.
Lowe's
Lowe's has announced the launch of drone delivery, the newest fulfillment method for the US retailer that promises select home improvement items directly to DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes.
A pilot is now live at Lowe's store in Matthews, N.C., and adds to same-day fulfillment options for customers, including buy online, pick up in store; curbside pickup and same-day delivery. The launch builds on Wing and DoorDash's existing drone delivery operations in the Charlotte area.
“Our mission is to solve problems and fulfill dreams for the home. To achieve this mission, we're removing friction from home improvement and making it easier for customers to enjoy their home. Any technology we implement is designed to eliminate that friction so our customers can complete their projects quickly," says Seemantini Godbole, Chief Information and AI Officer at Lowe's.
"By piloting drone delivery, we're addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next-generation fulfillment right when they need it."
Paul Smith
Paul Smith has completed its roll-out of Sitoo’s cloud native unified commerce and PoS platform for fashion and lifestyle retailers across 31 stores in eight countries. In a LinkedIn post, Sitoo said: “A major milestone with an amazing customer!”
It added: “After months of close collaboration, it’s fantastic to see Sitoo now live across all Paul Smith stores and markets - and even more exciting to think about what comes next. A huge thank you to the brilliant teams at Paul Smith and Sitoo who made this milestone possible. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together and excited to continue working closely as our partnership grows. Here’s to the next chapter!”
Tesco
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
Lager 157
Lager 157 has completed a pilot of ClarityRFID's Clarity Store solution, conducted in collaboration between the two teams across three stores: Naestved in Denmark, Nacka in Sweden and Raisio in Finland. This gave Lager 157 real-time, item level visibility into stock, and the results are now shaping plans for a wider roll-out across the retailer's store network.
During the pilot, Lager 157 says it saw stock accuracy reach as high as 98-99.8% and SKU accuracy climb as high as 97% in participating stores, improving the retailer's head office store level data. A full roll-out is planned for 2027.
“The pilot gave us a completely different level of visibility into our stock, down to the individual item,” says Gunnar Palm, Head of Controlling & Business Development at Lager 157. “That's exactly the insight we want as we plan our next stores.”
Aldi UK
From October, Aldi UK will be trialling a new partnership with Deliveroo across eight UK stores, giving customers access to its full grocery range through the on demand delivery firm’s app. Modelled on Aldi’s partnerships with DoorDash, Deliveroo’s parent company, in the United States and Australia, the latter’s riders will pick, pack and deliver orders directly from stores.
The trial is pitched as the only rapid delivery service available from a discount supermarket in the UK.
Customers will be able to order around 2,000 Aldi products, including fresh fruit and vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, household essentials and Specialbuys. They can order on-demand or choose a delivery window that suits them. A nationwide launch is currently planned for early 2027.
Revolut
Revolut is testing out what is pitched as the UK’s first in-store facial recognition checkout system, Pay with Smile. This taps Revolut Register, a new hospitality PoS hardware system, and is being piloted at select Kiss the Hippo cafés.
The future of in-store payments? Or a solution that is at best looking for a problem that doesn’t exist, or at worst yet another example of a big tech company launching an assault on privacy rights in a ruthless pursuit of profits? Answers on a postcard, please, to the usual address…
Once customers are enrolled, Pay with Smile uses facial technology to verify the identity of the user against the selfie ID checks that they completed when first signing up to Revolut to authenticate and process a payment.
Smythson
ESW has announced a partnership with British luxury lifestyle brand, Smythson, to support its international e-commerce growth plans.
Founded in 1887 and known for its leather diaries, notebooks, travel bags and accessories, Smythson has built a customer base across the UK, United States and international markets. ESW will support its US and rest of world e-commerce operations, providing the cross-border commerce infrastructure needed to deliver a seamless customer experience across international markets and support future growth ambitions.
Seb Villien, Digital & Logistics Director at Smythson, says: “As we continue to expand Smythson’s global presence, working with a partner like ESW allows us to reach customers beyond our core markets, while always maintaining our focus on the quality and experience our brand is known for.”
Dollar General
Instacart and Dollar General have announced a new partnership to offer same-day delivery of the latter’s everyday essentials through the former’s app and website. The partnership will launch with a pilot at approximately 7,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores in six states in the coming weeks with plans to expand to approximately 20,000 stores across 48 states this autumn.
“Dollar General’s vast footprint and longstanding commitment to affordability make them an important addition to the Instacart Marketplace,” says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. “As we expand this partnership to approximately 20,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores, we’ll help provide customers in communities across the country with even greater access to affordable food and everyday essentials, with the convenience of same-day delivery.”
“Our mission is Serving Others, and we continually look for new ways to provide customers with the value and convenience they count on," says Tony Rogers, Senior Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Dollar General. "Our partnership with Instacart provides another convenient way for customers to access affordable food, household essentials and other products they need while saving them valuable time."
Boots UK
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
Amazon
Amazon customers in the UK now have a new way to pay for their purchases with the launch of instalment options from Affirm. They can select Affirm as their payment method at checkout and apply to get an instant eligibility decision from the company.
0% Pay-in-3 splits the cost of the purchase into three interest free monthly payments, while a longer-term interest bearing (22% representative APR fixed) plan is available for up to 48 months. Both options are available on baskets of at least £50 and come with no late or hidden fees.
Customers can make payments in monthly instalments, which can be paid manually or set up with automatic debits using a bank account or debit card. They can manage their payment plans at any time in the Affirm app or website and make additional payments or pay their full balance at any time with no early repayment penalties.
JD.com
JD.com reports that its first 101HOME store will open on 28th September in Jing’an District Shanghai. Building on the launch of an online flagship store in 2025, this is pitched as a premium lifestyle retail destination that brings together global design, home furnishing solution, smart technology, fashion, renovation services, dining, art and cultural experiences under one roof.
The retailer says that with its global sourcing capabilities, self-operated retail model and omnichannel infrastructure, 101HOME will offer a seamless “shopping upon seeing” experience, allowing consumers to explore new possibilities for their homes and discover the art of everyday living. Spanning approximately 12,000 square metres across four floors, 101HOME is designed to meet the evolving needs of consumers from age 0 to 101, across different life stages, household structures and lifestyles.
It brings together more than 1,000 full category home and lifestyle brands, including over 30 international brands making their China debut and more than 150 domestic and international brands making their JD.com debut. At the heart of 101HOME are 33 “Dream Homes”, designed for different living situation, family structures, lifestyles and interests.
The Shanghai store features spaces created by British designer Kelly Hoppen, and Japanese designers Shuhei Aoyama and Takashi Honma. Chinese designer Wang Heng (Ryan) draws on Song dynasty inspired aesthetics to create a three-generation family home. Consumers can step into fully designed home settings and see how furniture, lighting and furnishings come together, offering inspiration for their own homes.
Best Buy Canada
Best Buy Canada has selected RELEX Solutions to optimise forecasting and replenishment across its retail network. It says it will deploy the company’s tech to improve inventory visibility, automate planning processes, and support omnichannel operations across stores and distribution centres.
Headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Best Buy Canada operates more than 300 stores supported by two DCs and manages approximately 2.1 million SKUs.
It was looking for a solution to improve alignment between inventory and customer demand that would support driving greater efficiency across its network. RELEX’s ability to incorporate supply chain constraints into replenishment planning, optimise inventory across channels, support large scale retail operations, and automate key planning processes aligned closely with its goals.
“Accurate planning is essential to meeting customer expectations in a competitive consumer electronics market,” says Christian Trudel, VP Inventory & Merchandising Operations at Best Buy Canada. “RELEX gives us the tools to improve planning efficiency that supports delivering a better experience for our customers across Canada.”
Airbnb
Home sharing platform Airbnb is expanding its grocery delivery service with Instacart across the US and Canada, allowing guests to order through its app ahead of their stays. This builds on a pilot that started in four cities earlier this year.
Guests can place orders up to three weeks before check-in, with $0 delivery fees on orders of $10 or more. The service does not require a separate Instacart account or app, and the listing address is automatically populated. The service will launch in Canada in the coming weeks.
In Phoenix, Arizona, and Orlando, Florida, hosts can also opt to receive grocery orders and stock the refrigerator and pantry before guests arrive.
Airbnb says groceries have been one of its most requested services. “We wanted groceries to feel like a natural part of a stay, not another errand,” says Juan David Borrero, Airbnb’s Global Head of Partnerships and Business Development.
Asda
Asda and InPost have announced a new partnership that will see up to 700 of the latter’s parcel lockers installed across the former’s UK store estate. This will give Asda customers a new way to send, collect and return parcels while they shop, and is pitched as one of InPost’s most significant UK retail partnerships to date.
The lockers will be installed across a mix of Asda superstores, supermarkets and Express locations.
Joseph Sutton, Director - Express, Fuel & Wholesale, says: "Our unmatched mix of services is a key part of what sets Asda apart, and we know customers increasingly value the convenience of being able to tick off multiple tasks in a single trip. We're delighted to be partnering with InPost to bring parcel lockers to up to 700 locations nationwide.
This roll-out gives customers a fast and flexible way to collect and return parcels, seamlessly fitting around their weekly shop and making everyday life a little easier."
Fanatics
Afterpay has been named the preferred buy now, pay later partner of Fanatics, expanding its relationship with the digital sports platform. Eligible shoppers can now use Afterpay’s Pay in 4 and Pay Monthly for products across Fanatics’ network of online stores.
“Being selected as Fanatics’ preferred BNPL partner is a meaningful milestone for us as we continue expanding into high intent shopping categories where flexibility matters,” says Tanuj Parikh, Head of Revenue, Cash App and Afterpay. “Fanatics sits at the centre of sports culture, bringing fans closer to the teams and athletes they love. Together, we’re offering fans more flexible options at checkout while supporting one of the most dynamic commerce ecosystems in sports.”
The moment builds on an existing Afterpay and Fanatics relationship, which included an activation at this summer’s Fanatics Fest event.
“Afterpay gives our customers the flexibility today’s shoppers expect, so fans can support their teams and celebrate the biggest moments in sports,” says Tucker Kain, Fanatics Chief Strategy and Growth Officer.
“This feature allows us to further our mission to relentlessly enhance the fan experience, whether that’s through the personalised discovery Fanatics Ads brings to shopping, the live energy of Fanatics Fest, or the flexibility Afterpay offers at checkout, and make our world class assortment of products available and accessible in more ways than ever before.”
Kingfisher Group
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
Co-op
Digital commerce data specialist eStoreBrands has announced a new partnership with Co-op to launch Co-op Catalyst, an analytics platform for the quick commerce category. The platform gives suppliers direct access to Co-op's own q-commerce data across coop.co.uk and its delivery aggregator partners.
Suppliers can track product performance, search positioning and store level availability, and use the same data as their Co-op category team. Backed by Co-op's footprint of 2,300 convenience stores and its aggregator partnerships, Catalyst is pitched as providing an up-to-date view of the UK's quick commerce convenience market that has not been available to suppliers before.
Francis Nicholas, VP Product Strategy at eStoreBrands, says: "Having worked for brand owners including P&G and Nomad Foods, I know first-hand how valuable retailer insight is, and this is exactly what buying, category and quick commerce teams have been missing. Quick commerce is one of the fastest growing channels in digital retail, and Co-op Catalyst gives suppliers the retailer's own view of it, which site monitoring alone cannot provide. We look forward to helping suppliers make recommendations that benefit Co-op, their business and shoppers alike."
Kate McCrae, Operations and QCommerce Director, Co-op, says: "We're really excited about this partnership. Co-op is the UK's leading convenience store and a pioneer in Quick Commerce, where we now have around 90% reach across the UK. We are really excited about this new partnership and the insights and opportunities it will bring, as sharing deeper data will be instrumental in helping us, our suppliers, and partners serve Co-op members and shoppers. Co-op Catalyst will help unlock this channel, enabling suppliers to apply core Category Management principles to up-to-date data and recommend actions that accelerate growth for both their brands and Co-op."
Catalyst opens to suppliers later in 2026.
Lagardère Travel Retail
Lagardère Travel Retail is leveraging Perfect Corp.’s Skincare Pro with a view to bringing a more personalised and engaging skincare discovery experience to travellers across its beauty retail operations at airports in Prague, Rome Fiumicino and Amsterdam Schiphol.
The deployment will expand to two additional airports by the end of 2026. Powered by AI skin analysis, Skincare Pro assesses 12 key skin concerns, including wrinkles, pores, spots, texture, dark circles, redness, oiliness, moisture, eye bags, radiance, acne and firmness.
“AI powered personalisation is transforming the way consumers discover and shop for beauty, and travel retail is an especially exciting environment for this innovation,” says Alice Chang, Founder and CEO at Perfect Corp. “With Skincare Pro, travellers can receive an intelligent, personalised skincare analysis and product recommendations within minutes, creating a more relevant and engaging beauty experience. We are delighted to partner with Lagardère Travel Retail to bring this technology to travelers across key European airports.”
Following the analysis, shoppers receive personalised recommendations designed to address their specific skin concerns. Those who complete a skin analysis can also receive a discount via QR code.
VILLOID
StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.
Amazon
An Amazon Just Walk Out technology powered store designed and built by Gallery has opened its doors at Memorial Hermann The Woodlands Medical Centre in the US.
In a LinkedIn post, Garett Buchholz, Sales at Gallery, said: "It was great working alongside all of the parties involved to bring this store to life. Projects like this take a strong partnership, collaboration, and a lot of coordination, and it’s always rewarding to see the finished product open and serving customers."
He added: "What’s especially exciting is seeing more Just Walk Out technology stores come online within the healthcare industry. The continued adoption speaks volumes about the potential use cases for frictionless retail in healthcare environments and the value it can bring to patients, staff, and visitors. Proud of the Gallery team and everyone who helped make this one happen!"
LolaLiza
LolaLiza has opened a new store featuring a custom AI fashion avatar created by Screenix. Displayed on a Samsung spatial screen and brought into the store in conjunction with DOBIT, the avatar aims to showcase LolaLiza’s collections in a fresh and dynamic way.
A spokesperson for Screenix says: “It turns traditional digital signage into dynamic inspirational content that feels completely at home in the physical retail environment. A great example of how technology, content and strong partnerships can create more engaging in-store experiences.”
They add: “A big thank you to LolaLiza for the trust, and to Samsung Display Solutions and DOBIT for the great collaboration. Congratulations to the entire LolaLiza team on the opening. We’re proud to be part of it.”
Snappy Technologies
Snappy Technologies, part of Snappy Group, has unveiled Snappy AI, a new AI powered assistant designed to help retailers understand their business performance, identify opportunities for improvement and make more informed decisions.
This has been built specifically for Snappy Shopper retailers to help them save time and get more value from their store data. Its initial capabilities will include answering questions about sales performance, bestselling products and helping retailers identify trends and opportunities.
Retailers will be able to ask follow up questions and receive tailored, data-based suggestions and complete tasks that would have previously taken hours in a matter of seconds. Snappy AI can also complete operational tasks, including changing store opening hours and updating product prices.
LeMieux
LeMieux has launched ReRide, a new peer-to-peer resale platform launching exclusively within the retailer's Insiders app, designed to bring its community together while giving quality products a longer life.
A spokesperson says: "By keeping well made products in use for longer, we’re helping reduce waste, encourage more conscious purchasing and create a marketplace where great kit continues its journey with another rider. ReRide is also a destination for collectors and long time LeMieux fans. Whether you’re searching for a discontinued colour, replacing a well loved favourite or completing a matching set from a previous season, ReRide makes it easier to discover those harder to find pieces that are no longer available to buy new."
They add: "Most importantly, ReRide has been created for the LeMieux community. It’s a place where riders can connect directly with one another, share trusted products and help fellow equestrians enjoy the quality and performance of LeMieux for years to come."
Tesco
Vontier Corporation reports that Tesco will integrate technologies from Gilbarco Veeder-Root and Invenco with a view to creating a scalable and efficient fuelling solution across the grocery retailer’s petrol stations.
“By leveraging the combined strengths of our market leading businesses, Vontier is proud to deliver integrated solutions designed to best serve the unique needs of our customers,” says Andy Bennett, Group President of Convenience Retail at Vontier. “Today's announcement combines the retail expertise of Tesco with the best in fuelling from Gilbarco Veeder-Root and best in payment from Invenco to create a state-of-the-art solution.”
According to those involved, Gilbarco Veeder-Root’s DOMS PSS 5000 Forecourt Controller and Invenco’s connected outdoor payment terminals will enable fast and compliant transactions at the pump or at the kiosk. The controller provides specialised software that connects Tesco’s PoS and software, providing real-time data on all aspects of the forecourt.

items.body:
Finnish grocery retailer and wholesaler Kesko teams with KNAPP for new supply chain automation solution
Finnish retailing conglomerate, Kesko, is building a new logistics centre in Nurmijärvi, Finland, and has selected KNAPP as its automation partner for the first phase of the project. Kesko is a grocery retailer and wholesaler and its new central warehouse in Nurmijärvi is being built for the company’s foodservice business for the hotel, restaurant and catering (HoReCa) sector. Construction work began at the beginning of 2026.
“We are building an automation solution designed to serve our business for decades to come,” says Pekka Tala, Development Director at Kesko. “That is why it was important for us to find a solution that not only meets today’s needs, but also enables us to develop our operations in the future.”
According to Tala, the fundamentals of logistics automation have remained similar in many respects, but system performance and reliability have advanced considerably. Software also plays a growing role, as automation solutions guide operations more intelligently than before.
Kesko and KNAPP have worked together previously, and a joint planning process reinforced the view that KNAPP’s solution is well aligned with the objectives set for the logistics centre. The single facility must be able to serve different customers and order types efficiently using the same technology platform.
“KNAPP has a strong understanding of what customers need, as well as innovative solutions and insight into how those solutions will develop in the future,” Tala says. “A logistics centre is a multi-year project and a long-term investment, so it is important for us to choose a partner that can look ahead and understand our needs years from now.”
The solution being supplied by KNAPP combines automation with manual logistics processes. It uses the strengths of both operating models where they best support the needs of the business and customer service. The system is designed to adapt to future changes and growing volumes. It includes automated pallet handling, high bay storage solutions, shuttle-based storage and goods to person small item picking.
“We are pleased to implement this project together with Kesko,” says Rudolf Hansl, Vice President, Food Retail Solutions at KNAPP. “The solution is designed to support future growth and creates the foundation for the continuous development of logistics operations. At the same time, this collaboration strengthens our presence in the Finnish market and marks an important step in further expanding our activities in the Nordic grocery retail sector.”
Planning for the automation solution is beginning now, with installation scheduled to begin in 2028, and the logistics centre is expected to go live in phases during 2029–2030.
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Supply chain automation will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
UK grocery giant Morrisons names former Kingfisher executive Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer
Morrisons has appointed Dr Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joins from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
He will take overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He will report directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh when he takes up the role on 1st October.
“Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way,” says Baitiéh.
“Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact.”
Ghasempour says: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”
Royal Mail inks deal to boost UK out of home network with acquisition of Quadient parcel lockers
Royal Mail has announced the acquisition of Quadient’s UK-based parcel locker network. Around 3,000 lockers will now become part of Royal Mail’s out of home network. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the calendar year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “Together with our existing lockers, parcel shops and parcel postboxes, this acquisition will further enhance our out of home network of 30,000 parcel points and strengthen our proposition for customers. This is an exciting step forward in making it even easier for customers to send, collect and return parcels in the way that suits them best, through lockers, shops and other convenient locations.”
The deal strengthens Royal Mail’s position and makes it a major player in a crowded UK parcel lockers market that also includes InPost, Amazon, and YEEP!
Former McDonald's and Compass Group executive Jon Braithwaite connects with Co-op as new Group CDIO
Jon Braithwaite has joined Co-op as Interim Group Chief Digital and Information Officer. His CV includes stints at McDonald’s, Compass Group, and Gala Coral Group. Braithwaite is also an advisory board member at micro-donations specialist Pennies.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “Co-op is a business that combines commercial scale with genuine social purpose, and few organisations are as trusted. Technology sits right at the heart of how we serve member-owners, customers and colleagues. I'm looking forward to working with the brilliant team here and building on the momentum already underway. Exciting times ahead.”
The clock is ticking: there is now just one week left to get your entries in for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
The eighth edition of the RTIH Innovation Awards is now up and running with the deadline for entries being Friday, 2nd October. That’s just one week away, so don’t delay, start working on your submissions today!
The awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027, celebrate global tech innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our latest winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Click here for FAQs, categories, and information on our judging panel.
Sign up for an account and submit your entry or entries here.
Boots pilot launching on TikTok Shop in partnership with THG Commerce on 28th September
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
Tesco teams with AIUTA to test out virtual try-on technology for F&F clothing in Sandhurst Extra store
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
Adobe research shows UK consumers increasingly using AI as part of their online shopping journeys
Adobe has released a new report, based on analysis of over ten billion transactions every month, revealing headline UK spending figures from January to August and how online shopping behaviours are shifting thanks to AI.
UK online spending has grown steadily in 2026 - up 3.9% YTD. Spending growth accelerated from early summer onwards, with June the highest spending month of the year so far (£10.6 billion, up 16.9% YoY), primarily caused by Amazon Prime Day occurring in June this year rather than July.
YoY growth in traffic to retail sites from AI sources peaked in August, up 149% YoY and up more than 1,400% compared with October 2024. Conversion rates from AI traffic sources (which, in the UK, overtook those from non-AI traffic for the first time) were 20% higher than non-AI channels in August.
Tally creator Simbe lays claim to largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology
Simbe reports that it has surpassed 3,000 autonomous units under contract, which is pitched as the largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology (as identified in the company's research).
In the decade since introducing Tally, an inventory robot, Simbe has been shifting from autonomous shelf digitisation to building a broader platform for the physical store.
Today, Simbe combines autonomous robots, computer vision, RFID, handheld and fixed sensing to continuously capture what is happening inside retail locations: from inventory availability and product location to prices, promotions, and merchandising conditions.
“Retailers are increasingly deploying physical intelligence across the enterprise,” says Deborah Weinswig, Founder and CEO at Coresight Research. “Simbe’s 3,000 unit milestone reflects that shift: trusted shelf-level data is becoming foundational to store operations, digital commerce, merchandising and supply chain decisions.”
Highlights include: More than 75 retail banners globally, including BJ’s Wholesale Club, Kroger, and SPAR; The first and only company to earn UL 3300 certification for a robot designed to operate in public; More than 90% of store managers working alongside Tally say the technology makes their jobs better.
All you need is love and connected teams: presenting last week's biggest retail technology plays
Including Tapestry, Catalyst Brands, Costco Wholesale, Amazon, Tesco, Uber Eats, The Entertainer, REWE, Westfield, Søstrene Grene, Kwik Fill, M&S, and Nobody's Child.
